Resume starts `PlayResume(run:)` at `--rate 1` (D8). *New planet* picks a source and a checkpoint (the newest by default), the weather overlay (on, with a spin-up of 20,000 steps, unless the source's weather is already on: the engine refuses a spin-up then), `director.enabled` (D2), the houses mode (`exact`, `clade`, `auto`; a note says when the source has no event chunks) and a name (the next free of `planet_a`), validates with `PlanetSpec.validate` and starts `PlayRequest.planet`. While `starting` the sheet shows the stderr lines and a Cancel (SIGINT at once). Every other non-empty directory is `PlayCatalog.other`: listed nowhere, its name taken (`existingNames`), because the engine refuses a name that exists. **Layout** (`LauncherLayout`): the sheet is 640 points wide and at most 640 tall (the World window's 700-point minimum less 60), 560 ideal; the header, the starting box (with its Cancel), the **Resume** list (the first three worlds, a scroll list of that height beyond them) and a **footer** with the planet's validation errors and *Make planet and play* are pinned; the *New planet* form and the unfinished builds (a collapsed disclosure, "Unfinished builds (N)") scroll between them. *Make planet and play* is the sheet's default action, so Return triggers it while the form is valid (it is disabled otherwise; the World window's own keys, §34.7, are not active under a sheet).

#### 33.4.6 The renderer (commit 9)

`Renderer` has two modes: the Lab's (`StreamFrame`, unchanged) and the World's (`configureWorld(header:)`). In the World mode `submit` refreshes the buffer set with `refreshWorld` and `encode` runs `encodeWorld`; the camera is the owner's (`WorldModel`) and is assigned before each draw. Shaders are added to the same source string (`Shaders.swift`, new constants `WorldU`, 80 bytes at buffer 7, pinned by a test) and the sphere shading of the Lab is now one function, `shadeSphere`, called by `sphereFragment` and `agentFragmentA` (the Lab's per-pixel GPU test passes on it unchanged). Entry points are camel case like the file's (`agentVertexA`, `agentFragmentA`, `agentFragmentFlat`, `bondVertexA`, `pointVertexA`, `pointFragment`, `mapVertex`, `mapFragment`), not the spec's snake case.

- **Alive-only.** `FRMA`'s arrays are uploaded as they are (`pos` as `packed_float3`, `orient` as `half2`, `rgb`, `bonds` as `uint2`): the instance id is the listed row, there is no alive test, and no interpolation (§33.4's measured displacement per step: median 0.021 units, p99 0.075).
- **The torus.** `agentVertexA`, `bondVertexA` and `pointVertexA` place a row at `target.xy + (d - L·rint(d/L))`, `d = pos.xy - target.xy` (`minimumImage`); a bond puts its first end at the image nearest the target and its second at the image nearest the first, so a bond across the seam is one short segment drawn as two half segments in their agents' colours. `Torus` (`wrap`, `wrapDelta`, `nearestImage`) is the same rule on the CPU (ties to even, as `rint`). The map is **one quad of 5 × 5 worlds** centred on the cell of the target, sampled with `address::repeat`, so the torus is tiled wherever the camera looks; the clip scene of the camera is fitted to it (`Camera.tiledScene`: radius `2.5·L·√2`, with margin, so the clip planes hold the quad's corners from the nearest to the farthest zoom) (**superseded by §36.5**: the map is one patch of one world, with its copies across the wrap in y; `tiledScene` and the 5 × 5 quad are gone). The camera target is kept in `[0, L)²` (`Camera.wrapTarget`) and its height in `[0, height]`; the zoom is clamped to `[4, L / (tan(fov/2)·max(1, aspect))]`, i.e. the visible half extent stays within one world (**superseded by §36.5**: the picture stays within 0.49 L of its centre along both axes, at every heading).
- **Two passes for the organisms.** The same listed rows are drawn twice (`flags.x`): pass 0 the rows whose body projects to at least 3 drawable pixels as ray-traced spheres (`agentFragmentA`), pass 1 the others as flat discs of at least 1.2 pixels (`agentFragmentFlat`: no ray test, a little shading towards the rim, the depth of the billboard). A ray test on a billboard under a pixel would draw nothing. At the planet level neither pass runs (§33.4.7): the optional layer is `pointVertexA`, one translucent 1.5-pixel point per row.
- **The map pass** is drawn first with no depth write (so it is also the floor of a 2D world, whose agents lie in its plane) and only when there is something to show (a map, or territory): sea from `T_s`, cloud from `D_c`, rain `(b/255)²·p_ref` as a blue-grey wash (the companded byte is used as the intensity), a faint tint where the vorticity has a sign (cyclonic warm, anticyclonic cool), the equators `y = 0` and `y = L/2` as 1-pixel lines, and the territory overlay (kin slot palette, alpha from purity, 25% at the planet and region levels, borders where the owners of neighbouring cells differ). Planes are `R8Unorm` (`P`, `D_c`, `T_s`) and `R8Snorm` (`zeta`) sampled linearly; the winds are uploaded as one `RGBA8Snorm` texture (`u1 v1 u2 v2`) for the wind tracers of W5 and are not read yet. `u = x/L`, `v = y/L`; the planes are row-major `[cy][cx]`, row 0 at `v = 0`, which puts y up on the screen in the planet pose.
- **The fade.** Every plane is the mix of the previous and the current delivery by `MapFade`: a wall-clock smoothstep of 0.4 s from the delivery of a `MAP1`, started by `WorldModel.deliver`, advanced by a display link that runs only while it does (`WorldMTKView.startAnimating`). A delivery during a fade restarts it from whichever end of it the picture is nearer to (a texture pair cannot hold a mixture); at a pause nothing arrives and a finished fade stays finished. The spec said "restarts from the current blend"; the fade being complete at nearly every delivery, that reading would have shown no fade at all.
- **Textures live in `Slot`.** Each of the three buffer sets holds its own `cur` and `prev` map textures (with the serials of the deliveries they hold) and territory texture, refreshed under the draw's ticket before the encoder exists, so that no texture is written while a committed draw samples it. `MapUploadPlan.make(have:want:)` picks swap-and-write-one over write-both when the set already holds the wanted previous map; tests pin that the sets share no texture and that a fourth draw writes in place.
- **Planet pose.** `Camera.planet(size:height:aspect:)`: the map seen from above, x to the right and y up (the way a map reads), the whole world in the smaller dimension (4% margin); a 2D world keeps the Lab's face-on view (`topDown`, y down) with the tiled clip scene (`Camera.world(for:aspect:)`) (**superseded by §36.5**: the starting pose is `WorldPose.home`, and `Camera.planet` and `Camera.world(for:)` are test poses only).

#### 33.4.7 Levels and overlays (commit 9)

`WorldLevels.level(distance:fovY:aspect:size:)` from the visible half extent at the floor `h = d·tan(fov/2)·max(1, aspect)`: **organism** when `d < 0.12 L`, else **planet** when `h >= 0.5 L` (**0.45 L since §36.5**) **and a weather map is in view** (`mapShown`: `display.map` and a `MAP1` held; a 2D or dry world has no planet level, and its home pose shows its organisms), else **region**. The map's opacity is 1, 0.6 and 0.25; the territory's alpha 25%, 25% and 12% (**superseded by §36.6**: the opacity and the territory are continuous and weaker; the instances have no level switch, §36.7). Agents are instances at the region and organism levels (`WorldDisplay.agents`), nothing at the planet level unless the point layer is on (`agentPoints`, default off: 40,413 organisms cover 45% to 82% of the map's pixels at 1.1 to 2.2 px/unit); the View menu's toggle refers to the layer of the level in view (**superseded by §36.7**: instances exist at every level, capped in size and faded in by a ramp). Bonds are drawn at the region and organism levels. The level is published by `WorldModel.level` and is a function of the camera, the free rectangle's aspect and `mapShown`. **The camera's limits** (review fixes): the farthest distance is `WorldLevels.maxDistance(..., home:)`, never nearer than the home pose of the window's shape (a wide window or a bottom dock; otherwise the first drag snapped the view in), and `Camera.keepFloorInReach` tilts a view that would show past the finite tiled map (a long distance at an oblique pitch: `farthestFloorDistance` beyond `tiledReach` = 2 L) to a steeper pitch, never a shallower; an eye under 5% of the reach above the floor is left alone (the edge is a hair under its horizon). (**Superseded by §36.5**: the farthest distance is the footprint's, `WorldPose.maxDistance`; the tilt is eased back until the picture is within one world, `WorldPose.limitTilt`; the planet level begins at a visible half extent of 0.45 L, since the view never shows more than 0.49 L.)

The **overlay** is a SwiftUI `Canvas` over the Metal view (`WorldOverlayView`, `allowsHitTesting(false)`) that watches `OverlayState.revision`, which changes on a tick (`STRM`, `ENVS`), on a camera edit and on every frame while an organism is selected: storm rings (radius `r` in points, at least 5; named storms bright, disturbances dim, coasting dashed, hemispheres in two tints), names (not at the organism level), tracks (unwrapped in `STRM`, so one polyline across the seam: the whole track is shifted by the multiple of `L` that brings the storm to its minimum image), warm pools from `ENVS` as dashed rings, and the selection ring. `WorldProjector` (pure, `AlifeCore`) projects with the camera on the free rectangle at the minimum image of the target; the picker of §33.4.8 uses it too.

#### 33.4.8 Interaction (commit 10)

The decisions are pure types of `AlifeCore`, each with its tests; `WorldModel+Interaction.swift` applies them to the camera, the overlay and the control channel, and `WorldMTKView` turns AppKit events into calls on the model.

**Picking** (`WorldPicker.pick(at:projector:store:display:)`, in the view's points with the origin at the top left, over the newest frame, `STRM`, `ENVS` and `TERR`, every point at the minimum image of the camera target). The pointer and the view are in points; the drawable's pixels do not come into it, so the tolerances are the same number of points at any backing scale. Order: (1) **organisms**, at the region and organism levels and only while they are drawn (`display.agents`); at the planet level organisms are not picked (40,000 of them are under every pointer). For each listed row the projected radius is `r·(h/2)/(w·tan(fov/2))` for a view `h` points high and depth `w`; a row is a candidate within `max(6 pt, projected radius)` of the pointer. Where the projected radius is under 6 pt the winner is the row **nearest the pointer on the screen, ties by depth**; where it is at least 6 pt the winner is the row **nearest the eye among those whose disc holds the pointer**; a hit on a disc beats a near miss on a small row. (2) **Storms**: inside the ring, or within 10 pt of a small one, the one the pointer is nearest to in ring radii. (3) **Warm pools**: inside their ring. (4) A **territory cell** with an owner (`display.territory`): the pointer's ray is cast onto the floor (`floorPoint`, `z = 0`; no hit above the horizon) and the cell is the wrapped point's `(x·nx/L, y·ny/L)`; the pick carries the owner's kin group id. Nothing else is `none`. `WorldPicker.describe` gives the tooltip line ("organism UID · kin · House X", the storm's name or "disturbance N", "warm pool", "KIN territory (dominance)"). A uid with no `IDNT` row (born since the last snapshot) is described as such.

**What a click means** (decision D10). A single click on an organism **selects and follows** it: the world's `follow UID` (the hand-off at death, so the inspector survives it) and the camera on it (`FollowTarget.organism`). A **shift-click** selects only (`focus UID`, no hand-off, the camera stays). A **double click**, or `F` on a selection, also flies in to the organism level. A click on a **storm** selects it and flies there at the region level, never farther out than the camera already is; a double click follows it. A click on a **warm pool** selects it and flies there. A click on a **territory cell** selects the owner kin group (its cast row and its cells are highlighted) and changes nothing else: not the camera, not the global colour mode (a test pins that no line is sent and the frame's colour index is the same). A click on nothing clears the selection and stops the follow (`focus off` if an organism was selected). `Esc` is the same. The selection is a `WorldSelection` (`none`, `organism(uid)`, `storm(id)`, `kin(id)`, `pool(index)`); an organism is a **uid**, never a row (rows are reused after a death). Each frame the overlay resolves the selected uid with a linear scan from the last row (`WorldStore.listedIndex(ofUID:hint:)`); a miss means dead.

**The hand-off.** `PlayController.onEvents` announces, before `onDelivery`, the events of each `EVNT` batch that the chronicle had not seen, with the batch's backlog flag. For a live `focus_handoff` (`a` the dead organism, `b` the successor) `WorldSelection.applyHandoff` moves the selection **only when `a` is what is selected now**, so a late hand-off never overrides a newer click; the camera's follow moves with it when it was on `a`; the pair is kept in `WorldModel.successors` for the inspector's Family row. Until the successor appears in a frame the camera **holds the point the organism died at** (`FollowState.lastPoint`). The backlog loaded at the start moves nothing and raises no toast. A click on the chronicle row of a hand-off selects the successor (the old uid is dead), a death selects the dead uid (the card says so).

**Follow and fly.** `FollowTarget` is `none`, `storm(id)` (the position of its newest `STRM` entry; it holds the last position when the storm ends), `lineage(kinID)` (the circular mean over the torus of the frame's rows whose `IDNT` kin slot is the group's, with the mean height, recomputed every 4th frame; rows born since the last `IDNT` are ignored; the table's `x, y, z` while no row is found) and `organism(uid)`. `CameraGlide` moves the camera's target (and, for a fly, its distance) to the goal with a **critically damped** approach, exact for any step of time: `e' = (e + (v + w e) t) e^{-w t}`, `v' = (v - w (v + w e) t) e^{-w t}`, `w = 1/τ`. The offset is taken at the **nearest image** of the goal (`Torus.wrapDelta`), so a goal across the seam is approached the short way and the camera never whips; the target is wrapped into `[0, L)` by the model. `τ` is 1 s for a follow (the spec's time constant; a goal that moves steadily is trailed by twice its speed times τ, two lags in series) and 0.35 s for a fly; one frame's step is capped at 0.1 s so that a stalled window does not jump. A fly ends when the offset is under 0.02 units, the speed under 0.05 units/s and the distance within 0.2%. The distance of a fly is `WorldLevels.flyDistance`: for a region the one at which the visible half extent is 0.2 L, for an organism 0.08 L (never nearer than 4 units). **A manual drag cancels the follow and the fly** (the selection stays); a zoom cancels only the distance a fly was heading for; `R` and `Esc` cancel both. The display link runs while the glide has not arrived and on every frame delivery while something is followed; a paused world with the camera at rest costs nothing.

**Hover.** The pointer over the map is picked as for a click, at most 60 times a second (a pick projects every listed row, about 42,000), and `OverlayState.hover` carries the pick and its line; the overlay draws a one-line tooltip near the pointer and an outline on a hovered organism or storm. Over a cast row `OverlayState.castHover` highlights the storm's ring or the group's territory. No round trip to the world, and so no need of a live process: the picture of a world that has ended is still named. No tooltip during a press or off the view.

**The Cast** is `CastPolicy` over the records: every live storm (named first, strongest first, then the disturbances; name, hemisphere, the peak `zeta/f0` as a bar full at 1.5, age in minutes of **game time** `steps/(60·B)` at the base rate, `coasting`); the **eight largest kin groups** by size from `IDNT.kin` (ties by slot): name, "named after House X" when the house is in the table, share of the organisms the snapshot lists, the archetype mix as a stacked bar tagged *provisional* unless every archetype in it passes the label gate (§33.7), births and deaths by cause of the last window, the cells of the territory map it owns, with "dynasties approximate" in the header under a clade fork; and the **Focus** (the selected organism and whether the camera follows it). A click on a storm row selects it and flies there, a double click follows; a click on a lineage row selects the kin group and flies to its centroid, a double click follows it. Selected rows are shaded.

**The inspector** is a card pinned at the bottom of the dock whenever something is selected, whichever tab is open (`Inspector.card(for:store:successors:)`). For an organism: the name line (kin group, house, "(approximate)" under a clade fork), the clade (from the `IDNT` row; a newborn has none yet), archetype and intent display names tagged *provisional* unless the label gate of §33.7 passes for that label ("warming up" before the labels are evaluated; the Budding overlay says "(forecast)"), the energy bar over `play.energy_cap`, age in steps and game minutes, generation, bonds, the parent (a button selects it when it is alive in the frame), and a note ("labels are provisional (labels v3: no held-out verdict for this world and rule set)", or the environment, or "validated"); the slots and labels come from the `FOCS` itself, so a newborn is complete. A dead organism says so and names its successor when known; an organism that is not in the frame says "not in the world"; a `FOCS` of another organism is not used (the card has what the frame knows). Storm, kin group and pool cards list their numbers. Children are not listed (not retained).

**The Chronicle tab** is `ChronicleReducer.groups`: newest first, grouped by **minute of game time** (`stepsPerMinute` = `round(60·B)` = 864 at 14.4), with the families of `ChronicleFilter` (Storms, Lineages, Houses, Director, System; the focus's own events belong to System, an unknown family is never hidden). A click flies to the event's `(x, y)` and selects the entity `a` (`ChronicleAction.of`: a storm, a kin group; a house, the director and the system select nothing). **Toasts** (`ToastQueue`; **G3b: from alerts, §34.7; events toast only in a world with no alert engine**): an event of importance 2 that is new and not in the backlog raises one for **3 s**, at most **3** at a time (a burst keeps the newest), once per id; a click on a toast does what a click on its row does. The model schedules its own expiry (`expireToasts`).

**Keys** (`WorldKeys`, its own table; the Lab's `f` is the field slice and `[` `]` the field layers): `space` pause/run (by the clock strip's state), `.` one step, `c` the next colour mode of the header's list, `1 2 3` agents (the 1 px points at the planet level) / bonds / territory, `f` follow the selection (and fly in), `[` `]` one rung slower/faster along 0.25x, 0.5x, 1x, 2x, max (**a paused world has no rate to change: the keys do nothing there**; space resumes), `r` reset the camera, `Esc` clear (**G3b: `Esc` goes one level back and `g`, `p`, `a`, `k` and `Return` are added: §34.7**). A command or control chord is the menu's. Keys act in the whole window (a local key monitor of `WorldMTKView`, for events of its window), whoever has the focus, except while text is being edited.

**Mouse** (additions to §33.4.6): a press that moves less than 4 points is a click (`clickSlop`), with the event's click count; left drag pans only beyond that (**§36.5: it grabs the map**), Option-click is not a pick (it is the orbit modifier), the pointer is tracked with an `NSTrackingArea` (`.inVisibleRect`, replaced and not piled up in `updateTrackingAreas`).

**Overlay** (additions to §33.4.7): the selected storm and pool get a heavier ring; a selected or hovered kin group's cells are filled and outlined in its colour at every copy of the world that shows in the view (`WorldProjector.cellCorners`); the selection ring is drawn at every level; the follow badge ("Following X", bottom left) and the toasts (top centre) are SwiftUI over the map.

**Found while testing, fixed:** `WorldProjector.points(ofUnits:at:)` placed its far end with `screen`, which wraps again; near the half-world from the target the length came out a world wide (a pool ring of 900 pt instead of 300). Both ends are now placed as they are (`screenOfImage`); a test pins the length at every distance from the target.

**Deviations from the spec text.** (1) A hand-off row of the chronicle selects the successor, not `a`. (2) `[` and `]` do nothing while paused (the spec says "slower/faster along the rate rungs" and the strip has no held rate then). (3) A single click follows with the camera as well as with the world (D10 says "select and follow"); shift-click is the select-only gesture. (4) Hover is throttled to 60 picks a second. (5) The toast queue holds three, not an unbounded stack; the spec fixes the 3 s only. (6) The zoom cancels the fly's distance but not the follow (the spec says only that a drag cancels it).

an unfinished planet build at each stage the code can leave, a research run never unfinished, a build whose lock is held, `other`), `LauncherLayoutTests`, `WorldLaunchArgumentTests`, `WorldStoreTests` (latest-wins, events once and in order, the ring, lookups), `ClockStripTests`, `DockLayoutTests`, `TorusTests`, `WorldLevelsTests`, `MapFadeTests` (the fade with an injected clock, the upload plan, a randomised check that the plan leaves the set holding what is wanted), `WorldPaletteTests` (with the territory image), `WorldProjectorTests` (the seam, glyphs, tracks across the seam, a storm behind the eye), `PlanetCameraTests` (in `CameraTests.swift`: the pose, the clip planes holding the tiled map from every zoom, the 2D pose). `AlifeControlTests`: `WorldLauncherTests` (besides the logic, the sheet hosted by `NSHostingView` at its largest and smallest height with 12 worlds, 14 unfinished builds and 30 sources: the pinned controls inside it, the Resume list three rows, the form scrolling), `PlayControllerTests` (a stand-in script with real pipes: the live world and its records, chunking by 7-byte writes, commands in order and a single `quit`, nothing before the header, the ladder with short durations: SIGINT after the first wait, SIGTERM at the end, no signal for a world that quits, a build interrupted at once and its progress, a world still saving refused, quitting ends every process, exit statuses and the last stderr line, a corrupt stream and a bad record stopped, a launch failure, replacement), `PlayMailboxTests`, `WorldLauncherTests`, `AppTerminationTests` (a stub for the world and short durations), `WorldModelTests` (the camera, the wrap, the clamp, the level, the refit, on a played fixture), `WorldRenderingTests` (uniform layout, the shader struct, the entry points, the minimum image in every world vertex function); #### 33.4.10 The Storm Worlds app (I59)

The game without the terminal. The Swift package still builds **one executable**; `gui/scripts/make-app.sh` bundles it twice, as `AlifeControl.app` (the research Lab, today's app) and as `Storm Worlds.app`, which opens straight into the World window. Nothing in the engine, the config, the stream or the play records changes, and `swift run` is unchanged.

**Which app (`AlifeCore/LaunchMode.swift`).** `LaunchMode` is `lab` or `world`, read from the `Info.plist` key `AlifeLaunchMode` (the script writes `lab` and `world`). A missing key, an empty, an unknown or a non-string value is `lab`, so a bundle from before the key and an unbundled `swift run` start the Lab. `--launch-mode world|lab` on the command line wins over the bundle (for an unbundled run; the last one wins; an unknown value leaves the bundle in charge). `@main enum AlifeEntry` picks the `App`: `StormWorldsApp.main()` when the plan's first scene is the World window, else `AlifeControlApp.main()`. `LaunchPlan` (`LaunchMode.plan`) holds what each mode does with its windows, and the app code reads it rather than testing the mode:

| | Lab | Storm Worlds |
|---|---|---|
| name (menus, About; the bundle's `CFBundleName` says the same) | Alife Control | Storm Worlds |
| first scene, so the window SwiftUI opens at launch | the main `WindowGroup` | `Window("Storm Worlds", id: "world")` |
| windows at launch (`windowsAtLaunch(worldArgument:)`) | `[lab]`, plus `world` for `--world RUN` | `[world]` (`--world RUN` starts RUN in it, before the World view exists, so that no launcher sheet opens over it) |
| the Lab is | the main window: the last one closing closes the viewer and the World window | a tool window (`Window("Alife Control", id: "lab")`, not restorable): closing it closes only the viewer, and a run started in it keeps going until it is stopped there (Window > Lab shows it again) or the app quits |
| Window-menu items | none of its own | World (Command-1), Lab (Command-2), before the window list, which keeps SwiftUI's own items (one per `Window` scene, by title, without key equivalents) and Bring All to Front: the game and the Lab are therefore listed twice, accepted, and the "3D Viewer" item opens the viewer window as in the Lab app |
| Settings scene (Command-comma) | no | the repository folder |
| the app quits when the last window closes | yes | yes |

The last row is a decision: Storm Worlds quits when its last window closes, as a single-window game does and as the Lab always has. Closing the World window stops the world through the ladder of §33.4.3 (it saves a checkpoint; `TerminationGate` holds the quit while it does). With the Lab open the app stays, and Window > World reopens the game. The window at launch is the launcher, not the most recent world: starting a simulation (GPU, `play.lock`, a checkpoint that can take 686 MB to write) without being asked is not cheap or safe, and the launcher is one click from it. Window identifiers (`AppWindow`: `lab`, `world`, `viewer3d`) are what the scenes use.

**The repository folder (`AlifeCore/RepoPathStore.swift`).** Both bundles need it and it is set once. A bundle that has `AlifeLaunchMode` keeps it under `repoPath` in the preferences domain `io.github.magicbundle.alife` (a plain domain, `~/Library/Preferences/io.github.magicbundle.alife.plist`; no app group). `load()` returns the shared value; with none, the first of the app's own preferences and the Lab's domain (`io.github.magicbundle.alifecontrol`, where the Lab has always kept it) is copied into the shared domain and returned, and what it was copied from is left alone (a migration that deletes nothing). `save()` writes the shared domain and mirrors the saving app's own. In the Lab that is the domain an older Lab build reads alone, so it keeps agreeing; Storm Worlds' own domain is not the Lab's, so a folder chosen in Storm Worlds is not seen by an older Lab build (the current Lab reads the shared domain first, so the installed pair agrees). An empty value counts as none. Whether the folder exists is `RepoFolder.initialPath`'s business, unchanged (the fallback of #36). A process without the key (`swift run`, the tests) uses its own preferences alone, as before: `swift run` in a worktree does not move the installed apps' folder. `ALIFE_PREFS_SUITE=name` replaces the shared domain, the app's own preferences as the place a save is mirrored to, and the Lab's domain, with the named one: the app's own preferences are then only read (a source for the first value) and never written, so that a bundle can be tried, even one with the owner's bundle ID, without touching the owner's preferences. `PreferenceDomain` abstracts the domain (`UserDefaults` and an in-memory one in the tests, which therefore leave no property list in the Library).

In Storm Worlds, `WorldWindowRoot` shows `RepoGateView` instead of `WorldView` while `!repoReady` and the play phase is `idle`: the folder field, **Choose...**, **Re-check**, the same status words as the Lab's Repository box, and a button for the Lab (its **Set up environment**) when the folder exists without `.venv/bin/alife`. The launcher would only say "No world yet", and it is a sheet that would hide a banner. A world that is open keeps its window whatever happens to the folder. The Settings scene has the same field. The window refreshes the check when the app becomes active. The dock side, the dock sizes and the window frames are per app (their `@AppStorage` keys live in each bundle's own domain); sharing them would touch `WorldView`.

**The bundles (`make-app.sh`).** `--app lab|storm|both` (default `lab`, so today's `make-app.sh [--install]` is unchanged; `both` is recommended with `--install`), `--out DIR`. One release build; per app an icon from `make-icon.swift <dir> lab|storm` (the Lab's is byte-identical to before; the storm icon is drawn by the script: a cloud, a bolt, rain and a world with a few cells), an `Info.plist` (`CFBundleIdentifier` `io.github.magicbundle.alifecontrol`, overridable with `BUNDLE_ID`, and `io.github.magicbundle.stormworlds`, `STORM_BUNDLE_ID`; `CFBundleName` and `CFBundleDisplayName` `AlifeControl` and `Storm Worlds`; `CFBundleExecutable` `AlifeControl` and `StormWorlds`, so that the menu bar, Activity Monitor and `pgrep` tell them apart; category developer tools and simulation games; the same `VERSION` and build number) and a signature: `--sign`, else the first Developer ID Application identity, else Apple Development, else ad-hoc, with the hardened runtime for the first two; `--sign -` never reaches the keychain. `--install` refuses, before building, if either app is running (and again after the build, before the first copy, so that a launch during the build leaves both copies as they were), and if `--out` is the install directory (the install would delete the bundles it just built) (`lsappinfo` for the bundle ID, `pgrep` for the installed executable; the former `osascript "application id ... is running"` could ask "Where is ...?" for an app that is not installed yet). Notarization is not done (the commands are sketched at the end of the script).

**Tests.** `AlifeCoreTests`: `LaunchModeTests` (13: the defaults, the parsing, the argument and its precedence, the mode read from a bundle on disk, the plan of each mode, the menu items and their distinct keys), `RepoPathStoreTests` (15, in-memory domains: the migrations and their order, the suite winning, the mirror, an empty value, the process's store with and without the key and with the override, which never writes the app's own preferences). `AlifeControlTests`: `StormWorldsSharedRepoTests` (3: two `RunController`s on one shared domain agree both ways; no folder anywhere says so; the delegate quits after the last window). `tests/test_app_bundles.py`: text checks that the script, the icon script and the Swift names agree (the key and values, the Lab's bundle ID against the migration domain, the storm identity, the default of `--app`, the icon variants, the README), and, on macOS with `ALIFE_APP_SMOKE=1` (slow), `gui/scripts/check-apps.sh`: a release build of both bundles, ad-hoc, every `Info.plist` key, the executable, the icon and `codesign --verify`. Not tested in the suite: SwiftUI's own scene behaviour. It was exercised by hand on ad-hoc test bundles with their own bundle IDs and `ALIFE_PREFS_SUITE` (2026-10-23): only the World window opens (and, with a usable folder, its launcher); with none, the gate; the Window menu is Minimize, Zoom, the three windows, World, Lab, Bring All to Front; Window > Lab opens the Lab beside the game; closing the World with the Lab open keeps the app, Window > World reopens it; closing the Lab leaves the game; closing the last window quits.

**Not done.** An in-app update; a notarized standalone Storm Worlds (with the engine bundled, so that it needs no repository); sharing the dock and window preferences; opening the most recent world at launch.

### 33.5 Performance, the bench and the gate

#### 33.5.1 The step loop at 14.4 steps/s

The base rate `B = 14.4` steps/s is a **design rate** (1x), not a ceiling: the cadences of the game (a chapter of 6,000 steps is 6.9 minutes, a ticker line 17 s) were derived with it, and the fused Metal kernel (row I48) makes the 64k3d step with weather 14.25 ms, 69.6 steps/s (measured, §30.9). The budget of a step at 1x is 69.4 ms. Inputs: the engine step with weather 14.3 ms and the observers' fold 1.4 ms per step (G1/G2, measured at 64k 2D; the 3D figure is an estimate of the same order), the snapshot's eval 1.7 ms and settle 38 ms every 250 steps (§29.12, measured), heavy metrics 7.4 ms (§29.9), and from this PR a tracker tick of about 3.4 ms (`read_frame` 0.12, `detect` 2.0, `update` 0.10, `MAP1` quantise 0.25, `STRM` 0.2, `INTN` host labels 0.7; the first four measured on a mature 16k-step weather, the rest estimated) and a frame of about 3.6 ms (colour evaluation and one transfer 1.5, encode 1.6 measured at 42,000 alive, write 0.5; the first and last estimated).

| component (ms) | typical step | frame step | tick step | boundary step (tick, snapshot, metrics row) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| engine step and observer fold | 15.7 | 15.7 | 15.7 | 15.7 + 1.7 |
| `FRMA` | - | 3.6 | 3.6 | 3.6 |
| tick work | - | - | 3.4 | 3.4 |
| settle, `IDNT`, `TERR`, `EVNT` | - | - | - | 40 |
| the runner's boundary work | - | - | - | +15 to +25 |
| **total** | 15.7 | 19.3 | 22.7 | **about 80 to 90** |
| budget at 1x / 2x | 69.4 / 34.7 | | | |

*The table is the estimate made before the bench; the measurement is below.* The costs are medians over the calls of each part, from `alife bench --play` on the M5 Pro (2026-10-22, MLX 0.32.3, the fused kNN kernel, the planet configuration of §33.5.3 forked from `64k3d_s0` at 450,000, 44,955 alive, 4,499 steps per arm; `docs/RESULTS_G3A.md` §4).

| component (ms) | estimate | measured, rate 1 | measured, `max` |
|---|---|---|---|
| engine step (reference, no observers) | 14.3 | 14.93 | 14.93 |
| runner step, typical (`loop_typical`) | 15.7 | 26.98 | 16.62 |
| of which observer fold (loop minus engine) | 1.4 | 12.04 | 1.69 |
| `FRMA` | 3.6 | 6.19 | 3.69 |
| storm tick | 3.4 | 7.54 | 4.30 |
| labels | 0.7 | 1.32 | 0.83 |
| tables (`IDNT`, `INTN`, `TERR`) | in the 40 | 3.86 | 3.23 |
| write (per step) | 0.5 | 0.38 | 0.17 |
| settle (`loop_snapshot - loop_typical`) | 38 to 40 | 58.76 | 42.68 |
| the runner's boundary work (no checkpoint) | 15 to 25 | 30.26 | 24.30 |
| **typical step** (`step_ms_typical`) | 15.7 to 22.7 | **33.45** | **19.11** |
| **boundary step** (`step_ms_boundary`) | 80 to 90 | **130.05** | **95.13** |
| checkpoint (686 MB, internal disk) | 50 to 60 (CPU probe) | 933.6 | 977.5 |

(The director-off arm; the `rules` arm differs by under 3% in every row.) **What the measurement changes.** (1) The typical step at 1x fits
its slot of 69.4 ms with room (33.4 ms); at `max` it is 19.1 ms and a sustained **52.96 steps/s (3.68x), 53.08 (3.69x) with the rule tier**
is measured (estimate 50 to 56), so fast-forward of at least 2x holds with margin and the ladder stays 0.25x to 2x plus `max`. (2) The
boundary step (every 250 steps, 17.4 s) is 127.6 to 130.0 ms at 1x: **184 to 187% of a slot**, not the estimated 115 to 130%, with the
settle (58.8 ms against 38 to 40) and the runner's boundary work (30.3 against 15 to 25) above their estimates. The scheduler's bounded debt absorbs it (`late_steps` 0 in
every arm and in the 20,000-step play); only a re-anchor after 0.25 s of lag is a `late_step`. At 2x (34.7 ms) the boundary step would be 3.7
slots; 2x was not benched (the arms are 1 and `max`). (3) The observer fold, the settle and the boundary work cost more at 1x than at `max` (12.0 against 1.7 ms, 58.8
against 42.7, 30.3 against 24.3): the likely cause is the GPU's clock at light load (§5.1 of the specification), not tested; the fold is derived against the reference engine from a plain run, so it also
holds any slowdown of the engine step at 1x. (4) A checkpoint is **0.93 to 0.98 s** on the internal disk, **13 skipped slots at 1x** (`save_stall_steps`, never `late_steps`), not the 0.05 to 0.06 s
of the CPU probe; on the external disk (estimated 1 to 3 s) it was not measured. (5) The stream is 21.17 MB/s at 1x (`FRMA` 98.0%, 1.44 MB a frame) and 39.70 MB/s at `max`.
The remedy named here if the boundary step proves a visible stutter at 1x, moving the host-only part of the kin matching (7.5 ms) and the colony tracker (9.4 ms) after the step without changing their results (a G3b/G2 follow-up), is more relevant than it was; the click-through
decides whether the stutter is visible.

#### 33.5.2 The client's frame budget

At 60 Hz the frame is 16.7 ms. CPU per displayed frame (uniforms, the map fade, the `Canvas` overlay only on a change) is under 1 ms, and per arriving frame (14.4 a second at 1x) the copy of 1.3 MB into a buffer set plus the decoder's copies about 1 ms (both estimates). GPU: 42,000 impostors at 1 to 10 pixels (none at the planet level), the map quad and the overlays, about 1.5 to 2 ms (estimate), 9 to 12% of the GPU at 60 fps against the step's 22% at 1x. The queue time-slices, so the risk is **latency, not throughput**: a 14 ms step burst can delay a client frame past 16.7 ms about once per step. The mitigations in order: the display at 30 Hz above 2x; draw only when something moved (a frame or tick delivery, the camera, an active fade or follow; an idle scene costs nothing). None touches the engine.

#### 33.5.3 `alife bench --play`

`alife bench --play` runs the play loop of `alife play` headless and reports it in a report of its own (`bench.run_play_bench`; the other parts of `bench` are skipped; `--json PATH` writes it). Flags: `--steps N` (measured steps per arm, default 2,000), `--play-warmup N` (default 300), `--play-rates max,1`, `--play-directors off,rules` (the default when `director.enabled` is set, else `off`), `--play-spinup N`, `--play-from SRC[:STEP]`, `--play-out DIR`, with `--preset`, `--overlay` and `--set` for the world. The world is the **planet configuration** (`--preset 64k3d --overlay storm --set director.enabled=true`, whose compiled step carries the levers the rule tier needs; `--play-directors rules` without it exits 2): a founder population by default, or, with `--play-from`, a fork of a checkpoint made as `alife play --init-from` makes it (an evolved population, which the observer and settle costs need to be representative). It is saved once as a state file (`--play-spinup N` first spins the weather up, §30.9) and every arm loads its own copy.

For each director mode and rate an **arm** plays the world for `warmup + steps` steps under `PlayPacer` (a subclass with a stopwatch on its parts) with the full record set, `stdout` replaced by a pipe drained by a reader thread, cadence `PLAY_CADENCE` (a metrics row and a snapshot every 250 steps, a checkpoint every 6,000) and `game.observe` on. Per arm the report has: `steps_per_s`, `achieved_x` (over `base_rate`), `step_ms` p50, p99 and max (the time from the exit of `before_step` to the next entry, everything the loop did for the step except waiting for its slot, boundary work included), `step_ms_typical`, `_snapshot` and `_boundary` (a boundary step is also a snapshot step and counts as a boundary), `step_counts` and `part_calls` (how many steps of each kind and how many times each part was timed, which the schedule fixes), `components_ms`, `late_steps`, `save_stall_steps`, `frames`, `bytes_per_s` by tag, `mb_per_s` and the final digest. The **components**: `engine` (the compiled step without observers, from the same state: a reference), `loop_typical` and `loop_snapshot` (the runner's step: engine, observer fold, `take_records`, the social log's append and, on a snapshot, the settle), `observer` (derived: `loop_typical - engine`, at least 0), `settle` (`loop_snapshot - loop_typical`), `frma`, `tick` (the storm layer), `labels`, `tables` (`IDNT`, `INTN`, `TERR` of a snapshot), `events`, `write` (the pipe, per step), `boundary` (the runner's work after the step: stack of the interval, heavy metrics, the weather block, `row_block`, the fsyncs and the director, **without** the checkpoint) and `save`. A part that never ran in the measured window is `null`.

**Purity is part of the report.** Per director mode the same world is also run with `runner.run` and no pacer, and `digests_equal` says that the final state digest of every arm equals it (`alife bench --play` exits 1 if not): pacing, frames, records and focus are not part of the trajectory (§33.2.4), now measured on the machine that plays. The `gate` of an arm reads the numbers of §33.5.4.

#### 33.5.4 The gate (G3a merge, "bench gates the window")

At **1x on the M5 Pro, 64k3d with the storm overlay**: achieved at least 0.98x over 5 minutes (`five_minutes` says whether the arm ran that long: `--steps 4400` is a little over 5 minutes at 14.4 steps/s), `late_steps` 0 (re-anchor drops only; saving is reported apart), `step_ms` p99 at most 66, the maximum reported (80 to 90 expected at the boundary), and the **client's draw p95 at most 25 ms** (§33.5.5); at **max**: achieved at least 2.5x. A miss is reported to the coordinator with the component table; **no physics or parameter is changed to pass.** The numbers are constants of `bench.py` (`PLAY_GATE_1X`, `PLAY_GATE_MAX`) so that the report and this section cannot drift.

**Result (Mac day, 2026-10-22, M5 Pro; `docs/RESULTS_G3A.md` §5): the gate passes, item by item.** 64k3d with the storm overlay, a fork of `64k3d_s0` at 450,000 (spin-up 20,000, 44,955 alive), 4,499 steps per arm after 300 of warm-up, the digest of every arm equal to the plain run's (`d39b433b…dad9b`):

| item | limit | director off | rules | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| achieved at 1x over 5 minutes (312.4 s) | at least 0.98x | 1.00006x | 1.00004x | pass |
| `late_steps` at 1x | 0 | 0 | 0 | pass |
| `step_ms` p99 at 1x | at most 66 | 47.6 | 50.4 | pass |
| `step_ms` maximum at 1x | reported (80 to 90 expected) | 143.8 | 141.1 | reported, above the expectation |
| the client's draw p95 (42,000 rows, 2200 x 1400, with the `rules` arm at 1x running; §33.5.5) | at most 25 | 2.41 (region, the worst of four) | | pass |
| achieved at `max` | at least 2.5x | 3.678x | 3.686x | pass |

The maximum and the boundary step (127.6 to 130.0 ms, expected 80 to 90) are findings, not misses (§33.5.1); no physics or parameter was changed.

#### 33.5.5 The client's share: `WorldRenderBench`

`ALIFE_GPU_TESTS=1 swift test --filter WorldRenderBench` (`Tests/AlifeControlTests/WorldRenderBench.swift`) draws synthetic worlds of the geometry of 64k3d (L = 320, height 80) offscreen at 60 Hz in the four views that matter (planet, planet with the 1 px points, region, organism), a new frame at the base rate (every fourth tick) and a new map every 1.7 s, and prints for each the GPU time of the world pass (`MTLCommandBuffer.gpuEndTime - gpuStartTime`) and the CPU time to refresh the buffer set and encode, as p50, p95 and maximum, and the draws **dropped** because all three buffer sets were in flight (the window would try again shortly). "Draw" is exactly that: **drawable acquisition and the compositor are not in it**, so a hand run in the real window also records the present-to-present interval (`Renderer.presentedHandler`, from `MTLDrawable.addPresentedHandler`). Hooks added to `Renderer` for it (no cost while unset): `timingHandler` (`DrawTiming`, called on the GPU's completion thread), `presentedHandler`, `OffscreenTarget`, `makeOffscreenTarget` and `drawNow(into:)` (a draw without waiting, false when no set is free); `renderOffscreen` uses the same target code. Settings by environment: `ALIFE_BENCH_ROWS` (default `64,42000`: the fixture's scale and 64k's), `ALIFE_BENCH_DRAWS` (300 a scenario), `ALIFE_BENCH_HZ` (60), `ALIFE_BENCH_WIDTH` and `ALIFE_BENCH_HEIGHT` (2200 x 1400 pixels); the results go to `world-render-bench.json` in `$ALIFE_GPU_TESTS_OUT`. The test asserts that every tick drew or was dropped and that no draw took a second; it does not assert the gate (a miss is a finding, not a failure). The gate's number is read with `alife bench --play --play-rates 1` running beside it. The arithmetic (`BenchStats`: percentiles by interpolation, the synthetic frame, the environment) has CPU tests (`BenchStatsTests`).

**What has been run.** The Python half on the CPU: `tests/test_bench.py` runs the bench on the 256-row storm world (all four arms, the digests equal, the parts positive, every tag in `bytes_per_s`) and through `cli.main` (`--play-spinup`, the refusals). The Swift half as a smoke on the M5 Pro's GPU (800 x 600 pixels, 64 and 4,096 rows, 60 draws a scenario): the harness works, no draw dropped, GPU time 0.13 to 0.22 ms at the median. **That was not the gate.** On the Mac day (2026-10-22, a debug build, offscreen, 300 draws a scenario at 2200 x 1400, nothing else on the GPU) the GPU time of a draw was 0.62 to 0.65 ms at the median at 64 rows and, at 42,000 rows, 0.65 (planet), 1.01 (planet with points), 2.72 (region) and 1.16 ms (organism), at most 2.83 ms, 0 dropped; the CPU encode p50 was 0.08 to 0.15 ms. **The gate's run**, the 42,000-row scale with 4,200 draws a scenario beside the `rules` arm at 1x (started 25 s into the arm, 282 s long): GPU p50 / p95 / max in ms 0.28 / 0.78 / 2.64 (planet), 0.54 / 1.19 / 3.78 (planet with points), 1.28 / 2.41 / 5.38 (region), 0.58 / 1.24 / 4.85 (organism), CPU encode p95 0.28 to 0.29, 0 dropped; the arm itself gave 1.00002x, `late_steps` 0 and an equal digest. The draw p95 gate is met at a tenth of its limit. Not measured: the present-to-present interval in a real window (`Renderer.presentedHandler`), a release build. The medians beside the engine are lower than those alone (0.28 against 0.65 at the planet level): the likely reason is the GPU's clock state (not tested), so the two sets are not comparable draw for draw (`docs/RESULTS_G3A.md` §3, §6).

The build order of the specification (§8 of `g3a/spec.md`), 13 commits on `games/g3a`: 0 two small engine edits (`RunDir._prune` keeps a fork's origin checkpoint, `phylo.load_tree(end=)`), 1 and 2 the records, Python and Swift, 3 the chronicle and the colour modes, 4 the storm layer, 5 the runner hook and the scheduler, 6 `alife play`, 7 houses at forks, 8 the app shell, 9 the renderer, 10 the interaction, 11 the bench and the docs. The Python tests are `tests/test_stream_records.py`, `test_play_{purity,hook,sched,control,focus,cli,planet,replay,envs,colors,identity,chronicle,storms,houses,labels_v3}.py` (the last is §33.7), `test_runio.py`, `test_analysis_activity.py`, `test_gui_sync.py` and `test_bench.py`; the Swift tests are listed in §33.4.9 and §33.1.13. The decisions D1 to D11 of the spec were taken as recommended by the coordinator (choice C19, to revisit): 14.4 steps/s is 1x; the first planet is a fork of `64k3d_s0` at 500,000 with the storm overlay, a 20,000-step spin-up and `director.enabled`; the dock is on the right at 360 pt; `runner.run(pacer=)` and `EngineSession` as refactors; checkpoints every 6,000 steps and on quit with the origin kept; the chronicle says only what the observers support; the two small engine edits; a planet opens running at 1x; no Swift job in CI (accepted risk); a single click selects and follows; organisms are not instanced at the planet level.

### 33.7 Integration with W2a and the observer rules of version 3 (the merge with `origin/main` 39301ba)

`origin/main` moved from 2d1ab0c to 39301ba while G3a was built: #33 (the fused kNN kernel by default in 2D, I52) and #34 (W2a, §32,
I50). G3a was written against `INTENT_VERSION` 2; the merge makes `INTENT_VERSION` 3 and `RULES_V3` (§32.7) the observer rules of every
world the play loop opens. This section is what the merge changed in G3a, as built (the merge commit and the integration commit are the
last two of `games/g3a`).

**The merge** (textual; behaviour of both sides kept). `runner.py`: W2a's dump arrays are built from the post-step state and evaluated in
the step's `mx.eval` (`mx.eval(state, out, *obs.arrays(), *dump.values())`), G3a's `recs = obs.take_records()` feeds `pacer.after_step`; with
`pacer=None` the loop is W2a's, line for line. `runio.py`: the storm files (`storms.jsonl`, `storms_<t>.json`, `play.json`, `play.lock`) and
W2a's dumps (`eco_<t>.npz`, `wx_<t>.npy`) both exist; `truncate_after` cuts the storm log, deletes the tracker states and the dumps after
the step, and `_prune` keeps a fork's origin checkpoint as before. `bench.py`: `--play` (own report) and `--weather-org`. `game/observer.py`:
`default_rules(cfg)` (`for_2d(RULES_V3)` in a 2D world), the tracer rig and `Observer.fresh(..., houses=, tracers=)` / `open(..., tracers=)`
beside G3a's `identity_rows`, `color_inputs`, the house seeding and the slot bytes; `OBSERVER_FORMAT` stays 4 (G3a adds no sidecar member).

**What had to change in G3a, found by running its tests on the merged tree and by reading every place that names an archetype or an
intent.**

1. **The archetype set is ten, not seven** (Drifter, Floater and Sinker are bytes 8 to 10; the enum is `Gatherer` 1 to `Generalist` 7).
   `colors.ARCH_PALETTE` has 11 entries (the module asserts `len == len(Archetype)`, so the merged tree did not import); the new colours are
   Drifter (0, 76, 140), Floater (0, 210, 220) and Sinker (139, 90, 43), none red and none equal to another archetype colour; the Swift
   `WorldPalette.archetypes` is the same table (`test_gui_sync`). The kin groups' `arch` mix in an `IDNT` table has one share per archetype,
   10 values (`len(ARCHETYPE_NAMES)`, W2a's `Society`), index `i` = archetype `i + 1`; the Swift lineage row no longer requires 7 values, and
   the worst-case table (16 houses, 16 kin groups of full-precision shares, 16 colonies) is 11,662 bytes against the 16 KiB cap (10,742 with seven shares)
   (`tests/test_play_labels_v3.py`).
2. **The header names the version-3 labels** (`streamrec.labels_block`, `PlayHeader.Labels`): `intent_version` 3, `arch` and `intent` as
   display names indexed by the byte (11 entries each, index 0 empty), and in a **weather world the storm names** (`report.label_names`,
   which selects `ARCHETYPE_STORM_DISPLAY` exactly when N1's `_label_display` does: version >= 3 and `cfg.weather.enabled`, so the Gatherer
   is a Grazer). `INTN`, `IDNT` and `FOCS` carry the bytes unchanged; `INTN.intent_version` is 3.
3. **The validity gate.** N1 withholds labels without a passing held-out verdict for the world, the rule set and the environment (§31, §32.13:
   `LABEL_VERDICTS` has no version-3 row, and none for version 2 either, so a V3 run narrates no label until W2b adds rows). The stream applies
   the same gate and the World window shows a label as valid only if all of it holds: (a) the verdict table has a row for
   `(intent_version, rules_digest, dims, world_key)`, where the digest is the observer's own (`obs.rules.digest()`: a 2D world's differs from
   `RULES_V3`'s, `for_2d`) and `world_key` is N1's (`report.world_key(cfg)`: the config hash with the director and game sections at their
   defaults); (b) that label's row passes N1's bar (`report.label_passes`: verdict `pass`, at least `n_pos_min` positives, margin at least
   `margin_min`, the smallest permutation p; the one function N1's label facts, its per-fact check and the header all call); (c) the
   environment is at its defaults. (a) and (b) are static and travel in the header as `labels.gate` = `{rules_digest, world_key, key_found,
   archetypes: [bytes], intents: [bytes]}` (`report.label_gate`; empty lists without a row; `labels_block` refuses a list without

   a label that is not valid keeps its name and its *provisional* tag (the inspector row, the cast bar), and the card's note says why ("no

## 34. Chapters, alerts, the live report and direct powers (games G3b)

**Status: built; the Mac day ran 2026-10-23 and the gate passes except the report-time item the bench cannot read (§34.8, `docs/RESULTS_G3B.md`); the click-through by hand and the first play-test by a person are open** (branch `games/g3b`, merged with `origin/main` 3a14aa6; specification `g3b/spec.md` revision 2, owner decisions taken as choice C20, to revisit). Written by the
commits of the build: the chronicle quality (§34.1), chapters and the pause (§34.2), alerts (§34.3), the live report and report v2 (§34.4), the player channel and the powers
(§34.5, with §34.5.1 the powers in the play loop), the records (§34.6), the World window's additions (§34.7), the bench and the gate (§34.8) and what is built and not run (§34.9).
G3c (recorded replay files, rewind, offline advance, canonical saves) is not built.

### 34.1 Chronicle quality: kin threads, storm persistence, the hand-off line

**Why first.** The chronicle of G3a told every kin `events` row at once, and the Mac-day play (planet p0, 20,000 steps, 80 social records at
the 250 cadence) showed what that is: 139 kin events in 23.2 minutes at 1x (112 of 201 events all told), 49% of the kin groups that formed
and ended inside the window lived two snapshots or less (median three), the same cluster re-formed under a new id 36 times (a tag centroid
within 0.15 of a group that ended one to four snapshots earlier; distinct groups listed together were never closer than 0.25), 69 of
77 toasts were kin splits and merges. Alerts, the ticker and the report would have inherited it. The rules below run in the host (no observer
change, no `SOCIAL_VERSION` bump, `social.jsonl` unchanged).

**Kin threads** (`game/kinthreads.py`, `KINTHREADS_VERSION` 2; `constants_digest()` is pinned by a test). A *thread* is a kin group through its
id changes (G2 gives a group that ends and comes back a new id, §29.14; its *tag centroid* is stable). `KinThreads.fold(record)` is called once per
social record, in order, and is a pure function of the record sequence. Constants: `P = 3` snapshots to establish, `R = 3` snapshots of absence
tolerated, `DELTA = 0.15` tag distance (strict), `TOAST_FACTOR = 4` (toast size `4 x kin_enter` of the record's `thresholds`, 348 members at the
planet's `n_ref`; 350 for a record without thresholds), `TOAST_LIFE = 8` snapshots, `NAME_GAP = 8` snapshots, `MAX_THREADS = 64`.
1. A listed id owned by a thread refreshes it. 2. A newly listed id (not in the first record of the fold) joins an *absent* thread
(no id listed now, `1 <= k - last <= R + 1`) if their tags are within `DELTA`: the assignment is global, all (id, thread) pairs sorted by
(distance, thread id, kin id) and taken greedily, each at most once; a taken pair is a *flap* and tells nothing; a left-over id starts a *candidate*.
3. A thread's size is the sum of its listed ids' sizes, its tag their size-weighted mean, its peak the largest size seen. 4. A candidate is
*established* at the first snapshot at which it is listed and `k - first + 1 >= P`: `formed` is told then (event step = that snapshot, the text
carries the first listing's step; its parent is the thread owning the `other` of the `split`/`born` row of the first listing). 5. A thread not listed for `R + 1`
consecutive snapshots *ends*: told if it was established, silent if not (a flicker). It ended *merged into X* iff the record after its last listing
carries a `merged` row for one of its last-listed ids and X is the thread owning the row's `other` (a `merged` or `dissolved` row arrives in the record
*after* the id's last listing: 56 of 56 and 12 of 12 on p0); otherwise it *dissolved*. A group that merged away and re-formed within `R` snapshots never ends.
6. The threads of the fold's first record are the initial cast: established, silent (a text about one has no lifetime clause). 7. A record whose
`origin` differs from the previous one (an observer restart renumbers the ids) closes the fold: every thread ends silently and the record is a new initial cast.
**Names.** A thread's name is the name of the first id listed in it, frozen (names are generated per kin id; without this a bridged
re-formation changed the displayed name 26 times in 36 bridges and 13 of 41 threads showed more than one name). When a thread is **created** (its
first listing, a candidate included) and another established thread of the same name is open, or ended less than `NAME_GAP` snapshots ago, or a candidate
of the same name is open and was listed at this record or the one before, the new one is shown with the lowest unused suffix ("Daudrall II", frozen too);
a later thread of the same house a long time afterwards keeps the bare name, and a candidate that flickers out or stays absent frees its suffix at once.
(`KINTHREADS_VERSION` 1 took the suffix at establishment, two snapshots after the Cast first showed the thread, so 3 of the 41 threads of the p0 window
changed their shown name over their life; version 2 shows one name from the first listing, tested over the 80 records: 41 threads, one name each. A saved
table of version 1 is refused and the refold takes its place.) The Cast takes the same name and the
thread id (`IDNT.kin[].name`, `.thread`; `Chronicler.cast_names`), so a group keeps one name and one swatch across a re-formation.

**Owner decision of 2026-10-23 (item 15, satellite budding).** Kin groups that bud off a large group count as new groups in the chronicle: a satellite that is
listed for `P` snapshots is a thread that *formed*, and one that merges back is told as *merged into*, as the rule above has it. `P` stays 3 and
`KINTHREADS_VERSION` stays 2 (no lifetime floor on a *merged into*, no larger `P`); the digest pinned by the test is unchanged. The Mac day's measure stands as
the record of what this costs: a thread named Pruashol formed four times and merged back three times between steps 474,750 and 487,250, and 4 of the 19 ended
threads lasted 1,500 steps or less; kin events were 2.04 a minute, inside the band of 1 to 3.
**State.** The table (at most 64 threads, about 10 KB) is saved with every checkpoint the loop writes as `observers/kinthreads_<t>.json`
(`RunDir.write_play_state`, the generic play-state file of which `storms_<t>.json` is the other member: pruned with its checkpoint, cut by
`truncate_after`) and read at `bind`; a missing or unusable file leaves the refold of `social.jsonl`, which is the same table (the fold is a pure
function of the records; a test stops the play at every record and resumes from the saved table and from the refold, including a candidate that establishes after
the resume, and compares with the uninterrupted play). The backlog events are always those of the refold.
**Texts** (`CHRONICLE_VERSION` 2; "since", never "because"): "{name} has held together since step {s0}: {size} members." (or "... after splitting from {other}: ..."),
"{name} merged into {other} at step {s}; it lasted {steps} steps and had up to {peak} members.", "{name} dissolved after {steps} steps, up to {peak} members."
(an initial thread: the same without the lifetime clause). Importance 2 for `formed` with `size >= TOAST_SIZE` and `ended` with `peak >= TOAST_SIZE`
and `life >= TOAST_LIFE`, 1 otherwise. `kin_untold(records, told, a, b)` is the number of raw kin rows of the records in `(a, b]` consumed by no told
event (a told event consumes at most one row, the `born`/`split` row of its thread's first listing or the `merged`/`dissolved` row of the record after its
last listing, counted in the record of the row), which N1's report states as "N further kin group changes did not last long enough to be listed" (stage 6).
**Measured on the 80 records of p0** (`tests/data/play20k_logs`, pinned): 139 raw kin rows become 45 told events (22 formed, 23 ended, 1.94 a minute,
against 6.0), 36 flaps bridged, 9 toasts (against 69; the size gate alone gives 13, persistence and bridging buy the readable list), 94 rows untold. One
planet, one seed, 23 minutes: every constant is provisional (the G3b Mac day measured one 21-minute window of the same planet: kin events 2.04 a minute, `RESULTS_G3B` §7.5). The cost is delay: `formed` is told 2 snapshots (500 steps, 35 s at
1x) after the group first listed, `ended` 4 snapshots (1,000 steps, 69 s) after its last listing.

**Storms** (`Chronicler.from_storms(step, events, detected)`, `storms.STORM_MIN_DETECTIONS = 8`). 8 of the 25 tracker events of p0 are tracks of one to three
detections and 5 are the storms that existed when the fork's tracker was made. A `born` or `split` is told when the track has 8 detections (200 steps at the
tick of 25; the detections are the ids of the log line's `storms`, so the backlog counts them), at the tick it reaches them; a `named` event is told at
once and replaces the birth sentence; `merged` and `dissolved` are told only for a track that was told as born or named (or named at the first
tick); the events of the first tick of a layer made by this run carry `"initial": true` (`StormLayer.initial_pending`, set by `alife play` for a new
world and by `StormLayer.open` for a tracker restarted at a step above 0; saved in the layer state while pending) and are not told: the storms appear in the
Cast and the report. 25 events become 12 (4 born, 6 named, 2 dissolved; 1.08 to 0.52 a minute). The flag is in the tick line the layer writes, so it is in the files of
a world made from G3b on; a world whose `storms.jsonl` was written by G3a has no flag, and a backlog rebuilt from it tells that layer's first tick (16 storm lines on the
Mac-day files against the pinned 12). That is said, not repaired: the lines cannot say which tick was the first of a layer. A birth of an id the chronicler holds (a restarted tracker reuses ids)
starts that id afresh.

**Focus.** A followed organism that dies and whose follow passes on is one line ("Organism 20619802 died (starved); follow passed to a child."), a death
with no successor keeps `focus_death`: 32 lines for 16 facts become 16.

| family (events a minute, p0) | G3a | G3b |
|---|---|---|
| kin | 5.99 | 1.94 |
| storm | 1.08 | 0.52 |
| focus | 1.38 | 0.69 (by construction) |
| system, director | 0.21 | 0.21 |
| total | 8.66 | 3.36 |

Tests: `tests/test_kinthreads.py` (each clause of the rule on synthetic sequences, the strict `DELTA`, ties, the suffix rule at `NAME_GAP - 1` and `NAME_GAP`, the state
round trip at every cut of the p0 window, the pins above), `tests/test_play_storm_persist.py` (the persistence rule, the first tick, restarted ids, the layer's flag, the
p0 pin), `tests/test_play_chronicle.py`, `tests/test_play_threads.py` (the pacer's side), `tests/test_play_focus.py`. Mutation checks by hand (`build/mut2/run_mut2.py`, 30 mutations of the thread fold, the storm counters, the layer flag and the play-state files: P and R off by one,
the bridging window, `DELTA` with `<=`, the flap counter, the importance thresholds, the suffix gap, the epoch reset, the tie-break, the weighted tag, the owner table, the exit row's age,
the saved flags, a birth at the ninth detection, a naming that keeps the birth, an end always told, initial events told, the layer flag not cleared or saved, the pruning and cutting of the
state files) were each caught; one is an equivalent mutant (bridging in a fold's first record: no absent thread exists there).

### 34.2 Chapters, the pause at their end, `autopause`, the write lock and the origin row

#### 34.2.1 The chapter and the clock fields

Chapter `n` (absolute) is the steps `(6000 (n - 1), 6000 n]`: a chapter's last step belongs to it, so at a boundary the bar reads 100% and the chapter changes at the next step. `play.ChapterClock(length)`
(host only; it reads no state and writes no file) gives `chapter(t) = max(1, ceil(t / length))` and `position(t) = (chapter, t - length (chapter - 1))`, `in_chapter` in `1..length` once `t > 0` and 0 at the start of a world; `is_end(t)` is
`t > 0 and t % length == 0`. `CLCK.chapter`, `.in_chapter` and `.chapter_len` take these values (G3a sent `t // 6000` and `t % 6000`, which labelled the first chapter of a fork "Chapter 0" and made the bar jump from 100% to 0% while the
card for the finished chapter was still up). The player's number is `n_abs - n_origin` with `n_origin = made_at_step // 6000` of `play.json`, which is the client's (§34.7): for a fork made at 450,000 the first step is absolute chapter 76
(Chapter 1) and the fork's own start step reads absolute chapter 75 at 100%, a state the client must not label "Chapter 0". **The server derives the number in one place:** `play.planet_origin_step(planet)` reads `made_at_step` of the `planet` block of `play.json` (the block `alife play` wrote, or the one of a resumed world), `PlayOptions.origin_step` carries it to the pacer (`PlayOptions.planet` is only the header's `source` and `houses`), `reportjob.origin_chapters(origin_step, length)` is `n_origin` and `reportjob.chapter_number(b, length, n_origin)` is `max(0, b // length - n_origin)`; the live `RPRT`, a withheld one and the backlog rebuilt from `reports.jsonl` at bind all take their number from it (the ticker is a field of the `RPRT` and carries no chapter number; the client's bar and card subtract the same `n_origin` from `CLCK.chapter`). `CLCK.chapter` stays absolute, and `reports.jsonl` and the offline `world_report build` and `verify` hold steps (`chapter_start`, `step`) and no chapter number, so they cannot disagree. **A world without an origin** (a preset played from step 0, an adopted run) has `origin_step` 0 and numbers from step 0 as before. **A `play.json` without a usable `made_at_step`** (a planet block without the key, or a value that is not a positive integer) is read as 0, which is also what the client reads (`PlayWorldFile` fails to decode a planet without the key, so `ChapterOrigin` returns 0): the two numberings agree whatever the file holds, and such a world counts from step 0 on both sides. G3a wrote the key for every planet (`cf2794f`), so the fallback is for a hand-edited file. 6000 is a multiple of 250, so a chapter ends on a metrics row, a social snapshot and a checkpoint (`PLAY_CADENCE`).
`PlayOptions.chapter` (default 6000) is the length; only the tests change it (to a multiple of their checkpoint cadence). The header's `play.chapter` is that length.

#### 34.2.2 The chapter end in the loop

In `before_checkpoint(state, t)` with `chapter.is_end(t)` (a stop checkpoint at another step is not a chapter end, and `bind` at a boundary is not one either, so a resume at a boundary pauses for no chapter):
(1) `_chapter_pending = True` (the pause starts at the next `before_step`, so no step is owed); (2) the `CLCK` is sent with `reason` 3 and `saving` 1, which is the chapter card ("Chapter 3 complete, saving");
(3) `PlayPacer.on_chapter_end(t)` is called if set: the report job of §34.4 starts here, off the loop thread, overlapped with the save. (The announcing `CLCK` is sent before the job starts, so that a worker's
record always follows the clock that opened the card: a deterministic stream order at no cost, since the job takes tens of milliseconds and the `CLCK` microseconds.) In `after_checkpoint`: `Scheduler.end_save(count=False)` when the
pause follows (`_chapter_pause_follows`: pending, armed, no `step N` batch running, no stop asked): the stall of the save is not lateness and, here, not even a `save_stall_steps`, because the world is about to stop and the
player is reading the card; with the pause off or a batch running the stall is counted as ever. Then the `CLCK` (saving 0, reason 3). The next `before_step`
consumes the pending flag (`_begin_chapter_pause`): with `autopause.chapter` on, no batch and no stop it pauses the scheduler, sends the one frame of the state the player reads (`_enter_pause`) and sets the pause reason to 3 until a `run`,
a `rate M > 0` or a `step` arrives; a `pause` or `rate 0` while it holds keeps the reason (the world is already paused for the chapter); with it off the world runs on and the card is a notification (reason 3 only while saving);
a `step N` batch never pauses by itself; `--until` and `quit` end a chapter pause without ceremony (the stop path of the loop is unchanged: `before_step` returns at once on a stop, a quit while the pause holds checkpoints as ever).
Nothing resumes by itself and nothing here reaches the trajectory: the same world with and without the pause has equal checkpoints, rows, event chunks and social log (`test_play_chapters`, `test_play_purity`).
Two consequences outside the loop. The client's `ClockStrip` reads a world as paused when `CLCK.rate` is 0 or the reason is 1, 2 or 5; reason 3 or 4 with a running rate is the card being announced during the save (or a chapter end whose pause is
off) and must not flicker the strip to "paused" for a second. And `bench --play`'s pacer starts with every pause off, the chapter's and the alert classes' (`PlayOptions.unattended`, which the scripted tests use too): an arm has no reader to press `run`, and one that crosses a chapter end or meets an alert must measure the loop, not wait (the stall of that save
is then counted as the hitch it is).

#### 34.2.3 `autopause`

`autopause on|off` sets the chapter pause and every alert class, `autopause chapter on|off` the chapter pause, `autopause alert CLASS on|off` one class (an unknown class is noted on stderr and changes nothing); applied between steps like any control
line, answered with a `CLCK` (so the flags are echoed), presentation-only. The state is `play.Autopause` (`chapter`, `alert: {class: bool}`); `CLCK.flags` bit 0 is `chapter`, bit 1 is any class armed; the header's `play.autopause` carries the
defaults (`{"chapter": true, "alert": {class: bool}}`, the classes and defaults of §34.3.2; `autopause alert chapter on|off` is `autopause chapter on|off`: the chapter end is an alert class with its own switch). The server keeps no preference file: the client persists the player's choice and sends it back after the header.

#### 34.2.4 The write lock

`PlayPacer._write` takes one re-entrant lock around the whole `write_all` loop of a record and the `bytes_by_tag` update, and so does `_fail`; `PlayPacer.post(tag, make, *, step)` is the entry for a worker thread (the report job, a later select
job): it takes the lock, takes the `seq` of its tag inside it and writes `make(step, seq)`, so the records of one tag reach the stream in the order of their `seq` and a worker's record is never cut by the loop's write of a 1.4 MB `FRMA`
(several short writes) nor the other way round. A reader that has gone is the pacer's failure whichever thread saw it (the loop takes its ordinary stop path at its next call); nothing is written after a failure. `streamrec.Sequencer.take`
takes its own lock (the dict it replaced whole lost an increment when two threads took different tags).

#### 34.2.5 The origin row

A new world has no metrics row at its start step, and N1 (§31) cuts a chapter from rows at both ends, so Chapter 1 of every world would fail to build. `alife play` writes `meta.json["origin_row"]` when it creates a world (a preset or a
fork) on the snapshot grid: `play.origin_row(state, cfg)` returns `{"step", "steps": 0, "origin": true, "observers": {"alive"}, "clades_alive", "top_clade_share"}` from one `snapshot_metrics(heavy=True)` and a count of the live organisms (no
social head: the observer has taken no snapshot at its start step). It is not a row of `metrics.jsonl`, which the runner (`first_row`, `carrying_capacity_est`), the Lab and every analysis script read. A world with no observers or a start
step off the grid (a fork at step 12 with snapshots every 250) has none: its first, partial chapter is an arrival chapter with no report. A resume keeps the row it was made with. Reading it is the report job's (§34.4).

Tests: `tests/test_play_chapters.py` (the clock at 0, 1, 5,999, 6,000, 6,001 and for forks at 450,000 and 450,001; the header; `Autopause`; the pause at the next `before_step` with nothing of step 31 written before it ends; the pause at the maximum rate;
off; a batch; `pause` and `rate 0` inside the pause; `rate max` out of it; `--until`; quit; a stop checkpoint off the grid; a resume at a boundary; the hook after the announcing clock; the stall counted with the pause off and not with it on;
`end_save`; the digests with and without the pause; the lock: a two-thread `Sequencer` test, a worker's record against a sink that takes 5 bytes a write, a reader closed during a report, a report posted during a slow save arriving between the two
clocks; the origin row on and off the grid), `test_play_cli` (the row through `alife play`, kept by a resume), `test_play_planet` (none at step 12), `test_play_control` (the lines), `test_play_purity` (the seeded script gains the G3b lines).

### 34.3 Alerts

An **alert** is something the world wants the player to look at; an event (`EVNT`, §33.2.3) is the log. `game/alerts.py` (`ALERT_VERSION` 1) holds the classes, their thresholds as named constants (pinned by
`constants_digest()`, provisional after the G3b Mac day, which measured one window: 0.38 alerts of importance 2 or more a minute on the alert surface, `RESULTS_G3B` §7.5; a changed one needs a version bump) and `AlertEngine`, a pure function of the host quantities each hook hands it plus its own small state (armed flags, last-fired steps, short
histories). It writes no `State`, no digest-relevant file and reads no clock (the `engine` class is handed wall-clock samples by the caller). No alert is predictive, causal or evaluative: the texts are closed templates (`alerts.TEXTS`) of
exact quantities, "since" and never "because", and `tests/test_alerts.py` runs the report lexicon (`game.lexicon`, §31) over every template and every text of the `p0` window.

#### 34.3.1 Where the engine is called

| hook (`PlayPacer`) | call | inputs |
|---|---|---|
| `after_step`, a snapshot | `on_record(rec, told, threads)` | the social record, the thread events the chronicle told (`Chronicler.told_threads`, with their sentences) and the `KinThreads` table |
| `after_step`, a storm tick | `on_tick(t, storms, events, told)` | the tick's detected tracks, every tracker event and the ones the chronicle told (`Chronicler.told_storm`: its persistence rule decides what is told) |
| `after_step`, a snapshot, with `--alerts experimental` | `on_territory(t, owner, storms, threads, size)` | the territory grid of the `TERR` just sent |
| `before_checkpoint`, a chapter end | `on_chapter(t)` | the chapter clock |
| `after_boundary` | `on_row(row, t, entries, applied, effects)` | the metrics row, the director's entries (the provenance rule reads the recent ones), the entries applied at this boundary and the timed effects the log holds (`play.director_effects`) |
| `_service`, every `WAIT_S` | `engine_check(now, t, late_steps, achieved, requested, running)` | the injected clock and the scheduler's counters |
| `_fail` | `failure(t, error)` | the exception |

Order at one step is the loop's: the social record, the storm tick, the chapter end (`before_checkpoint`), then the row (`after_boundary`, which the runner calls after the checkpoint). After each call the pacer `_emit_alerts()`: the lines
go to `alerts.jsonl` first (durable before the client sees them), then the `ALRT` records (at most 16 alerts each), and a requested pause is noted. The engine's state is not saved: a resume re-arms everything, `bind` primes the
histories silently (`prime_rows` from the last 25 rows of `metrics.jsonl`, the last chapter ends and the origin row, `prime_records` from the social log for the houses, `prime_storms` from the tracker's named storms), and the **first evaluation after
open arms the level classes without raising them**: a world opened in a collapse raises no `pop_low` at once.

#### 34.3.2 The classes

Every class has a nominal importance, a surface, the importance from which an armed class pauses (`pause_min`) and a `calibrated` flag; the header's `play.alerts.classes` lists them (`alerts.registry()`), `play.autopause.alert` the
classes whose pause the player can switch and their defaults (`alerts.default_autopause()`: `pop_fall`, `pop_low` and `engine` on, the rest off; the chapter pause has its own switch, `autopause chapter`, and `autopause alert chapter on|off` is
that switch). The **alert** surface is the stack (a toast by importance, a pause if armed); the **log** surface is a chronicle row with a fly-to point, sent as importance 0 (its nominal importance is kept in `alerts.jsonl`) and never pauses.
A row of fewer steps than the world's metrics interval (`AlertEngine.cadence`, set at `bind` from `run.metrics_every`; 200 for an engine that was not told, as `fold_logs` infers it from the longest row) is a partial interval: the row a stop writes off the grid and the first one after a resume. It adds **nothing**: no sample to the windows, no rate, no evaluation (and it does not end the silent first evaluation after an open), so that a quit and a resume say what the uninterrupted play says (third review, stage 8: a stop at 7,601 raised a `pop_fall` at the trough that the grid never samples). The origin row (`steps` 0) is a sample. "The last N rows" below is the current row and the N before it.

| class | predicate | imp | surface | pause default | dedupe / clear |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chapter` | `t % chapter == 0` (`before_checkpoint`) | 3 | alert | on (the chapter switch) | per chapter; cleared by the player's `run`, `step` or a rate out of the chapter pause; a new one clears an older one nobody cleared |
| `pop_fall` | `fall = 1 - alive / max(last 6 rows)` (`alive` = `observers.alive`, the count at the end of the row) `>= 0.08`; importance 3 if `fall >= 0.15` or the one-row fall `>= 0.10`; the starvation clause when `deaths_starved >= 1.35 x` the median of the prior 8 rows | 2 or 3 | alert | on, pauses from 3 | re-arms below 0.04 or after 6,000 steps (cleared then); a deeper fall updates (`updated`); under the provenance rule it stays importance 1 until it is a hard fall |
| `pop_low` | `alive < 0.5 x max(last 24 rows)`; **unconditional** | 3 | alert | on | cleared at `>= 0.6 x` |
| `pop_slide` | at a chapter end `alive <= 0.80 x max(the 3 previous chapter ends)` | 2 | alert | off | cleared at `>= 0.90 x` (at a chapter end) |
| `pop_surge` | `alive / min(last 6 rows) - 1 >= 0.10` | 1 | alert | off | as `pop_fall` |
| `storm_named` | a track reaches named strength and the chronicle told it (not an initial one) | 2 | alert | off | per storm |
| `storm_strong` | a named storm's `zeta_now >= 0.70` f0 | 1 | log | off | per storm, 6,000 steps |
| `storm_ended` | the chronicle told a track's end (named or a disturbance it had told) | 1 | log | off | per storm |
| `storm_toll` | `deaths_storm >= 10` and `>= 3 x` the median of the prior 8 rows | 1 | log | off | 1,500 steps |
| `lineage_formed` | a thread told `formed` with `size >= 4 x kin_enter` | 2 | log | off | per thread |
| `lineage_ended` | a thread told `ended` with `peak >= 4 x kin_enter` and a life of 8 snapshots | 2 (3 if watched) | alert if watched, else log | off | per thread |
| `lineage_collapse` | a watched thread's size `<= 0.6 x` its maximum over the last 4 snapshots, no `merged` row of its ids in that window | 2 | alert | off | 6,000 steps |
| `house_fading` | a house listed `>= 8` times with `peak >= 200` now `<= 25%` of its peak, or no longer in the top 16 | 1 | log | off | per house |
| `effect_ending` | a timed effect whose end is within 500 steps | 1 | alert | off | per effect; cleared at the end |
| `director_acted` | an entry by `rule` or `llm` applied at a boundary | 2 | alert | off | per entry |
