| `storm_over_lineage` (**experimental**, `calibrated` false) | `>= 3` cells and `>= 25%` of a watched thread's territory cells within 1.5 radii of a named storm's centre (the world is periodic) | 1 | log | off | 3,000 steps; evaluated only with `--alerts experimental` |
| `engine` | `late_steps` rises by 3 within 10 s; or the achieved rate under 0.9 x the request for 20 s while running (after 5 s); a presenter failure | 1 (3 on failure) | alert | on, pauses from 3 | 300 s of the clock per key; a failure asks for no pause (the play is stopping) |
| `summary` | the rate limit (below) | 1 | alert | never | one alert, updated, cleared when nothing was held for 1,500 steps |

**Owner decision of 2026-10-23 (item 16).** `storm_named` stays on the alert surface, as spec D3 has it: a storm's naming is a toast (importance 2, never a pause
by default). On the Mac day's window 4 of the 8 alerts of importance 2 or more were namings (0.38 a minute in all, 0.19 without them); the rate is inside the
band (at most 0.6) and the owner chose to keep them. No behaviour changed.

**The watch set.** `watch KIN_ID` adds the thread that owns the kin id (at most 3; a note otherwise), `unwatch KIN_ID` removes it, `watch off` clears the set; with none set, the three largest threads are watched. Only the lineage classes read it. A watched
thread that re-forms under a new id stays watched (the set holds thread ids); a thread that ends leaves the set; an observer restart (a new `origin`) empties it.

**The provenance rule.** If a forward entry that takes food away (a `habitat_loss`, or a `regen_pulse` of a factor under 1; the player's or the director's, not a revert: a Food x1.3 is no provenance for a fall) was applied in the 500 steps before the row, and the fall is not yet as deep as a hard one (`fall < 0.15`), a `pop_fall` is importance 1, never pauses, refers to that entry
(`ref` = `{"kind": "power", "id": step_applied}`) and says so ("A regrowth pulse of x0.80 for 10,000 steps has been active since step 466,000."); it is not upgraded while the 500 steps run out, but a demoted fall that deepens to `0.15` under the maximum (a hard fall) is **raised to importance 3** (`updated`, the entry still stated, it pauses if the class is armed): a fall is a hard one whatever came before it (third review, stage 8; on p0 the aftermath of the director's move at 466,000 is raised at 466,500, 17.5% under the maximum). `pop_low` is unconditional.

**Owner decision of 2026-10-23 (the Mac day's fourth pause).** A population fall of 15% or more under the maximum of the window is importance 3 and
pauses the world (the class is armed by default) **whatever the cause, including the aftermath of the player's own power**: the player is told what their
Blight did, once, with one pause. The stage-8 rule above is therefore the intended behaviour, not a compromise; the spec's D3 band "a fall right after a power
never pauses" (spec §11) is superseded for falls of 15% or more and stands for the shallower ones, which the provenance rule demotes to importance 1. No
behaviour changed with the decision. On the Mac day's window the pause was the 21.9% fall after the player's Blight (`docs/RESULTS_G3B.md`).

#### 34.3.3 Identity, states, the rate limit and the pauses

An alert is `(class, key)`; its `id` is `first_step * 1000 + 600 + index` (index per step, 400 at most) and is stable for its life; a change of text or importance is re-sent with the next `version` and state `updated`, the end of its condition sends
`cleared` (the client removes the row and any pause flag). One `take()` hands the pacer each id once, with its newest state (an `ALRT` may not name an id twice, and the client keeps the newest `version`); the log keeps every transition. An alert below importance
3 expires 3,000 steps after it was last sent (`expires`); importance 3 stays until cleared or acknowledged.

**Rate limit.** At most `CAP_N = 4` importance-2 alerts of the alert surface per `CAP_WINDOW = 1500` steps; later ones are logged with `suppressed_by: "cap"` and counted in the `summary` alert. Exempt: importance 3, every class whose pause is armed,
`chapter` and `engine`, so a burst never folds a pausing alert.

**Pauses.** A raised (or upgraded) alert of the alert surface asks for a pause when its class is armed and `imp >= pause_min`. The pacer pauses at the next `before_step` with `CLCK.reason` 4 (`_begin_alert_pause`: the one frame of the state the player reads, then
the pause until a `run`, a `rate M > 0` or a `step`), unless the world is already paused, a `step N` batch is running or a stop was asked. At most one pause per step: **the chapter pause wins** (when the step is a chapter end with the pause armed, `pause_ok` is false and
the alerts of that step say `pause: false`; the card carries them), a `step N` batch never auto-pauses (`pause_ok` false inside it), and after the player resumes the key that caused the pause does not pause again until its rule re-arms it. The chapter alert
itself flags the chapter pause (`pause` = the switch) but never asks for an alert pause. `PlayOptions.unattended` starts a world with no pause armed (the benchmark's arms, the scripted tests).

#### 34.3.4 The files and the lines

`alerts.jsonl` (in the run directory) holds one line per transition: the 18 keys of the `ALRT` alert plus `nominal` (the importance before the surface rule) and `suppressed_by` (`null` or `"cap"`), and, for `ack`, `{id, version: 0, step, class, state:
"acknowledged"}`. It is appended with an fsync before the `ALRT` is sent; `RunDir.truncate_after` cuts it (and `alerts.replay.jsonl`) to the lines with `step <= step`, always, whatever `keep_director` is (a replay regenerates the lines after the
checkpoint, and every class but `engine` is deterministic in the steps). A replay writes the `engine` class (wall-clock based) to `alerts.replay.jsonl`, not `alerts.jsonl`. `ack ALERT_ID` appends the acknowledgement (a note for an id the engine does not know; the alerts of the backlog are known: `AlertEngine.know`);
`alerts.backlog(lines, t)` is what a client opening the world at `t` is shown, as `ALRT` with the backlog flag, no toast and no pause: the newest state of each alert that is not cleared, not acknowledged, not held back, expires after `t` and is below importance 3 (an importance-3 alert has no expiry, and the chapter's is one: its clearing belongs to a session that is over), the newest 16 by id. `--alerts experimental` (`PlayOptions.alerts_experimental`) switches on the classes marked experimental; without it `on_territory` returns at once and nothing about them is logged.

#### 34.3.5 Measured on the Mac-day play, deviations from the spec text, tests

`alerts.fold_logs` feeds the engine the files of a finished play in the loop's order. On the committed trim of `p0` (`tests/data/play20k_logs`, 82 rows, 23.7 min at 1x, the server defaults) it gives 35 lines: `chapter` 3 (456,000, 462,000, 468,000), `pop_fall` 1
(466,250, importance 1 under the provenance rule, referring to the director's `regen_pulse` of 466,000, cleared at 467,750), `director_acted` 1, `storm_named` 6, `storm_strong` 3, `storm_toll` 3, `storm_ended` 2, `lineage_formed` 4, `lineage_ended` 5 (9 toast-size
threads), `house_fading` 4, and two `chapter` clearings (the fold never presses `run`); nothing else (`pop_low`, `pop_slide` and `pop_surge` none; `pop_slide` at 468,000 is 35,934 / 44,910 = 0.8002, a hair above 0.80). Alert surface: 11 alerts, 10 of importance
2 or more (0.42 a minute; target at most 0.6). With the defaults the world pauses at 3 steps of the window, the three chapter ends, and for nothing else. Differences from the spec's table, all from its rules read exactly: `house_fading` is 4 (the table counted the houses
that left the top 16, not those that fell to a quarter of their peak while listed: Mycleav, a house of 3,700, was at 24%); `storm_ended` counts the end of a disturbance the chronicle had told too (2, as the table says; the class text says "named storm").
Other choices: the windows are the current row and the N before it (7 rows for `pop_fall` and `pop_surge`, 25 for `pop_low`; the spec's 13.9% at 466,250 needs the 7); the text of `pop_fall` gives the maximum and its distance in steps rather than the one-row fall; an
alert of the log surface is importance 0 on the wire; the class `summary` is the spec's "N more alerts"; the `ref` of a power is the entry's `step_applied` for the director's (the player's `PLAN` id arrives with the powers); a presenter failure
is logged and flagged (`engine`, importance 3) but cannot reach a client whose stream is gone. Tests: `tests/test_alerts.py` (each class on synthetic sequences, the provenance rule, the silent first evaluation, dedupe, re-arm, `updated` and `cleared`, the cap and its
exemptions, the pause flags, the chapter alert, the watch set, the engine class on an injected clock, the experimental class, the backlog, the `p0` pins by count and by a digest of the texts, every text and title through the lexicon and the `ALRT` checks),
`tests/test_play_alerts.py` (the loop: the chapter alert before the card and its clearing, the pause with reason 4 and its end, presentation only by checkpoint digests, a switched-off class, the chapter pause winning, a batch, `unattended`, `ack`, `watch`, the log
before the client, the backlog of a resumed world, the cuts of `truncate_after`, the replay's own file, the engine class on the pacer's clock, a failure in the log); `test_play_purity` covers `autopause`, `watch`, `ack` in its seeded script.

### 34.4 The live report: report version 2 and the report job

**What it is.** At each chapter end (§34.2) a played world builds the template report of the chapter and sends it as an `RPRT` (§34.6) while the world saves. It is N1's report (§31) with the change set below, so `REPORT_VERSION` is 2, `TEMPLATE_VERSION` 2
and `LEXICON_VERSION` 3 (`CHECKER_VERSION` stays 1); a record of version 1 verifies as `versions_differ`, and the record gains two digests, `kinthreads_digest` (`kinthreads.constants_digest`) and `storm_rules_digest` (`report.storm_rules_digest`: the
chronicle's `STORM_MIN_DETECTIONS` and `NAME_ZETA`), because the sheet now depends on both rules. Nothing is held in memory that the files do not have, with one exception made equal on purpose (the sidecar `meta`, 34.4.3), so **the live record is the
offline record**: `python -m alife.analysis.world_report verify RUN --reports RUN/reports.jsonl` passes on a played world, and `build` over the same chapters writes the same file byte for byte (tested). No model writes or orders a word: the select mode stays
G3c's and `report.select` does not exist.

#### 34.4.1 The sheet of version 2

`RunView` gains `storms` (the lines of `observers/storms.jsonl`), `kin_states` (the saved kin thread tables by step), `tail_from` and the property `origin_row` (`meta.json["origin_row"]`); `load_run(path, tail_from=, sidecar_meta=)` reads the rows and records from
`tail_from` on, from the end of their files (`runio.read_jsonl_from`: equal to the filter of the whole read, a torn last line ignored), and takes the sidecar `meta` of a step in memory. The facts a sheet has, with their rules:

- **Kin events are the chronicle's.** `report.thread_fold(rd, a, b, origin)` folds the records of the chapter's observer epoch with `KinThreads` (§34.1) from the table at `a`, which is the one saved with the checkpoint of `a` (`kinthreads_<a>.json`) when it
  is usable (same epoch, same step, same constants) and otherwise the refold of the epoch's records up to `a` (a pure function of them: the two are the same table, tested). It reads **nothing after `b`**, so what a chapter tells does not depend on how far
  the world has played. A view read with `tail_from` that has neither the table nor the records raises `TailError` (a `ReportError`) and the job reads the whole log. The facts: `thread` (the events told in `(a, b]`, the largest first: `event`, `name`,
  `other`, `first_step`, `end`, `steps`, `size`, `peak`, `told`, `imp`, `initial`, `kin`, `x`, `y`; at most `quota_events` 6) and `untold` (`kin_untold`: the raw kin rows of the chapter no told event consumed). The raw `events` rows of the kin groups are
  not facts any more (no `reid`, no suspect or churn gate for them; the colony events keep both), and the largest group's fact carries the thread it belongs to and the largest thread at `a` with its share then, so that "the Teshash kin was the largest kin
  group" is told only when that changed or its share moved by two points (`largest_move`).
- **Storms** (`report.storm_fold`): the lines of the tracker log up to `b` go through the chronicle's own persistence rule (`Chronicler.from_storms`: 8 detections, a naming at once, an end only for a track that was told, the first tick of a layer not at all), keeping per track
  its hemisphere, born, named and ended steps, strongest vorticity and place. `storms` (tracked and named at the last tick, tracks first told in the chapter, told ends, told namings, the longest lived) and up to three `storm` facts (a storm named or ended in the
  chapter, the strongest first: `name`, `hemisphere`, `ratio` = peak vorticity over `NAME_ZETA`, `named_step`, `end`, `age`, place). Whole-log folds: 24,600 ticks take 0.09 s.
- **Counts that are not lists.** `turnover` (`born`, `died`, `k` = deaths over the mean of the two population counts), `starve` (the row with the most starved when it is `starve_ratio` 1.35 times the chapter's median row, the lower middle row), `stormdeaths` (rows with
  `storm_death_min` 10 deaths in storms or more, at most three).
- **Houses**: `extinct_top`, how many of the houses that died out had been among the 16 largest at the record before (counted from the second record of the chapter on when the record at `a` is not there); the headline `HH` needs it to be at least one (version 1 headlined
  "101 houses died out", the turnover of a world of 79 houses).
- **Windows** (`_window_facts`): a timed entry (**one that has a duration**, not one of two names: a Bloom has a span and a window) is compared from the last row at or before its first step (clamped to `a`) to the last row at or before its end (clamped to `b`); the
  fact carries `r0`, `r1` and `w0`, and the sentence `W` says "From {from} at step {r0} to {to} at step {r1}, with the change applied at step {w0}." A row after the entry is never the baseline (it already holds part of the effect), so a power cast between two rows
  has a consequence. `window_sentences` is on.
- **The player's entries** (`is_player`, `after_start`; rule P, §34.5): a player's record at `step_applied = s` is applied after the checkpoint at `s`, so a replay from `start_step` applies it where it does not apply a boundary entry at `start_step`: `_in_fold_order`,
  `fold_levers`, `check_env`, `spans`' ignored count and `build_sheet`'s forward entries use `after_start` (`>= start_step` for the player's records, `> start_step` for the rest). `SOURCE_WORDS["player"]` is "the player"; `I-fert-d` is the sentence of a Bloom (a fertility gain with a duration).
- **The origin row.** The first chapter of a world starts at its start step, where it has no metrics row: `build_sheet` takes `meta.json["origin_row"]` as the row at `a` when `a == start_step` and the log has none, `_check_chapter` accepts it for that cut (a count of the
  living is all it needs) and the facts that need the social head or the labels of the row at `a` (the houses delta, the label facts) are left out, with `excluded.facts_dropped = ["no social baseline at the origin"]`. A world without the row (a preset made before G3b, a start off the snapshot grid) behaves
  as in N1 version 1: its first chapter cannot be cut.
- **The quiet form.** A chapter is quiet when its population moved by less than `quiet_pop` 3% without a deep dip, nothing was in force or applied (no intervention, no standing lever), no storm was named or ended and no thread event was worth a toast (importance 2). Its headline is `HQ` ("A quiet chapter"), the lead, and a body of
  the turnover and the changes too short to list, and nothing else (`QUIET_BODY`); the card shrinks to those.

**The body.** The deaths list of version 1 ("270,753 deaths: 137,575 by starvation, 132,019 by attack", four to six generations of turnover, which reads as a catastrophe) is the turnover sentence `TO`; causes appear only where they depart: `DS` (a row at 1.35 times the median), `ST-d`
and `DC` (catastrophe deaths). The lowest count is a candidate only for a deep dip. Mandatory: `TO`, `DC`, `P-low` (deep dip), `KS` and `END`. The candidates are taken in the order of `SALIENCE_ORDER`: `D`, `P-low`, `DS`, `ST-n`, `ST-b`, then **`EV`**, in which the largest thread event, the strongest
storm's sentence, the next thread event, and so on are taken in turn (so a chapter with many events of one kind still says the other), then `ST-peak`, `ST-d`, the groups and the rest; displayed in `SECTION_ORDER` (`D`, `P-low`, `DS`, `ST`, `E`, `KS`, `G`, ...). The number cut by the six-line cap
is not counted in `KS`; `KS` counts the raw rows no thread told.

**The ticker** (template only): per snapshot of the chapter, by priority, the intervention line of an entry applied in `[s - 250, s)`, else the sentence of the largest thread event told at `s`, else the first storm named and then the first ended in `(s - 250, s]` (dated by the storm's step), else nothing:
the population filler of version 1 is gone.

**Templates and the lexicon.** 101 templates (88 in N1). New: `TO`, `DC`, `DS`, `ST-d`, `ST-n`, `ST-b`, `ST-named`, `ST-peak`, `ST-end`, `KT-formed`, `KT-formed-from`, `KT-ended-into`, `KT-ended-into-i`, `KT-ended`, `KT-ended-i` (the texts of the chronicle, §34.1, with report number formats),
`KS` ("{n} further kin group changes did not last long enough to be listed."), `HK-formed`, `HK-ended-into`, `HK-ended`, `HS`, `HQ`, `I-fert-d`, `T:KT-*`, `T:ST-named`, `T:ST-end`; the window sentence changed. Removed: `D-1`, `D-2`, the six `E-*` kin sentences, `HE-*`, `T-pop`, `T:E-*`. New slot formats `dec1`, `dec2` and `name`
(a thread's or a storm's name, masked by the checker like a label), new agreement words `organism`, `storm`, `change`, the hemisphere words in the vocabulary. **Lexicon 3**: a new list `L3` of storm words (storm, disturbance, hemisphere, vorticity, weather, wind, ...) allowed in the `ST-*` templates, `HS` and their ticker lines only (R6), and the V8 term "last" no longer matches
"did not last" (`re:(?<!not\s)last`, so `KS` is the exact sentence of the specification and "the last chapter" is still refused). The gates (R5) of the new templates are re-derived from the facts they cite (`_gate_problems`): the turnover from the births, the deaths and the two population counts, `DS` from the 1.35 rule, the storm sentences from the chapter's bounds,
the thread sentences from the event kind, the window from its rows.

**Constants** (`ReportRules`, pinned by its digest; none is a config key): `quiet_pop` 0.03, `starve_ratio` 1.35, `starve_rows_min` 4, `storm_death_min` 10, `largest_move` 0.02, `quota_storms` 3, `quota_storm_deaths` 3, `window_sentences` true; removed: `kin_churn_factor`, `max_mandatory_events`, `quiet_change`.

#### 34.4.2 `reports.jsonl`, the `RPRT` object and the strips

`RunDir.put_report(rec)` rewrites `reports.jsonl` atomically with the record of the chapter replaced, the records sorted by `(step, chapter_start)` and any line that is not a report record kept after them (what `world_report build` does); `truncate_after` cuts the records of chapters that ended after
the step, whatever `keep_director` is (a replay regenerates them). `reportjob.report_object(rec, n_origin, length, since)` makes the `RPRT` JSON (§34.6): `chapter` is the number the player sees (`reportjob.chapter_number`: `n_abs - n_origin`, with `n_origin = reportjob.origin_chapters(PlayOptions.origin_step, chapter)` and `origin_step` the `made_at_step` of `play.json`, §34.2.1), `refs` of a sentence are the keys of the entities its
facts name (`K<kin id>` for a thread or a group, `S<id>` for a storm, `H<id>` for the largest house, with name and place from the fact; the lead and the interventions name none), `ticker` is the record's, `latency_s` the job's wall time, `fallback` null, `mode` 0, `final` true. **`since`** is a pure function of the director's log and the
alert log up to `b` (`reportjob.since_of`): `influence` (`PLAYER_BUDGET` 6 less the cost of the player's entries in the last 18,000 steps), `alerts` (alerts of the alert surface raised in `[a, b)` by class, the chapter alert and the rate limit's summary aside), `ending` (the timed effects, the director's and the player's, that end within the next chapter).
The job builds it inside the checkpoint stall of `b`, so it holds what exists then, for a world being opened as for the live job: **a player's record at `b` is not in it** (rule P applies it after the checkpoint; the same goes for the report itself: `spans` treats a player's record at `b` as outside `(a, b]`, so an effect a player's Food of one chapter's length ends "still in place at step b" in the report of the chapter it was cast in, and the chapter that starts at `b` tells that it ended, third review stage 8) and the alerts of the row at `b` are raised after it (an alert at `a` is counted by this chapter, one at `b` by the next).
A chapter that cannot be cut from the files (a row missing, no origin row) is a **withheld** object: empty, with the reason, no record in `reports.jsonl`; never a guess. The first chapter of a world that started off the chapter grid (`b - length < start_step`, an arrival chapter) is not queued: `ReportJob.start` posts a withheld object with the notice `ARRIVAL_REASON` ("this world began part way through it"), where the job's error string ("the cut 450000 is not the step of a metrics row") used to reach the card. The sentences of an `RPRT` have **unique ids** (`check_report` refuses a repeat; the sentences of one intervention fact are `F10`, `F10.2`, ...), and the client lists them by id.

#### 34.4.3 The job

`reportjob.ReportJob(path, length=, n_origin=, emit=, note=)` has one worker thread at a time (not a daemon, so a record being written is not cut off; it leaves when its queue is empty, so it never keeps a process alive, and `start` makes a new one). `PlayPacer.before_checkpoint` of a chapter end sends the `CLCK` that
opens the card (reason 3, saving 1) and then calls `on_chapter_end(t)` = `_start_report`, which queues the chapter with `Observer.meta()` taken on the loop thread: the sidecar of `b` is written inside the checkpoint that has just started, so a job that read the files would take the sidecar before it, and the hand-over (`RunView.sidecars[b] = meta`)
makes the label facts what the file will say (tested with differing metas). The worker then: `load_run(tail_from=a)`, `build_sheet`, `narrate` (template mode), `put_report`, `since_of`, `report_object`, and posts the `RPRT` through `PlayPacer.post` (the write lock of §34.2.4), which lands between the two `CLCK` of the stall (tested on the stream's order);
a `TailError` (no saved table, e.g. its checkpoint was pruned) reads the whole log; any other exception is a note on stderr and a withheld object. `PlayPacer.close` (called by `serve_play`, the bench and the test helper) lets the worker finish what it has and joins it with a 5 s timeout; what it did not finish is rebuilt when the world is opened.
At `bind` (`_open_reports`): the last three records of `reports.jsonl` are sent as the backlog (flag bit 0, after the alert backlog, before the first `CLCK`), and the chapter ends among the last three that have no record (`reportjob.missing_chapters`: inside the world, on the snapshot grid) are queued for the worker and sent as backlog when built. A world whose
snapshots are not at `ReportRules.snapshot_every` (250) or whose chapter is not a whole number of them has no job and no `RPRT` in its header (`PlayOptions.chapter` is shortened by tests only). The job reads files only; it never touches the pacer's state or the device.

**Cost.** On the committed trim of `p0` (85 rows, 80 records, 820 ticks, CPU) `load_run` + `build_sheet` + `narrate` take 7 to 26 ms; on a tiny world a whole job takes 3 ms. The tail read keeps the cost of the rows and records at the chapter's size (25 rows and 24 records); the tracker log is read whole (the persistence rule needs it) and
its fold of 24,600 ticks takes 0.09 s, so a job at 600,000 steps of play is estimated at a few tenths of a second, off the loop thread. The performance gate of the specification (§10) measures it on the planet; it is not built yet.

#### 34.4.4 The three chapters of `p0`, deviations from the spec text, tests

The Mac-day play of planet `p0` (`tests/data/report_p0`, a run directory reduced to the keys the report reads by `tests/data/make_report_p0.py`; the source files are the coordinator's) gives, for the chapters of the specification's table (§5.2a), the reports pinned in `tests/test_report_v2.py`:
(450,250, 456,250] "3 storms reached named strength" / the population fell from 44,860 to 44,799 (-0.1%) / "269,868 organisms were born and 269,860 died: a turnover of 6.0 times the population." / "6 storms were tracked at the end of the chapter, 4 of them named." / "3 storms formed and 0 dissolved during the chapter." /
"Storm Phaitraern reached named strength at step 451,600." / "Pruashol merged into Teshash at step 454,000; it had up to 4,659 members." / "45 further kin group changes did not last long enough to be listed."; (456,000, 462,000] the same shape with "2 storms reached named strength", turnover 6.1, "Storm Phaitraern dissolved
at step 458,825 after 8,725 steps." and 10 changes too short to list; (462,000, 468,000] "Population fell to 35,934", turnover 6.3, "8,249 starved in the 250 steps to step 466,250, against a median of 5,451.", "Stauthaend merged into Teshash at step 464,750; it lasted 9,500 steps and had up to 4,539 members.", 28 changes too short to list, the
director's `runaway_damper` move, "It was still in place at step 468,000." and the window "From 42,873 at step 466,000 to 35,934 at step 468,000, with the change applied at step 466,000." No chapter is quiet (the first two carry storm events). The v1 text (§5.2a, measured) had four kin sentences about groups that split and merged inside 750 steps, the headline
"101 houses died out" and the deaths list. The ticker of a chapter has 7 to 9 lines (thread events, storm namings and ends, the entry).

Differences from the hand-derived target of the specification's §5.2a, all from its rules read exactly: the median of the starved row is the chapter's (5,451), not the alert's prior eight rows (5,676); the first chapter lists `ST-b` ("3 storms formed and 0 dissolved") and one naming, where the table's target listed the counts differently and two kin sentences; the window says "the change"
where the table says "the power" (a director's move is not a power); `KS` is 45, 10 and 28 (the table's second figure, 6, was a hand count: stage 2 measured 10); the sentence on the largest group is told only when it changed, which it did not in these chapters. The body takes the thread events and the storm sentences in turn (`EV`), which the table did not specify.

Other choices: `thread` facts are the events the fold tells in the chapter whatever their importance (the quiet rule reads `imp`); a storm without a name is counted but never has a sentence of its own; `window` entries need an entry with a duration, so an untimed gain has none; `ST-peak` is told for every storm fact but sits below the events in the cap; `since.alerts` counts only the alert surface;
`REPORT_V1` is still the name of the default `ReportRules` (the object whose digest the sheet carries); the `RPRT` of a chapter withheld at a replay is rebuilt like any other.

Tests: `test_report_v2.py` (the three p0 chapters pinned in full with their tickers, the storm and `untold` counts, the window rows, the chronicle's events against the report's, the versions and a version-1 record, the storm digest, the tail-read sheet equal to the full-read sheet on two chapters, `TailError`, a saved table of another epoch or step ignored and an unreadable one refolded, the sheet
as a function of the files up to `b`, the origin row (the first chapter, no row, off the grid, no count), the player's entries (`is_player` against `actions.is_player`, a power at the origin step, the env check, a Bloom, a cancel), a quiet chapter of a real run, the storm fold on a scripted tracker log (detections, the initial track, the ends, the chapter halves adding to the whole), the
deaths-in-storms and starved thresholds, houses that died out), `test_report_job.py` (a played world of three chapters: the records verify and a `build` writes the same file; the first chapter from the origin row; a world with no origin row withholds it; the stream order; the object against its record; the backlog; a missing report rebuilt at open; the
live job reads from the end; the whole-log fallback; the sidecar hand-over; a failing build; the worker's order, shutdown, timeout and idle exit; `since_of`, `missing_chapters`, `report_object` on `p0`; `read_jsonl_from` against the filter on random files; `put_report`; `truncate_after`; no job without observers), and the rewritten `test_game_report`, `test_game_report_templates`,
`test_game_report_select` and `test_analysis_world_report` (the synthetic run, the probe sheets and the golden tiny and e2e runs are regenerated by their maker scripts, `--golden-only` rebuilding the goldens from the committed run files).

### 34.5 The player channel and powers

**What it is.** A power cannot wait for a rule boundary (a multiple of `rule_every`, at a metrics row), so `alife play`
gets its own application point in `runner.run`: `Director.apply_pending(state, t, stopping=...)` at the top of loop
iteration `t`, between steps `t - 1` and `t`, after `pacer.before_step`. The pacer only enqueues (`queue_player`,
pure Python, from the loop thread); the runner applies, so the "state is borrowed" rule (§33.2.4) is untouched. It is
a no-op, one comparison and no sync, unless a request is queued, a player's effect has reached its end, or (replay) the
log has a player's record at `t`; `pacer=None` with nothing queued executes the old loop line for line (tested by the
digest matrix of the tree against its parent commit, 2D and tiny3d, and by the identity of the research folds below).

**Modes.** `run.director = player` (§26.2): a `Director` with no tracker, no archive, no rule decisions and no LLM tier;
it applies what the pacer queued and the reverts that end the player's own effects. **It also ends what the director
began** (third review, stage 8): a world launched in it can hold a timed effect of the rule tier or the model (last
played under `--director rules`, or a research run adopted by `alife play`), and the lever would stay held for ever (Food
refused, Cancel unable to end it). `due(t)` is true at a boundary (`t % rule_every == 0`) at or after the end of such an
effect, and `on_boundary` writes the revert as `live` writes it (same step, same entry, vitals of the latest row: a
boundary record before the checkpoint, so every path that cuts or replays the log treats it as a rule's) and nothing
else; with no such effect `due()` is false, as before. With no
power applied it is digest-equal to `off` (inert env, §26 D1; tested). `live` also accepts player records (`alife play
--director rules`); `replay` applies the logged ones and takes no request (`queue_player` and `plan_player` raise).
`alife play` launches in `player` when the world has `director.enabled` (the default launch; `--director off` means the
same) and in `off` otherwise; `--director rules` is `live`, `--replay` is `replay`. `cli._play_serve` rewrites
`config.json` with the mode and builds the director with `game_specs=True`.

**Records.** A *record of the player channel* (`actions.is_player`) is `source == "player"` (a power) or `source ==
"revert"` with `scope == "player"` (the end or the cancellation of a timed power). A power carries the usual entry fields
(`step_applied`, `persona`, `action`, `params`, `prev`, `duration`, `reason`, `vitals_step`) and `scope: "player"`,
`command` (the client's request id), `power` (`food`, `bloom`, `blight`, `strike`: `actions.GAME_POWERS`), `specs:
"game-v0"`, `cost`, and `vitals: {"n_alive": ...}` of the latest metrics row (there is no tracker); a revert carries
`reverts` (the origin step), and a cancellation also the `command`. `reason` comes from a closed template
(`director.PLAYER_REASON`). The header of `director.jsonl` gains `game_specs: "game-v0"` **only when `alife play` opens
the log** (`make_header(..., game_specs=True)`): an unconditional key would make `needs_header` append a header to every
resumed research log. `log.validate_log` accepts a player's record only after a header that names a `game_specs` this
code implements.

**Rule P: a record of the player channel at step `s` is applied after the checkpoint at `s`.** A boundary entry at `s`
is applied at the end of iteration `s - 1`, after the row at `s` and before the checkpoint, so the checkpoint holds it;
a player's record at `s` is applied at the top of iteration `s`, so the checkpoint does not. The chapter pause sits on a
checkpoint step, so the most common power lands exactly there. One rule in every place that cuts or replays by step:
`RunDir._director_cut` (`truncate_after(s)`) keeps a player's record only if `step_applied < s` and any other record if
`<= s`, and a line of `commands.jsonl` (`COMMANDS_FILE`, the player's inputs; written by the pacer in a later commit)
only if `t < s`; a replay's `Director.__init__` keeps a player's record with `step_applied >= start_step` (the others
`> start_step`) in `pending_player`, applied by `apply_pending`, while `_replay` pops only the others at the boundary.
So a crash-resume from the checkpoint at `s` drops a power applied at `s` from the log with its budget, cooldown and
lever hold, and the world is what it was at `s`; the replay's checkpoint at an on-grid player step equals the live one
(both tested). `commands.jsonl` follows `director.jsonl` and is not cut by a replay (`keep_director`).

**The game table.** `actions.GAME_SPECS` (`GAME_SPEC_VERSION` "game-v0") is a table of `Spec` rows keyed like `MENU` and
**overrides it; it is not a subset**: Food `regen_pulse` (mult 0.6 to 1.5 with the open range 0.9 to 1.15 *refused*, not
clamped; duration 3,000 to 12,000; cost 1; cooldown 3,000), Bloom `fertility_shift` (a *timed* gain, 1.5 to 2.0;
3,000 to 12,000; 1; 3,000; the move form does not exist), Blight `habitat_loss` (3,000 to 12,000; 2; 6,000), Strike
`catastrophe` (kill_p 0.3 to 0.6, radius 20 to 80 in the units of a 1024-wide world and scaled by `L / 1024` like the
research range, so 6.25 to 25 on the 320-wide planet; one step; 1; 3,000). Durations round up to `Spec.quantum` (250 for
the player; `director.rule_every` where it is `None`, as for `MENU`), and a `Spec` may list `excluded` open ranges.
`MENU` is byte-identical. `Spec` gained `quantum` and `excluded`, both off for `MENU`; `clamp(..., specs=)`,
`radius_bounds(cfg, specs)`, and the checks behind `validate_entry` take the table, which `validate_entry` picks from the
record (`is_player`). A player's record may be at any non-negative step (the rest: a positive multiple of `rule_every`),
carries its scope, a command, the power for its action, the table's version and cost. `SOURCES` stays the research ones; `GAME_SOURCES` adds `player`, for the player's records only. A revert
is valid for an action whose table row is timed (`fertility_shift` is timed in `GAME_SPECS` and permanent in `MENU`, so a
research revert of it is still refused). Influence is `PLAYER_BUDGET` (6) cost units per `PLAYER_BUDGET_WINDOW` (18,000)
steps.

**Timed is a property of the entry** (it has a duration), not of the action's name: `pacing.fold`, `log.validate_log`
and `Director` test `actions.is_timed(entry)`. The permanent `fertility_shift` gains of the research logs
(`eval_s0_C` 4, `eval_s1_C` 1, `eval_s0_RC` 3, `duration` null) hold no lever, as before. `actions.TIMED` stays the
names of `MENU`'s timed rows.

**Pacing scopes.** `pacing.fold(entries, t, scope)` with `scope` `rule`, `player` or `None` (all): the rule scope
ignores the player's records in `spent`, `ends`, `last_*` (so in budget, cooldown and drama), the player scope ignores
everything else in them, `None` counts all; the cost is `entry["cost"]` when it has one (else `MENU`'s, identical on a
research log). `active` (lever exclusivity: `regen`, `patch:<p>`) is shared and each `Effect` carries its `scope`;
`due_reverts(p, t, scope)` returns only that scope's, so the rule tier never reverts a player's effect and the player
never reverts a rule's. `Director._context` and `_decide` use `scope="rule"`, and the extinction rescue's override of the
regen lever supersedes a player's pulse as it does any older one; a lever held by the player is a blocked note ("regen is
held by the player") for the rule tier, not a supersede. `pacing.player_blocked(mine, shared, action, params, t)` is the
player's eligibility: the cooldown from the end of the action's latest player effect (cancelling does not shorten it), the
rolling influence, and a lever held by any active effect.

**Applying.** `apply_pending(state, t)` in live and player mode: (1) the reverts of the player's effects due at `t`
(`due_reverts(..., "player")`; an effect ends at `origin + duration`, which is off every grid when the origin is), then
(2) the queued requests in order, each *planned again against the state as it is* (`clamp` with the game table,
`player_blocked`, `validate_entry`, `apply`); a refusal is kept for `take_player` and logged nowhere. What was applied is
appended to `director.jsonl` (fsync) before the state is returned. `plan_player(state, request, t)` is the dry run
(preview): it folds the queue in first and changes nothing. A **cancel** (`PlayerRequest.cancel`) ends the running effects
of that power (those of one patch with `patch`): a `revert` with `scope: "player"` and `reason` "cancelled by the player"
written at `t`, no refund.
With `stopping` (the pacer asked for a stop or SIGINT is latched; the loop still runs one more step) the queue is dropped
unlogged and no new power is applied, so a quit never logs a power for a world that is going away; the ends of running
effects still apply (otherwise a stopped and resumed world would differ from an uninterrupted one by a step), and a
replay applies its records regardless (its checkpoint must hold them).

**Identity for research logs** (tested): `fold`, `due_reverts`, `budget_used`, `cooldown_ready` and `validate_log` over
the nine research `director.jsonl` files of the evaluation and the 3D runs give the same results before and after
(`tests/director_identity.py`, `tests/data/director_logs/`, digests computed on the parent commit), the 2D digest matrix
of the tree is bit-identical to its parent commit's on the CPU, and so are the tiny3d state (`1fe07a9f…`) and legacy
(`556de6c6…`) digests. (The powers' pacer lines, `PLAN` and the precedent table came with the powers, §34.5.1; the origin
step in N1's fold with the report, §34.4.)

#### 34.5.1 The powers in the play loop (`game/powers.py`, `game/precedents.py`, commit 7)

**Names and lines.** Food (`regen_pulse`), Bloom (`fertility_shift`), Blight (`habitat_loss`) and Strike (`catastrophe`)
are `powers.POWER_SPECS` over `actions.GAME_POWERS`; each takes the keys of its row only (Food `mult steps`, Bloom
`patch x y gain steps`, Blight `patch x y steps`, Strike `x y radius kill`; another key is refused). Defaults: `steps`
6,000 for a timed power, Bloom's `gain` the middle of the table's range, Strike's `radius` and `kill` the middle of
theirs; Food has no default `mult` (the direction matters) and a Strike needs its `x y`. A patch power takes `patch=i` or the
patch nearest (torus) to `x y`, the click the window makes. `request_of` makes the `PlayerRequest` and the `raw` object of
the plan (the player's values, defaults filled in, a click resolved to its patch). The line grammar bounds `id`, `steps`
and `patch` at an int64 and a decimal at a finite number (a 400-digit decimal is `inf` in a float and cannot be JSON).

**The exchange** (`PowerDesk.handle`, called from `PlayPacer._command` at the top of iteration `t`, the step the power would
be applied at; a paused world stands at `t`, so the power lands at the first step after `run` or `step`). `power preview`
dry-runs the director (`plan_player`: the queue folded in first, nothing changed) and answers one `PLAN`, `preview`, with the
reply flag. `power` makes the same checks, calls `queue_player`, answers `queued` and sends an `ENVS` (the units it holds). The
runner applies it at the top of this iteration; the next `after_step` takes what the director did (`take_player`): `applied`
(the entry's `step_applied`), an `EVNT` of kind 20 `power_applied` (importance 1, a strike at its place) and an `ENVS` (the
effect, the units, the lever). `power cancel NAME id=N` answers `queued` ("Food stops at step t. No refund; ready again at
step r"), then `cancelled` under its own id with the `EVNT` of kind 21 `power_ended` (importance 0) and an `ENVS`; the
cooldown runs from the planned end. The natural end of an effect is the director's own revert: an `EVNT` 21 and an `ENVS`, no
alert (the surfaces of one power are its cards, §34.3). A refusal is a `PLAN` `refused` with the reason in the player's words
(the reply flag for a preview), written by code before the engine's own check: **cooldown, then units, then lever** ("Food is
cooling down until step 9,100." / "Blight costs 2 units; 1 left until step 18,110." / "Food is busy: the regen lever is held
until step 6,100."); the engine's messages (a value in the dead zone, a nonexistent patch) are put in the player's words by
`player_words`, and an engine message with a word the lexicon forbids is replaced by a plain one. In a **replay** a power is
refused ("A replay plays the log back; it takes no new power."), the logged ones are shown (`applied`, the cards, `ENVS`
with their source `player`) and nothing is written to `commands.jsonl`; a world with no director refuses too. A request still
queued at `quit` is dropped (never logged): its `commands.jsonl` line says `queued`. `intent TEXT` is answered with a `PLAN`
of kind `intent`, id 0, `refused`, "intent is not available in this build" (the shape of G4's plan row).

**The plan.** `PowerDesk.plan` builds the 20 keys of `PLAN` from the director's entry for the request: `params` the clamped
values, `clamped` the names of the line's keys the engine moved (a bound, the duration rounded up to the quantum, a wrapped
coordinate), `ends` = `t + duration`, `ready` = `ends + cooldown` (a strike: `t + cooldown`), `holds` the lever (`regen`,
`patch:i`), `influence` after the request, `text` a sentence from closed templates ("Food x1.3 for 6,000 steps (6.9 min at
1x), cost 1, 5 of 6 units left after."; Bloom and Blight name the patch; Strike names the centre, radius and kill chance),
`caution` clauses of at most 100 characters (the lever held until a step, said "if applied now, ..." in a preview or a queued request of a world that is running, whose
power lands a few steps later, and plainly when the world is paused or the plan is the applied one; Food and Bloom: "population N of 65,536 slots", the organisms against the slots of the state, which are no carrying capacity; Strike: the organisms in the column and the deaths on average, read once from the state between steps; "lands when the
world resumes" while paused), and the `precedent`. The **precedent** is the table of `game/precedents.py`
(`PRECEDENT_VERSION` 1), keyed `(action, direction)`: the only row is Food downward, from the 14 damper pulses of the 3D
director runs (`RESULTS_3D_RUNS` §5.4: ln `n_alive` -0.136, interval -0.150 to -0.124, complete within about 1,000 steps,
reversing within about 1,000 steps of the end): "Earlier x0.8 pulses (14 in the 3D director runs): the population fell 13% (12% to
14%) within about 1,000 steps and rose again within about 1,000 steps of the end." A direction with no row says "No earlier case
for x1.3." and never shows the other direction's result; the object is `{version, key, n, line, source, step, action, params,
rows}` (the last four keep the shape of the spec's §7.4). The world's own earlier cases are only a `since` fact.

**Influence** is a fold over the log (`powers.influence`): `have` = `PLAYER_BUDGET` minus the costs of the player's entries in
`(t - window, t]`, `cap`, `window` (`PLAYER_BUDGET_WINDOW`) and `free_at`, the steps at which each spent unit comes back
(`step + window`, a unit of cost 2 twice). The units a queued request will hold are folded in from the moment it is queued
(`PowerDesk.reserved`, released when it is applied or refused). `ENVS` gains, for a world that takes powers: `influence`,
`patches` (the food patches with their current gain and sigma, from `State.patch_pos` and the environment) and `powers`
(`{ready, busy}` per power from the same eligibility code; a patch power is checked without a target).

**The since card** (`PLAN` `since`, one per milestone, the client keeps one card per id): the milestones are +250 and +1,000 steps
after the application and the end of a timed effect (the step of its revert or of the cancellation); at each metrics row the
desk sends a `PLAN` when a milestone has a row. `since.rows` holds the row at or before the application (a power is applied
after the row at its own step, so that row is the "before"), the first row after it (the row whose interval holds the
application: a strike's catastrophe deaths are in it) and the first row at or after each milestone, as `{step, alive (the
living at the end of the row), starved, killed, born, storm, catastrophe}` from the metrics row. A card is a function of the
entry, the step it ended at and the metrics rows, so a world that is opened (a resume, a replay) rebuilds the cards still open
from `director.jsonl` and `metrics.jsonl` and sends `applied` and what the card holds (`PowerDesk.open`), and the cards go on
as an uninterrupted world's would (tested). A strike's card also carries `disc` = `{before, after}`, the organisms in its
column read from the state when it was queued and one step after it was applied (two host reads of `pos` and `alive` between
steps; the spec drew them from the frames, which are not built at those steps).

**`commands.jsonl`** (`runio.COMMANDS_FILE`, append-only, fsync): one line per `power` or `intent` line, `{id, t, verb, status,
line, entry_step, reason}` with `t` the step the line was handled at (the iteration; also the step the power is applied at),
`verb` `preview`, `power`, `cancel` or `intent` and `status` `preview`, `queued`, `refused`. The last line of an id says what
became of it: a queued request gets an `applied` line (`entry_step`) when the director has applied it, or a `refused` line (a
request that passed the checks and was refused when applied; none was seen, the dry run and the application share one code
path). `RunDir.truncate_after` cuts it by `t < step` (rule P) when the director log is cut, and a replay never writes or cuts
it. It is the input log of G5's frequency analysis ("one input every two minutes").

**The lexicon.** Every string above (the sentences, cautions, precedent lines, refusals, cancel texts, the engine's messages in
the player's words) passes `lexicon` v3 on the `NEVER` and `LABEL` lists (lever words are the interventions' own and allowed).
The spec's wording hit the lexicon in four places and is changed: the budget is "units" in sentences ("influence" is a causal
word, `influenc-`), "needs" is "is missing" (`need-`), "no running effect" is "nothing to cancel" (`effect-`), and Strike's
"expected deaths" is "deaths on average" (`expect-`). The refusal of `intent` quotes the line's own name, which the lexicon lists
as a motive word; it is the one string where the name is masked in the test, as a display name is.

**The ledger.** A power adds no energy path: Food and Blight and Bloom write `env_*` fields the step already reads, Strike kills
through the catastrophe the step already has (its deaths are `deaths_catastrophe`, their energy goes where any death's goes).
The exact 16-term ledger closes at every row of a session of all four powers (`ledger_error` 0 on every row, a strike aimed at an
organism included), and a preview, a refusal or an ignored line leaves checkpoints, rows and events equal to a plain run's.

Tests: `tests/test_powers.py` (the table, the header block, every request and refusal, influence and readiness, the since
rows, the column count, the precedent, the lexicon), `tests/test_play_powers.py` (a session of previews, powers, a cancel,
refusals and `intent` against the exact `PLAN`, `ENVS`, `EVNT` and `commands.jsonl` sequences; digest equality for previews and
refusals; a power while paused; the queue dropped at `quit`; the ledger with all four powers; the cards against the metrics rows
and against the offline function; replay equality by `resume --director replay` and `play --replay` with the inputs untouched;
a replay that refuses; rule P at a chapter end with a crash-resume that cuts the record and its input lines and reproduces the
log byte for byte; a resume that rebuilds the open cards; the live and the backlog chronicle rows equal; a rule tier beside a
player), `test_play_control.py` (the bounds of the grammar, the handlers), `test_play_chronicle.py` (the six power templates).

---

### 34.6 The records: `ALRT`, `RPRT`, `PLAN` and the additions to `ENVS`, `CLCK`, `EVNT` and `IDNT`

Conventions of §33.1.1 (little endian; tag, `u32 len`, the 16-byte common head `u64 step, u32 seq, u16 version, u16 flags`; JSON UTF-8 from `json.dumps(allow_nan=False,
ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))`, `json_len` unpadded then 0 to 3 zero bytes). The three new tags are **queued** (never dropped, in order, deduplicated by their id) and
compatible: **no stream bump**. A client that does not know a tag skips it by its length, one that does not know its version skips and counts it. The header's `play.records` and
`play.versions` list the tags a world sends. The initial state of a G3b world is the header, `FRMA`, `IDNT`, `INTN`, `TERR`, `ENVS`, `MAP1`, `STRM`, `EVNT` (backlog), `ALRT`
(backlog), `RPRT` (backlog, the last three reports), `PLAN` (none), `CLCK`.

**`ALRT`** (version 1; flags bit 0 = backlog, which raises no toast and no pause): the head, `u32 count` (offset 16), `u32 json_len` (20), a JSON array of at most 16 alerts from
offset 24, zero padding (`len = 24 + json_len + pad`; a decoder checks `count` against the array). The JSON of the record is at most 24 KiB. An alert is
`{"id", "version", "step", "class", "key", "state", "surface", "imp", "title", "text", "x", "y", "z", "ref", "pause", "expires", "watched", "calibrated"}`:
`id = first_step * 1000 + 600 + index`, **stable for the alert's life** (the chronicle's families use 0 to 500, so ids never clash); `version` is 1 when raised and grows by one at each
update (a client keeps the newest version of an id); `state` `raised`, `updated` or `cleared` (a cleared alert is removed from the stack); `surface` `alert` (stack, toast, pause) or
`log` (a chronicle row and ticker line with fly-to); `imp` 0 to 3; `title` at most 48 characters and `text` at most 160 (code-written from exact quantities, through N1's lexicon); `x y z` null
when the alert has no place; `ref` null or `{"kind": storm|kin|house|world|power|organism, "id"}`; `pause` whether this alert paused the world; `expires` a step or null; `watched`
whether it concerns a watched thread; `calibrated` whether a measurement backs its threshold. The encoder refuses a class outside the header's registry, a state, surface or
importance outside the lists, `raised` with a version other than 1, `updated` with a version below 2, an id below the alert range, a text over its cap and a repeated id.

**`RPRT`** (version 1; flags bit 0 = backlog, bit 1 = final): the head, `u32 chapter` (16), `u32 mode` (20; 0 template, 1 select, 2 away), `u32 json_len` (24), `u32 reserved` (28, zero), the
JSON from offset 32 (at most 64 KiB), zero padding. The JSON is the report of N1 with its sections: `{"chapter", "n_abs", "a", "b", "mode", "final", "withheld", "headline", "lead", "body",
"interventions", "ticker", "since", "entities", "versions", "facts_digest", "latency_s", "fallback"}`. The head and the JSON cannot disagree (the encoder takes `chapter`, `mode` and the
final flag from the JSON, the independent decoder checks them); a sentence is `{"id", "text", "refs"}` (`body` adds `origin`) and its `refs` are keys of `entities`, so a click flies to
the entity; a report that could not be cut carries `withheld` reasons and nothing else (`headline` and `lead` null, empty lists), never a guess. The client keeps the newest record per
`(chapter, mode)`; a template report is final, a select report is sent pending (`final` false) and replaced.

**`PLAN`** (version 1; flags bit 0 = reply to a `power preview`): the head, `u32 json_len` (16), the JSON from offset 20 (at most 8 KiB), zero padding. The JSON is `{"id", "kind", "status",
"power", "action", "raw", "params", "clamped", "duration", "step_applied", "ends", "cost", "influence", "ready", "holds", "text", "caution", "precedent", "since", "refused"}`: `id` is the client's
request number (the required `id=N` of every `power` line, echoed in every `PLAN` of the two-click flow), `kind` `power` or `intent`, `status` `preview`, `queued`, `applied`, `refused`, `since` or
`cancelled`, `text` at most 160 characters and each `caution` at most 100. `refused` is a reason exactly when the status is `refused`; an `applied` plan names its `step_applied`; a `preview` is
always a reply. `intent` is answered `refused` ("intent is not available in this build") in G3b, with id 0 (the line has none); the shape is G4's plan row. A `since` plan's `since` is `{"from", "rows"}` and, for a strike, `"disc": {"before", "after"}`; the `precedent` of a power is `{"version", "key", "n", "line", "source", "step", "action", "params", "rows"}` (§34.5.1).

**Header keys** (written only when the world uses them, like the other optional keys): `play.alerts` = `{"version": 1, "classes": {name: {"imp", "pause", "label", "calibrated", "surface"}},
"cap": {"n": 4, "window": 1500, "exempt": ["imp3", "pause", "chapter", "engine"]}}` (the registry an `ALRT` names its classes from); `play.autopause` = `{"chapter": bool, "alert": {class: bool}}` (the
defaults; the client sends its own choice back with `autopause` lines); `play.powers` = `{name: {"action", "label", "cost", "cooldown", "scope" (global, patch or column), "duration" ([low, high] or null), "params" (a range, or a list of ranges where the table excludes one)}}` (`powers.header_block`, written for a world whose director takes powers); `play.game_specs` = the name of the game table
(`"game-v0"`).

**Additions to existing records** (JSON keys and flag bits, no version bump): `ENVS.influence` `{"have", "cap", "window", "free_at"}` (the steps at which spent units come back; `have <= cap`),
`ENVS.patches` `[{"i", "x", "y", "gain", "sigma"}]` (the food patches the powers target), `ENVS.powers` `{name: {"ready", "busy"}}` (the step a power is ready and the reason it is not
usable, or null), and `effects[].source` `rule`, `llm` or `player`; `CLCK.flags` bit 0 (the pause at a chapter end is armed) and bit 1 (at least one alert class is armed; bit 2, the world keeps the newest save only, is §34.10's), `reason` 3 (chapter) and
4 (alert) and the chapter fields with the 1-based meaning of §34.2; `EVNT` kinds 20 `power_applied` and 21 `power_ended` (with 18 and 19 of §34.1); `IDNT.kin[].thread` (§34.1).

**As built (commit 2).** The encoders (`streamrec.encode_alrt`, `encode_rprt`, `encode_plan`, with `check_alert`, `check_report`, `check_plan`, `check_envs`, `alerts_block`, `autopause_block`,
`powers_block`, `header_play(alerts=, autopause=, powers=, game_specs=)`, the `CLCK` flags check and kinds 20 and 21), the independent decoder (`tests/play_decode.py`, written from this section),
and the fixture `tests/data/play_tiny3d_g3b.bin` + `.json` (a chapter end at step 12000: the new header keys, a backlog and a live `ALRT` of every importance, state and ref kind, three `RPRT`
modes and a withheld one, `PLAN` of every status and an intent refusal, `ENVS` with a player effect, `IDNT` with threads, `CLCK` reasons 3 and 4, and an `ALRT` of an unknown version that is
skipped). The three older fixtures keep their bytes except the header's event registry, which now lists kinds 18 to 21, so the Swift decoder of G3a still reads them; the Swift side of the new records
is the next stage (commit 3, below). The play loop sends `ALRT` since the alert engine (§34.3), `RPRT` since the report job (§34.4) and `PLAN` since the powers (§34.5.1); `PLAN` is in every world's `play.records` (a world with no director answers a `power` line with a refusal); the clock fields have their 1-based meaning and `CLCK` reasons 3
and the flags since §34.2.

Tests: `tests/test_stream_records.py` (the layout offsets, padding and flags of each record against the independent decoder, every refusal of the encoders, the caps, the header keys only
when given, `ENVS` and `CLCK` additions, the decoder's own refusals, the fixtures rebuilt byte for byte). Mutation checks by hand (25 mutations of the encoders' limits, flags and
consistency rules) were each caught.

#### 34.6.1 The control lines of the decide half (commit 3: the grammar; each handler comes with its stage)

```text
command = ... | "autopause" ( "on" | "off" | "chapter" ( "on" | "off" ) | "alert" CLASS ( "on" | "off" ) )
              | "watch" ( KIN_ID | "off" ) | "unwatch" KIN_ID | "ack" ALERT_ID
              | "power" [ "preview" | "cancel" ] NAME "id=" N { KEY "=" VALUE } | "intent" TEXT
              | "saves" ( "all" | "newest" )                                                   (§34.10)
NAME = "food" | "bloom" | "blight" | "strike"
KEY  = "mult" | "steps" | "patch" | "gain" | "x" | "y" | "radius" | "kill"      (steps and patch are whole numbers, the rest decimals)
```
Lower case except the free text of `intent`; `CLASS` is `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`; `KIN_ID`, `ALERT_ID` and `N` are non-negative integers (an int64 for the first two); `id=N` is required and the client's own number
(echoed in every `PLAN` of the exchange); a key is named at most once; `power cancel` takes only the id. The grammar checks the shape of a value; its range is the power's to clamp or refuse (§34.5). Presentation-only
lines: `autopause`, `watch`, `unwatch`, `ack`, a `power preview` and a refused `power`; the only lines that change a trajectory are an applied `power` and `power cancel`, which are logged (`director.jsonl`). `play.parse_play_command` returns an `AutopauseLine` or
a `PowerLine` as the argument of its `PlayCommand`; `PlayCommand.swift` (`AutopauseSetting`, `PowerCommand`) writes the same lines, `tests/data/play_command_lines.txt` lists every one of them and `test_gui_sync` ties the names and keys
to `play.POWER_NAMES` and `POWER_KEYS`. Until its stage a line was parsed and answered with a note on stderr ("not available in this build yet"): `autopause` came with the chapter clock (§34.2),
`watch`, `unwatch` and `ack` with the alert engine (§34.3), `power` and `intent` with the powers (§34.5.1); `play.UNBUILT_LINES` is empty. `id`, `steps` and `patch` are bounded at an int64 and a decimal must be finite.

#### 34.6.2 The Swift side of the records (commit 3)

`PlayRecords.swift`: `PlayAlert`, `PlayAlertBatch` (`ALRT`), `ReportBody` and `PlayReport` (`RPRT`), `PlanBody` and `PlayPlan` (`PLAN`), three more cases of `StreamRecord`, `PlayHeader.Alerts`, `.Autopause`, `.Power` and `gameSpecs`,
`PlayEnvironment.Influence`, `.Patch` and `.PowerState` (the `ENVS` additions), `IdentityTables.Kin.thread` and the `CLCK` flag accessors. The decoder checks what the encoders check: the prefix counts against the length before the payload
is waited for, the JSON caps (24 KiB, 64 KiB, 8 KiB), at most 16 alerts and no repeated id, an id in the alert range, importance 0 to 3, the title and text caps, `raised` at version 1 and `updated` at 2 or more, the head of an `RPRT` against its JSON
(chapter, mode, final), a withheld report that is empty, a reserved word that is zero, and in a `PLAN` the caps, `refused` exactly when refused, an applied plan naming its step and a preview that is a reply. A tag of another version is skipped by its length and counted.
The mailbox queues the three tags like `EVNT`. `WorldStore` gains `AlertBoard` (the newest `version` of each id in id order, 200 kept; `cleared` stays in the ring but leaves the stack; an unknown id is new; the stack is the `alert`
surface minus the cleared, the acknowledged and the expired, and an alert with no `expires` stays until cleared or acknowledged; only an explicit `acknowledge` acknowledges), `ReportShelf` (the newest record per `(chapter, mode)`, 24 chapters kept,
a pending report never replaces a final one, `current(chapter:)` prefers a select report that has arrived) and `PlanLog` (50 records, one card per request id), and exposes the player's influence, patches and power states from `ENVS`.
`PlayController` reports what each alert batch did (`onAlerts`, with the backlog flag) before the delivery. Tests: `PlayRecordsG3bTests` (the fixture, every refusal by hand-built records, truncation, unknown versions, the header keys),
`WorldStoreG3bTests`, `PlayCommandTests` (the new lines), the mailbox and controller tests, and `test_gui_sync` (the keys of every new Swift type against the encoders' key sets and the independent decoder's sidecar, the caps and the flag bits).

### 34.7 The World window: the decide half (commit 8)

The window of G3a (§33.4) keeps its structure; this commit adds what the player reads and does at a chapter's end, and the places those go. Every decision is a pure type of `AlifeCore` (no window, no clock),
tested alone; the views lay out what they decided and send clicks to `WorldModel`. **Presentation never changes a trajectory; the only lines of the window that do are an applied `power` and `power cancel`.**

| piece | file | content |
|---|---|---|
| `ChapterBar`, `ChapterOrigin` | `AlifeCore/ChapterBar.swift` | the label "Chapter N" (`CLCK.chapter` less the origin, at least 1), `in_chapter / chapter_len`, "next report in m:ss" at the achieved pace, the lock and the bell from `CLCK.flags`, the marks of toast-sized events and alerts; `ChapterOrigin.chapter` reads `made_at_step / chapter` from `play.json` |
| `AlertStack`, `AlertRow`, `WatchSet`, `DockBudget` | `AlifeCore/AlertStack.swift`, `DockLayout.swift` | the stack layout and the watch set (three kin groups), the rows that fit a dock |
| `ChapterCard`, `SinceStrip`, `ReportCard`, `ReportTabModel` | `AlifeCore/ChapterCard.swift` | the card over the map, the strip, the report as the window lays it out, the Report tab |
| `PowersModel`, `PowerOffer`, `PowerCatalog`, `PowerPreviewCard`, `InfluenceMeter`, `ActiveEffect`, `PowerCardModel` | `AlifeCore/PowersModel.swift` | the grid and the aim-preview-confirm exchange, as a state machine over lines and `PLAN` records |
| `AutopausePrefs`, `AttentionTracker`, `WorldTitle` | `AlifeCore/WorldPresentation.swift` | the pauses the player chose, the dock icon and badge, the window's title |
| `Ticker`, `ToastQueue` | `AlifeCore/WorldChronicle.swift` | the line at the bottom of the map; toasts from alerts (and from events in a world with no alert engine) |
| `Numbers` | `AlifeCore/Numbers.swift` | thousands grouped by a comma whatever the locale |
| `WorldModel+Decide`, `ChapterBarView`, `AlertStackView`, `ChapterCardView`, `ReportTabView`, `PowersTabView`, `TickerView` | `AlifeControl/` | the glue and the views |
| `StorageScan`, `StorageFormat`, `StorageHealth`, `StorageTrend`, `StorageReadout`, `SaveModeView`, `SaveMode` | `AlifeCore/Storage.swift`, `PlayCommand.swift` | the size of a world on disk, its text, the warning, the growth and the save mode the window shows (§34.10) |
| `StorageMonitor`, `StorageStripView`, `StorageDetailsView`, `StorageBadge` | `AlifeControl/StorageMonitor.swift`, `StorageViews.swift` | the 5-second measurement and the strip with the recording switch (§34.10) |

**The chapter bar** sits in the clock strip. The number is `CLCK.chapter - originChapter`, where `PlayController.originChapter` is read once, when the header arrives, from `runs/<world>/play.json` (`made_at_step / header.chapter`; 0 for a preset, an
adopted run or an unreadable file). The first moment of a fork (step 450,000: the clock names chapter 75 at 100%) is "Chapter 1" at 0%, never "Chapter 0" or a full bar; a fork at an off-grid step keeps the same origin chapter and its first chapter is the
arrival chapter. The lock is the truth of `CLCK.flags` bit 0 and a click sends `autopause chapter on|off`; the bell is bit 1. The strip's readout names the stop: "Chapter 3 complete" (reason 3) and the title of the newest pausing alert on the stack (reason 4).

**The alert stack** shows the alerts of the `alert` surface that are not cleared, not acknowledged and not expired, **most important first and the newest first among equals**, so that a pausing alert is never the one hidden under the "+N more". Three rows
when the dock is roomy; `DockBudget.alertRows` gives fewer when it is not, never none. A row has the tone of its importance, its title and text, a mark for a class with no measurement behind it ("provisional"), an arrow (fly to its place and select its
storm, group or organism, `ChronicleAction.of(alert)`), a star for a kin alert (`watch` / `unwatch`, at most three; the Cast's rows have the same star) and a check (`ack ID`). **Nothing else removes a row**: not `Esc`, not Continue, not the arrow. While the chapter card (or its notice) is up, the chapter's own alert is not a row (`AlertStack.layout(excluding:)`): the card and the strip's "Chapter 3 complete" announce it, and a third announcement costs a row in a dock that has none to spare.
A side dock has the rows between the clock strip and the tabs; a bottom dock, or a collapsed one, has them over the map, top left. **The dock fits the minimum window.** Measured through `NSHostingView` at width 360 (`theSideDockFitsTheMinimumWindow`): the clock
strip with its chapter bar 125 points (131 before §34.10 trimmed its bottom padding to 4), the Storage strip of §34.10 20 and its 6 below, the tab picker 40, an alert row 44 (48 with its gap), the dock header 28, the list's least 120 and the inspector card 261 for an organism, 189 for a storm and 126 for a group (the dock caps it at 300 and scrolls it); with the card
budgeted at 262 (270 before the Storage strip took its room), a 700-point dock has room for **two** rows beside the open inspector and three without it (three beside the inspector now need 760 points, not 740; the strip has no second line, so switching the save mode never costs a row). The order in which the layout gives way is the spec's: the card's since strip scrolls, the alert rows cap, the card's body keeps headline and lead.

**The chapter card** is over the map while `CLCK.reason` is 3: `saving` (the checkpoint is being written: the title, "saving…", the report if it has landed, else the previous chapter's headline greyed; no buttons), `ready` (the world is stopped: the report, the since
strip and the buttons Continue, Continue at 2x, Powers and Show on map) and `notice` (the pause is off, the world runs on: the same words in a small banner with Report and a close button, shown **once per chapter** and gone after 15 s). The report is the template record of
the chapter with that absolute number (`ReportShelf.report(nAbs:)`); a withheld one says why and nothing else; a quiet chapter shows headline, lead and buttons; the card keeps six body lines and says how many are in the tab, and on a map under 520 points high it keeps headline and lead.
The since strip is the live `ENVS` (units and the step the next comes back, the powers usable now, the effects that end within a chapter), the report's alert counts by class label (else counted on the board) and the three most important alerts of the chapter with their arrows. **`Esc` folds the card
to a one-line bar, never resumes**; the card also folds by itself while a patch or column power is being aimed and unfolds when that ends (the map is the target). A new chapter's card starts unfolded.

**The Report tab** shows the newest chapter in full (headline, lead, every body sentence, the interventions last, the since strip, the ticker lines) and the earlier ones (24 kept) as headlines that open. A click on a sentence flies to the first entity in its `refs` that the report can place
(`ChronicleAction.of(refs:entities:)`). **The Powers tab** is the grid (Food, Bloom, Blight, Strike from the header's `powers`, with the bounds, cost, cooldown ring from `ENVS.powers` and the world's own reason when a power is busy), two greyed rows for the storm levers (W4), the units as
pips (each spent one with the step it returns), the sliders, the preview card, the running effects with "End early" (no refund; the cooldown is the planned end's) and one card per request. `PowersModel` is a state machine: `idle`, `aiming` (a patch or column power waits for a click),
`previewing(id)`, `previewed(id)`, `refused(id, reason)` and `submitted(id)`. **The exchange.** Choosing Food sends `power preview food id=N mult=1.3 steps=6000` at once; Bloom, Blight and Strike wait for a click on the map, which names the nearest patch on the torus (`patch=i`) or the column
(`x=… y=…`, from `WorldProjector.world(at:height:)`, the plane at the camera target's height), and then send the preview. A slider is sent when it is let go and asks for a new preview with a **new id**; the answer to an older id is ignored. Confirm (`Return`) sends `power NAME id=N …` with the id and values of the preview
the player saw, and the world re-checks them (a stale preview is refused, never applied). A setting skips the second click for a cost-1 power (off by default). Ids start past every id the window has seen in the plan log, so a resumed world's cards keep theirs. The values come from the header: `[lo, hi]` or two ranges with a hole (Food's dead zone,
where a value moves to the nearest accepted edge, the lower on a tie), durations in multiples of 250, `kill_p` written `kill` on the line. A strike's card shows the organisms in its column before and after (`PLAN.since.disc`). In a short dock the editor and Confirm sit below the grid: choosing a power, and its preview arriving, scroll the bottom of the editor into view, and the inspector under the tabs takes its card's height, not the cap (its frame used to stretch to 300 points and leave a blank under the card). **While a power is chosen** the Powers tab keeps `DockBudget.editor` (300) points: the inspector card waits (the selection is kept, the card returns when the power is done), and the alert rows give way, never below one (`alertRows(dockHeight:inspectorOpen:editing:)`; at 700 points three rows and a 356-point tab, where two rows and the open inspector left about 180).

**Keys** (`WorldKeys`, DESIGN §33.4.8 extended): `space` pause/run, `g` continue (`continueRun`: resume; never pauses), `.` step, `c` colour, `1 2 3` layers, `f` follow, `[ ]` rate, `r` reset camera (**§36.5: `r` and `h` fly Home, `n` is north up, `i` the minimap**), `p` the Powers tab (`showPowers`), `a` fly to the newest alert (`flyToAlert`), `k` acknowledge the newest alert on the stack
(`acknowledgeAlert`), `Return` confirm the previewed power (`confirmPower`: **only while the Powers tab shows the preview**, `WorldModel.returnConfirmsPower`; a new chapter drops an unsent preview or aim) and `Esc` (`escape`). **`Esc` has one meaning per state and never resumes or acknowledges**: it cancels aiming, else drops the preview of a power, else folds the chapter card, else clears the selection and the follow (G3a's meaning), one level per press;
a power already sent is not the player's to take back. `test_gui_sync` pins the table against this section.

**The pauses the player chose** are an `AutopausePrefs` (chapter on or off, a class on or off) in the user defaults, shown in the View menu ("Pauses") and sent after every header as the `autopause` lines that differ from the header's defaults (a class the world does not know is left out). **The ticker** is one line at the bottom of the map: the newest told event of the chronicle
(importance 1 or more, no system or focus events), log-surface alert or a line of a live report dated within one snapshot (250 steps) of the chapter's end (the older ones of its chapter were told when they happened, and the Report tab has them), for 17 s, no filler; a click flies to its place. **Toasts** now come from alerts (stack surface, importance 2 or more, not the chapter's own alert, which is the card, and never the backlog); in a world with no alert engine (a G3a header) events toast as before.
**Attention**: a stop (reason 3 or 4 at rate 0) arriving while the window is not key calls `NSApp.requestUserAttention(.informationalRequest)` once per stop and sets the dock badge to the number of stack alerts raised since; the badge goes when the window becomes key or the app active. **The chronicle** hides the raw kin events (kinds 1 to 4, which G3b no longer tells) in a G3b world; the View menu's developer item shows them.

**The three cosmetic findings of the G3a Mac day** (`RESULTS_G3A` §8): the lineage rows no longer truncate "died: 3,091 starved, 3,099 killed…" (their own line, wrapping), counts are grouped by `Numbers.grouped` and set `verbatim` ("6,216 born", not the locale's "6.216"; the strip's step, a chronicle row's step and a group's header `steps 11,232 to 12,095` as well, `Numbers.stepLabel`), and the dock and the window title say "Planet p0" with "forked from runs/…" under it
(`WorldTitle`), not the run's directory name.

**Deviations from the spec text.** (1) The chapter alert is not also a toast (the card or notice is its announcement). (2) The alert stack orders by importance first, then newest (the spec says newest first). (3) The lineage rows' star is in the Cast tab as well as on alert rows. (4) The ticker also takes a live report's last ticker line. (5) The card folds by itself while a power is aimed, as a derived state, not a stored one.
(6) The raw kin events are hidden only in a world with an alert engine, so a G3a stream keeps its lineages. (7) `ChapterBar.ticks` marks events of importance 2 and the alerts of the stack. (8) The alert rows' budget is a measured function, not "two": one to three.

**Tests.** `AlifeCoreTests` 373 to 465 (+92): `ChapterBarTests`, `AlertStackTests`, `ChapterCardTests`, `PowersModelTests`, `WorldPresentationTests`, `NumbersTests`, `AlertToastAndTickerTests`, `WorldProjectorUnprojectTests`, `ClockStripDecideTests`, `DockBudgetTests`, `PlanSinceDiscTests`, and the key table. `AlifeControlTests` 202 to 240 (+38): `WorldDecideTests` (the lines that reach the world,
Esc's levels, the notice, the pauses re-sent, the two-click flow and a strike aimed on the map, with nothing else sent), `WorldDecideViewTests` (the views draw, the side dock fits the minimum window), `PlayControllerDecideTests` (the origin, the hooks, `ack`).
