### 34.8 Performance, the bench and the gate (commit 9)

`alife bench --play` (§33.5) gains the **player** director mode (`--play-directors off,rules,player`, all three when `director.enabled`), **scripted powers** (`--play-powers`), a **resumed played world** (`--play-resume SRC[:STEP]`, a run's checkpoint or a state file as it is, with the weather and the director as that world has them)
and `--play-chapter N` (tests shorten the chapter). The gate of the G3b merge (spec §10) is read from it, on the planet configuration:

| item | measurement | limit |
|---|---|---|
| achieved at 1x, `late_steps`, `step_ms` p99; achieved at max | as G3a (§33.5.3) | 0.98x, 0, 66 ms; 2.5x |
| click to `PLAN` applied | `ScriptedControl` notes when a power's line is handed over, `BenchPacer._write` when its `applied` record is written; p95 over the arm's clicks | 0.5 s (C6: 2 s) |
| report | from `before_checkpoint` of a chapter end to its `RPRT` on the stream (a worker's write) | 500 ms |
| digest of an arm without powers | equal to a run with no pacer, per director mode (`off`, `rules`, `player`) | equal |
| digest of an arm with powers | equal to `_replay_digest`: the arm's own `director.jsonl` replayed from its first step by `runner.run` with `run.director=replay` (what `resume --director replay` does) | equal; and different from the plain run (the powers are the trajectory's) |

The two scripted powers (`power_script`): a **Food x1.3 for 3,000 steps** half way between the end of the warm-up and the next chapter's end, and a **Strike** (the table's smallest radius, kill 0.45, at the world's centre) **at the chapter-end step itself** (rule P). The arm
must hold that chapter end in its measured part (`ConfigError` otherwise, with the steps it would need): the Mac day resumes a played planet's checkpoint some steps before a chapter's end (`--play-resume`; the p0 checkpoint at 470,002 is 4,000 steps before 474,000, and 300 + 4,320 steps hold it). The arm adds a **chapter, report and alert line**:
the chapter ends it held, the report's time on the stream, and the time and calls of the alert engine (`on_record`, `on_tick`, `on_row`, `on_chapter`, `on_territory`, `engine_check` wrapped by the bench pacer). Nothing in the arms arms a pause (an arm has nobody to press `run`).

**Tests and checks.** `tests/test_bench.py` (+10): the player arm without powers equals the plain run (three director modes); scripted powers are applied at the steps they were sent (a Food at 20, a Strike at the chapter-end step 30), both are in the arm's own log as the player's, and the arm equals the replay of that log and differs from the plain run;
the arm refuses a chapter end that is not in its measured part (before it, at its start, at its last step); the player mode needs the levers; `ScriptedControl`; the gate reads latency and report time; `alife bench --play --play-powers --play-chapter` and `--play-resume` from the command line; the bench pacer parses the `RPRT` and `PLAN` records it writes (a backlog report is not a chapter's, a worker's write is not the loop's, the first `applied` stands);
a refused power is not applied and fails the gate. Mutations by hand: 69 of the window's pure types, its model and views (66 caught at first, 2 equivalent or empty, 3 gaps closed by tests: the pace under 50 steps a second, a disarmed lock while stopped at the card, an event that must not toast in a world with alerts), and 15 of the bench (13 caught at first, 2 gaps closed: `all_applied` and the gate's use of it).
**A real process.** The decide half was also run against a real `alife play` (CPU, tiny3d, a director, `--rate max`) from a throwaway Swift test (not committed): through its first chapter (two alert stops acknowledged and continued, the card with the report "Population dipped to 18", the strip, two alert rows), a Food previewed and confirmed (a card "applied", the unit spent, the effect to 12,000), and a Strike aimed
on the map (preview "Strike at (64.0, 64.0), radius 6.25 ...", applied, the ticker line); no protocol mismatch was found.

**Not run here.** The bench's code is tested on the CPU with 256-row worlds and a 30-step chapter (`tests/test_bench.py`): the report job exists only for a chapter that is a whole number of 250-step snapshots, so a smoke arm has no report time; the Mac day runs the real chapter. No Metal bench, no GPU test, no LM Studio call was made by this commit.

**Built (this branch, nine commits and the stages that landed them):** the player channel and rule P (§34.5), kin threads and storm persistence (§34.1), the records (§34.6), chapters and the pause (§34.2), alerts (§34.3), report v2 and the job (§34.4), the powers (§34.5.1), the window (§34.7) and the bench (§34.8). Checked on the CPU: the fast
Python suite, the bit-identity of the trajectory with the player channel unused (the 2D digest matrix against `a8956b9`, the tiny3d digests, the nine research director logs), replay equality of played powers by both replay commands, `swift build` and `swift test` with warnings as errors.

**Run on the Mac day (2026-10-23, §34.8, `docs/RESULTS_G3B.md`):** Metal purity for the new and extended files (34 files, 1,393 passed); the gate on the planet configuration and at 2x (passes; the report-time item is not readable in the bench); click-to-applied on the GPU; the chapter stall with the report readable inside it (the stall itself was measured; the card was rendered offscreen, not seen with a person's eyes); a play of 18,001 steps on one window (p0) with a strict scripted reader against the bands of spec §11 (chronicle, kin and alert rates inside; 4 pauses, one of them the aftermath of a power).
**Still not run:** the second window of the play (a fork of `64k3d_s1`) and the 20,000th step; the client's draw beside a running engine; the 2D digest matrix and `test_weather_w2_instruments` on Metal; the first play-test by a person in `player` mode (inputs per chapter from `commands.jsonl`: whether the owner acts at all without an objective, D9; the Mac day's `commands.jsonl` is a script's); the click-through.
**Known defects:** the bench's report time (copy the source's history into the arm, or refuse a chapter it cannot report). The report chapter number from the planet's origin was found on the Mac day (the render showed the Report tab at "Chapter 79" on `p0`) and is fixed in `G3b: report chapters count from the planet origin`: `cli.py` passes `made_at_step` as `PlayOptions.origin_step` for a new planet and a resume, with `tests/test_report_chapter_origin.py` (a planet made at a non-zero step) and the unit tests of the arithmetic.
**Precondition (spec §11):** the owner's click-through of the G3a window (`RESULTS_G3A` §9 item 1) was to happen before the Mac day, and the window's own click-through (the card, the stack, the Powers tab, aiming a strike on the map) with it; it did not (the Mac day ran without it), so the window has been drawn by tests and rendered offscreen and looked at (`RESULTS_G3B` §8), and no person has used it.

**Open, for the owner (choice C20 took every recommendation):** whether a fresh preset world should have a few rows of grace before its founding die-off raises `pop_fall` and stops it (stage 4); the objective (D9), which waits for the owner's first play-through (inputs per chapter from `commands.jsonl`); the lineage alert classes on the stack for a watched thread; and the Strike cooldown (D10).

### 34.10 Storage: the size monitor and the save mode (the owner's request of 2026-10-23, row I56)

The owner, on his first play of the World window: the window should monitor live the size of a run on disk if it is being recorded, and the player should be able to switch recording off from the side panel. A played world records no video. About 99% of its disk is the **saves** (one 686 MB checkpoint at every chapter end, every 6,000 steps, and on quit; the last three and the origin are kept, so a world plateaus near 3 GB; a 4,000-step session left `runs/planet_a` at 2.6 GB with four saves: the origin 500,000, 500,001, 504,000 and the quit save 504,001) and the rest is **logs** (event chunks about 0.6 KB a step, the observers' files, metrics, alerts, reports, `director.jsonl` with the player's powers, `commands.jsonl`), a few MB a chapter, which the reports and the replays read. **Decision (the owner): switching recording off means keep only the newest save, plus the origin, which is always kept. Saves still happen at chapter ends and on quit, each replacing the previous one; the logs are still written.** The design note of the build is this section; nothing else changed in the engine.

**The save mode** is a storage setting of the played world, `all` (the default: `run.keep_checkpoints`, 3, and the origin) or `newest` (the newest save and the origin).

- *Grammar.* `saves all` / `saves newest` (§33.2.6, §34.6.1): `play.parse_play_command` returns `PlayCommand("saves", "all" | "newest")`, anything else is a `ControlError` (the line is ignored with a note). `PlayCommand.saves(SaveMode)` writes it; `tests/data/play_command_lines.txt` lists both lines and `test_gui_sync` parses them.
- *Where it acts.* `RunDir.keep_newest` (an attribute of the object, not a config key, so it is not in the config hash and no `POST_V01_KEYS` entry is needed): `save_checkpoint` prunes down to `keep = 1` when it is set, else to `run.keep_checkpoints`. `_prune` already protects step 0, `meta.start_step` (the fork's origin) and whatever `LATEST` names, and removes the observer sidecars and play-state files of the checkpoints it removes, so the origin and the newest save are never deleted in either mode, and a sidecar lives as long as its save. The pruning comes after the new save is written and named in `LATEST`, so a complete save exists at every instant (a full disk fails the write of the new file and leaves the old one). In `newest` mode the one older save is the only fallback, so before it goes `save_checkpoint` makes sure of the new one: it flushes it past the drive's cache (`runio._full_sync`: `F_FULLFSYNC`; `os.fsync` on macOS stops at the drive, which a power cut can still empty; `os.fsync` where the call is refused; one flush a save, in this mode only), then reads its header and length back (`runio.state_file_is_complete`: the header names the step, the file is at least as long as its last tensor ends) and prunes only if that passes; failing, the prune is the `all` one, so the older saves stay, and stderr says so ("does not read back whole; the older saves are kept"). `_prune` also removes the temporary files of a save that a kill interrupted (a state file's is up to 686 MB): `step_<t>.safetensors.tmp` and `LATEST.tmp` in `checkpoints/`, a sidecar's `step_<t>.npz.tmp` and a play-state file's `<name>_<t>.json.tmp` in `observers/` (`runio._SAVE_TMP_RE`). The one process that saves a run writes these names only in `save_checkpoint` and the play loop's `before_checkpoint`, which are done when it prunes, so every such file is debris; any other `*.tmp` (a houses file that `alife houses` may be writing) is left alone.
- *When.* **The switch deletes nothing.** `saves newest` makes the next save (the next chapter end, or the quit save, or the first save of a resume) prune; `saves all` keeps the saves from then on (the ones already pruned are gone; the count of three starts again). A `saves` line that changes nothing does nothing. The window says so ("Older saves are deleted at the next save, not now").
- *Persistence.* `play.json` has `saves: "newest"` while the mode is `newest` (absent means `all`, so the files of existing worlds are unchanged); `cli._play_serve` carries it through `ready()`, which rewrites `play.json` at every start, and into `PlayOptions.saves`; `alife play --saves all|newest` overrides it for the session and is kept; a `play.json` with another value is refused with exit 2 before anything is touched. The pacer rewrites `play.json` (read, change, atomic write) when the line changes the mode, so a quit, a crash after the line and a resume all keep it; a directory with no `play.json` (a world driven by `runner.run` in a test) has nothing to keep it in. `serve_play` sets `rd.keep_newest` before the runner starts, so even the starting checkpoint is saved in the mode.
- *Log.* A change appends `{"t": step, "verb": "saves", "status": "applied", "mode", "was"}` to `commands.jsonl` (the player's inputs; a replay writes none). The rule-P cut of `truncate_after` (lines with `t < step`) may drop a line written at the checkpoint step on a resume; the mode itself is in `play.json`, the log is history.
- *Echo.* The header's `play.saves = {"mode", "keep", "adopted"?}` (`streamrec.saves_block`, written only when given like the other optional keys; the pacer always gives it; `keep` is `run.keep_checkpoints`; `adopted: true`, present only then, marks a research run played in place, which refuses a `saves newest` line, see below) and `CLCK.flags` bit 2 (`CLCK_FLAG_SAVES_NEWEST`) while the mode is `newest`. An older client reads only bits 0 and 1 and ignores the header key; an older server sends neither, and the client then keeps the toggle off (it shows "keeps its last saves"). The client treats the clock as the truth, with its own pending request until the next `CLCK` shows it or a second passes (as for the rate). Every `saves` line is answered with a `CLCK`. `PlayHeader.Saves`, `PlayClock.savesNewestOnly`, `SaveModeView`.
- *It never changes a trajectory.* The mode only decides which files stay on disk. `test_play_saves`: a world whose mode is toggled by a seeded script (valid and invalid lines) equals the plain run on the state digest, the metrics rows, the event chunks, the social log, the director log and every save and sidecar it still has, in 2D and 3D, observed and not; `kept` is a subset of the plain run's saves and holds the origin and the last.
- *Interactions checked.* **Rule P and the player channel:** a power sent at a chapter end is applied after the checkpoint of that step and the number of saves kept is not an input of a resume (the newest is), so a world in `newest` mode with a power at the chapter end resumes from the quit save to the uninterrupted digest and the same `director.jsonl`, byte for byte (`test_a_power_at_a_chapter_end_and_a_resume_in_newest_mode`). **The chapter-end save of §34.2:** unchanged, it replaces the previous save in `newest`; the report job reads the sidecar of step `t` inside the checkpoint, the newest at that moment. **`--checkpoint STEP --truncate`:** only the saves that exist can be named, so in `newest` mode none older than the origin. **The launcher:** lists `checkpoints/step_<t>.safetensors`, so it shows fewer saves (nothing else, `PlayWorlds.swift` is not touched). **Houses at forks:** the origin is `start_step`, protected, and the `exact` houses read it. **A research run played in place** (`alife play RUN --adopt`; `RunDir.adopted`: the directory has the `config.pre_play.json` its first adoption wrote, which nothing removes): `_keep_checkpoints` keeps the run's own value so that the first save prunes nothing in `all` mode (and says so only in that mode). Its older checkpoints are the research's (`init-from RUN:STEP`, the houses, the activity analyses), which a click must not delete. So a `saves newest` control line that would change the mode of such a world is refused with a note (`PlayPacer._set_saves`; `saves all`, and a `saves newest` that changes nothing, are taken), the header says `play.saves.adopted: true`, and the window does not offer switching Recording off there (`SaveModeView.offers`, the tooltip says why and how). The explicit way is the flag: when `alife play RUN [--adopt] --saves newest` turns a world to `newest`, stderr says, after every check and before anything is touched, which checkpoints its first save deletes (`cli._newest_note`: "3 checkpoint(s) of the research run (steps 30 to 90) are DELETED at the first save"; every one up to the chosen checkpoint but step 0 and the origin; nothing is said for a world already in `newest`). The rule is the adoption, not the number of saves kept: a research run with the default `keep_checkpoints` of 3 and a single checkpoint is protected too. **The kin-thread sidecars:** a quit save replaces the save at the chapter's start in `newest` mode and takes `kinthreads_<a>.json` with it, so after a quit and a resume the first chapter report, the backlog at open and `world_report verify` of an older chapter refold the social log from the origin (`TailError` fallback of `thread_fold`); the output is identical, the cost grows with the log (an accepted limit, measured by the review at one fallback per resume, and the same for the chapters beyond the last three in `all` mode).

**The size monitor** is the client's: `AlifeCore/Storage.swift` and `AlifeControl/StorageMonitor.swift`, `StorageViews.swift`. No engine cost and no record carries a size.

- *Measured.* `StorageScan.measure(world:)` walks `runs/<world>` with `FileManager.enumerator` and reads attributes only (`totalFileAllocatedSize`, falling back to `fileSize`; no file is opened). **Saves** are everything under `checkpoints/` (a `*.tmp` being written included: it is space on disk), **logs** everything else; `saveCount` counts `step_<t>.safetensors` and `newestSaveBytes` is the size of the highest step. The root is resolved first (a world archived to another volume is a link), and so is a `checkpoints/` that is itself a link; sizes are allocated blocks, so many small log files read larger than their content, and the details say "on disk" and count saves ("4 saves"), not files. A file that appears or disappears during the walk, as a save does (a temporary name, a rename, the pruning of an old save), is counted or not and is never an error. Free space is `volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage`, else `volumeAvailableCapacity`, of the world's volume.
- *When.* On a background task every 5 seconds, and at once when a save ends (`CLCK.saving` falls: the new file is in place and the pruning has happened); the first sample is taken when the header arrives. A new world forgets the old sample, trend and pending measurement (a late answer of the old world is dropped); each request is numbered and an answer older than one already published is dropped too (a slow periodic scan that began before a save ended cannot overwrite the save-end scan), and the growth is told the chapter and the saving state of when the scan was asked for, which is what the directory was in (a scan begun during a save and answered after it is a mid-save total, not a baseline). The loop measures once more when the world stops being live (ended, failed) and then ends, so a finished world is not scanned every 5 seconds; a new header starts a new loop.
- *Growth.* `StorageTrend`: since the world went live (the first sample) and "this chapter (approx.)": a chapter ends with its save, which belongs to the chapter it closes, so the baseline is the first sample taken once that save is done (`CLCK.saving` fell), or the first sample for a world attached mid-chapter; a prune later in the chapter makes it negative ("-1.4 GB").
- *Warning.* `StorageHealth.level(free:, saveBytes:)`: **low** under three saves of room (a typical 700 MB save stands for the newest when there is none), **critical** under 5/4 of a save (a save is written whole before the old one goes). The strip's number turns orange or red, its tooltip and the details say "Low disk space: 1.5 GB free (a save is about 686 MB)" or "Almost no disk space: the next save (about 686 MB) may not fit"; while the dock is collapsed the clock badge over the map says "low disk" or "disk almost full".
- *Where.* The **Storage strip** (`StorageStripView`) sits under the clock strip, in a side dock and in the bottom dock's clock column: one line, `[disk] 2.6 GB` (a button opening the details popover: saves and logs sizes and the number of saves, growth this chapter and this session, the room left, the help text) and a **Recording** switch (a `Toggle`, on = `all`, off = `newest`; the word is on the strip, not only in the help). Its tooltip says what each state keeps and does: "Recording is on: the last 3 saves and the origin are kept. Switching it off keeps only the newest save and the origin, and deletes the older ones at the next save. ..." and, off, "Recording is off: only the newest save and the origin are kept. Older saves are deleted at the next save, not now. ...". There is no second line (it cost the dock an alert row exactly when the player switched); the details popover says the same ("Recording is off: keeping the newest save and the origin.", plus the pending deletion while three or more saves are on disk). When the disk is `low` or `critical` the strip prints the room left beside the size in small type ("2.1 GB 1.5 GB free"), the details add "Switching Recording off keeps only the newest save, about one save of disk instead of three" while the mode is `all`, and the badge says "disk almost full (400 MB free)". The strip's ideal width is at most 252 points in every state, inside the 260 of the narrowest side dock (`theStripFitsTheNarrowestDock`). Switching is not confirmed (the owner asked for an easy switch; the deletion is stated in the tooltip); it is disabled when no world is live, when the server predates the line (no `play.saves`), and, to off, in a research run played in place (`play.saves.adopted`; its tooltip: "Recording stays on: this world is a research run played in place, ... start it with: alife play RUN --saves newest"; the details then do not suggest switching off either). *Stage B3 of §34.11 replaces the switch with the three-way choice, and takes the room left out of the strip (the tooltip and the details keep it); the text above is the first build's.*
- *The dock budget (§34.7).* The strip is 20 points and 6 below it; `DockBudget.storage` = 26 (and no note line), `clockStrip` 126 (the clock strip's bottom padding went from 10 to 4), `inspector` 262 (measured 261): a 700-point dock still has two alert rows beside the open inspector, in either save mode, and three need 760 points (740 before). `theSideDockFitsTheMinimumWindow` measures the strip. **The bottom dock's least height** `DockLayout.minBottomExtent` went from 160 to 192: its header and divider (29) plus the clock column (the clock strip and the Storage strip, 151 in every clock state) is 180, and the tabs column (picker 40 and the list's least 120) 189; at 160 the switch was cut off (`theBottomDocksClockColumnFitsItsLeastHeight`). The window's minimum height 700 leaves a bottom dock up to 340.

**Tests.** Python: `tests/test_play_saves.py` (18: the grammar; the pruning in both modes on a fork with sidecars and play-state files, the origin, the quit save, the way back; the switch deleting nothing and the next save applying it; the header, the clock flag, the log, `play.json` (and a `play.json` that cannot be written, which does not stop the world), the replay; the trajectory equality in four arms; the power at a chapter end and a resume; three chapters with their reports, which are the same in either mode and verify from the files of the world that kept the newest save only; the CLI chain of five sessions, the flag, the refusal of a bad `play.json`), `test_stream_records` (the flag range, `saves_block`, the g3b fixture with the header block and the flag), `test_gui_sync` (the `Saves` keys, the bit-2 accessor, the command lines). Review fixes (storage monitor): `test_play_saves` adds the notes of `--saves newest` at the adoption and on a later session, the refusal of the line in a research run played in place (also one with the play value of `keep_checkpoints`, and the way back to `all`), a play world still taking the line, the check of a short new save, the flush before the prune, and the removal of a killed save's temporary files but not of another `*.tmp` (27 in all); `test_stream_records` the `adopted` key. Swift: `StorageTests` (the measurement on a temporary directory with checkpoints and logs, a link, a missing directory, a churning directory; the formatting; the thresholds; the growth; the mode; the readout), `StorageMonitorTests` (when it measures, the late answer, the stale answer, the scan asked during a save, the switch in a research run played in place, the loop ending with the world, the switch sending its line and following the echo and the timeout, the strip's height and width, the bottom dock's column), `PlayCommandTests`, `PlayRecordsG3bTests`, `DockBudgetTests`.

### 34.11 Light saves: compressed saves, one loader, and the save path (the owner's request of 2026-10-24, row I64)

The owner: "a lightweight option to resume a planet's achieved state for a later run, without having to record large files on disk." A save is 687 MB; 95% is the brains (`W1` `[65536,116,32]` f16 and `W2` `[65536,33,39]` f16 at full capacity). Measured on the full save of `planet_a-4` (the table under *Measured*): zstd level 17 with long-distance matching (`window_log` 27) keeps 0.339 of the bytes (233 MB) in 10.9 s; level 19 keeps 0.264 but takes 26.7 s, past the budget; decompression takes about 0.4 s at every level. The shipped level is 15 (the review of I64, §34.11 *Review fixes*): 0.365 of the bytes (250 MB) in 4.3 s on 18 threads, where level 17 takes 15.5 s on 8 threads and 24.5 s on 4.

**Owner decisions of 2026-10-24** (not to be revisited): (1) lossless **zstd** saves with an exact resume, using the dependency `zstandard` (over the stdlib `lzma`); old uncompressed saves keep loading everywhere; (2) a **one-save mode** (`saves single`): keep only the newest save and drop the origin, after auditing what reads the origin (each such reader degrades with a message, never a crash); (3) **a planet made from an own world links the source save** instead of copying it (`os.link` on the same volume, else a copy), and the launcher makes Resume the obvious way to continue a world. Data safety comes first: at every instant at least one complete, loadable save of the world exists, and a crash or kill at any point leaves a resumable world (the rules under *Data safety*).
Decision (3) is implemented only where the link is exact (stage B2): a planet made from a played world is not yet linked, see *The planet's first save* and *Not in this change*; the owner decided on 2026-10-24 to keep it so: such a planet keeps its own compressed origin (about 250 MB at level 15), and Resume, which makes no copy, is the way to continue a world. The planet_a chain's premise (each "Make planet" copied the 687 MB save) is not what the code did: a planet from a played world was written again from its transformed state, so each continuation was a new full save (now compressed, about 230 MB; B2's reading of the code).

The four stages of the plan: **B1** the format, the one loader and the save path; **B2** the save mode `single`, the origin audit and the planet's link; **B3** the Swift side (the save choice, the shared-save line, the launcher hint); **B4** these docs and the full fast suite.

Stage B1 (the format, the one loader and the save path):

- **Format.** A compressed save is `checkpoints/step_<t>.safetensors.zst`: the zstd frame of the exact safetensors bytes, so decoding it gives the file `mx.load` reads. The frame names its size and carries a checksum; a frame that does not end (truncated), bytes after its end, or a checksum mismatch raise `CheckpointError`, never a hang. Level `runio.ZST_LEVEL` = 17, `ZST_WINDOW_LOG` = 27, `enable_ldm`, `threads=-1`. The dependency is `zstandard` (owner's choice over the stdlib `lzma`).
- **Measured (B1; CPU; the full save of `planet_a-4`, 686,866,344 bytes; `zstandard` 0.25.0 with `from_level(level, size, enable_ldm=True, window_log=27, threads=-1, write_checksum=True, write_content_size=True)`, 18 threads).**

  | level | bytes | ratio | compress (s) | decompress (s) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 9 | 304,374,354 | 0.443 | 1.33 | 0.43 |
  | 12 | 260,863,934 | 0.380 | 1.91 | 0.42 |
  | 15 | 250,352,932 | 0.365 | 4.26 | 0.41 |
  | 17 | 233,032,489 | 0.339 | 10.93 | 0.44 |
  | 19 | 181,663,873 | 0.264 | 26.65 | 0.51 |

  The level was first chosen as 17 (the best ratio whose compression stays within about 15 s on 18 threads); the review (below) found that budget does not hold on a 6-8 core Mac, so the shipped level is `ZST_LEVEL` = 15 (7% more bytes than 17, a background compress on 8 threads takes about 6 s instead of 15 s). Level 19 keeps 0.264 of the bytes but takes 26.7 s. Decompression is about 0.4 s at every level. The check on the real file (B1, a copy in scratch): compression 11.38 s to 233,032,489 bytes at level 17, decoding 0.53 s, and the decoded bytes identical to the plain file.
- **Both names are checkpoints.** `_CKPT_RE` accepts `step_<t>.safetensors` (old saves, unchanged, loaded everywhere) and the `.zst`. `checkpoints()` lists one entry per step (the compressed one when both exist), `checkpoint_at` and `latest_checkpoint` return either, `LATEST` may name either. The `_SAVE_TMP_RE` debris names cover `.safetensors.zst.tmp`.
- **One loader (every reader goes through `runio`).** `load_checkpoint` decodes a `.zst` into a temporary file through `state_file` (removed on exit) and loads that; `checkpoint_metadata` streams only the first pieces of the frame (the header, not the body); `read_state_arrays(path, keys)` reads the named arrays (`analysis/phylo._alive_uids`, `alive` and `uid`); `state_file_is_complete` decodes a `.zst` whole (checksum included) before the one-save mode may delete older saves. The readers that take a path (`cli.py` `--init-from FILE`, the analyses through `checkpoint_at`, `signals`, `resim`, `stream`, `houses`, `w0`, `bench`) need no change: they take the path `runio` returns. The GUI reads names only: `StorageScan.saveStep(of:)` (the storage monitor, `Storage.swift`) and `PlayCatalogScanner.checkpointSteps` (the launcher's listing, `PlayWorlds.swift`) accept both names and ignore `*.tmp`.
- **The save path (`RunDir.compress`, set by `serve_play` from `PlayOptions.compress`, default `True`; a runtime setting like `keep_newest`, so it is in neither the config hash nor `play.json`; there is no CLI flag).** `save_checkpoint` first calls `wait_saves()`, which waits for the save in flight and raises its error once. The synchronous part writes the plain save as an ordinary atomic state file (`write_state_file`: `step_<t>.safetensors.tmp`, fsync, `os.replace`), checks it whole (`state_file_is_complete`; a failure removes it and keeps `LATEST`), and moves `LATEST` onto it. So the world has a complete, loadable save from the moment the plain file is named, including the origin of a new world. A non-daemon worker thread then compresses that plain file to `.zst.tmp` (`compress_file`, fsynced), checks the frame whole **before the name moves** (`state_file_is_complete` on the temporary file, the frame decoded and its checksum verified), and only then `os.replace`s it to `.zst`, fsyncs it (`_full_sync`), moves `LATEST` over it, deletes the plain copy and prunes (`_prune_saves`). A check that fails removes the `.zst.tmp`, leaves `LATEST` on the plain save and keeps every older save (a note on stderr). Only the calling thread removes debris (`_remove_debris`, before a save starts), so a worker never deletes a file of a save the play loop is still writing. The play loop calls `wait_saves()` in `before_checkpoint` (its error is raised after the sidecars and play-state files of the checkpoint are written, so a resume at the next checkpoint stays exact; the raise stops the play) and in `serve_play`'s `finally`. The wait is not ended by a signal: a `KeyboardInterrupt` during it is recorded and raised once the save is whole or failed, so a quit save is not lost. The ladder's SIGINT comes at +30 s, so the budget for the quit save is **30 s** (the SIGTERM rung is at +40 s); a full planet's compress takes about 4 s at level 15 on 18 threads, 6 s on 8.
- **Crash safety.** `LATEST` moves only over a complete save, and a `.zst` is named only after its whole-file check has passed. At every instant the world has a complete save that `LATEST` names or a newer one on disk: before a compressed save, `LATEST` is the previous one; from the plain save's name on, the plain save (complete by its own check); from the `.zst`'s name on, the `.zst`. The older saves are deleted only after `LATEST` names the new one. A kill between a save's name and its `LATEST` leaves a complete newer save that `LATEST` does not name: `RunDir.adopt_newest_save()` moves `LATEST` to it when a play resumes (`cli._play_resume`, before the check for `--truncate`), so a resume takes it without `--truncate`, and the GUI, which never passes `--truncate`, does the same. The `*.tmp` debris is removed by the next save. A worker's failure (an error or a kill of the thread) leaves the same state: `LATEST` on the plain save or the previous `.zst`, and the error surfaces in the play loop at its next save or at the end.
- **Resuming a compressed save needs temporary space** the size of the plain save: `load_checkpoint` and `read_state_arrays` decode the frame into a temporary file under `$TMPDIR` (about 687 MB for the full planet), removed on exit. A full system volume therefore blocks the resume of an intact world (the error says so), and a kill during the decode leaves that file in `$TMPDIR` (not in the world). Streaming the decode into `mx.load` would remove the need; it is not done.
- **It never changes a trajectory.** Tests (`tests/test_runio_light.py`, 11; the review's cases, `tests/test_light_saves_review.py`): the round trip is bit-identical (the decoded bytes equal the plain file, so every tensor and the metadata); the header of a torn `.zst` reads; the loaded state digest equals the plain one; corrupt, truncated, trailing and non-zstd files raise `CheckpointError` (and `state_file_is_complete` is False); both names are checkpoints; a run resumed from its step-10 save with `compress` on equals the plain run (the state digest of every save, the metrics rows except the wall-clock columns); the newest-only compressed mode keeps the newest save and the origin; a save killed in its thread leaves `LATEST` on the previous save, which loads.
- **Data safety (every stage; what a reviewer checks).** (1) A save is written whole under a temporary name (`.tmp`), fsynced, and only then `os.replace`d to its name; a save is checked whole before `LATEST` names it: a plain save by `state_file_is_complete`, a compressed one by its frame decoded to the end (checksum included) before its name moves. `LATEST` moves over a save only after that check, so a save that fails it is never named. (2) An older save is deleted only after `LATEST` names the new one, and in `newest` or `single` only after the new save is on the drive (`_full_sync`). (3) The newest save is never deleted, in any mode. The origin is kept in `all` and `newest`; `single` drops it at the next save after the new one is whole. (4) Debris (a save's `*.tmp`) is removed by the calling thread before a save starts; the worker removes only the temporary file of its own compress, on its own failure, and never a plain save it is compressing. A temporary file is unlinked before it is written, so a stale hard link to another save is never written through. A failed write unlinks its partial file. (5) A kill or an error at any point leaves a complete save that loads and that `LATEST` names or a newer one on disk, which `adopt_newest_save` makes the newest (`tests/test_runio_light.py`, `tests/test_play_single.py`, `tests/test_light_saves_review.py`). (6) A linked origin is a second name for the source's bytes: a prune of either world removes only its own name, and the bytes stay while the other name exists (a hard link). If the source has been pruned, the origin is saved from the state in memory.
- **The save mode `single` (stage B2).** `saves single` (grammar: `play.parse_play_command`, `streamrec.SAVE_MODES`,
  `tests/data/play_command_lines.txt`; the Swift `SaveMode.single`) keeps only the newest save: step 0 and the origin
  go too. `CLCK.flags` bit 3 (`CLCK_FLAG_SAVES_SINGLE`) comes with bit 2, so a client that knows only bit 2 shows
  `newest`; `play.json` has `saves: "single"`, `--saves single` is accepted, the header says `play.saves.mode` `single`.
  `RunDir.set_save_mode(mode)` sets `keep_newest` and `drop_origin`; `_prune_saves(keep, origin=)` keeps the newest
  `keep` steps, `LATEST`, and with `origin` step 0 and the origin, and deletes every other save file of either name
  (a step may hold a plain and a compressed file), then the sidecars and play-state files of the steps gone. The
  single prune runs only over a save that is whole (`state_file_is_complete`, decoded) and `LATEST` names: a failure
  or kill before that leaves every older save in place (`tests/test_play_single.py`, 4 places x plain/compressed).
  A switch deletes nothing; the next save applies it, as `newest` does. `alife play --saves single` on a world with
  checkpoints says what its first save deletes (`cli._newest_note`).
- **Readers of an origin, audited (B2).** A fork's origin is `meta.start_step`. Each reader and its behaviour when
  the origin (or any step) is not kept: `phylo.load_tree` (a fork's founders are read from the origin save: a
  `ValueError` that says `saves single`; origin 0 needs no save); `phylo`'s `check_checkpoint` at the end (already
  `None`); `houses.source_problem` (a fork is refused as before; a step not kept is refused with the kept steps,
  `HouseError`); `cli._select_checkpoint` (`CheckpointError` with the kept steps: `--checkpoint`, `--truncate`, the
  fork's `RUN:STEP`); `analysis/resim` (`FileNotFoundError` when no save at or before the step); `signals.load_state`,
  and so `labels`, `social` and `observer` (`FileNotFoundError` with the kept steps; an observer's `resumed` flag is
  false, so it starts from a fresh sidecar, a note only); `w0.load_tracer_source` (`FileNotFoundError`); the kin-thread
  table of a report and the director's blocked set (both already `None` or empty when the save is missing); the
  report job, the clock and the chapter boundaries (`start_step` is metadata only); `evaluation.lineage_stats` through
  `phylo` (a fork of a single world is refused by `phylo`, as above; the evaluation's own arms are research runs,
  not played worlds). The play's resume takes the newest save, so it does not read the origin.
- **The planet's first save links its source save (B2, `alife play --init-from RUN:STEP`).** `cli._prepare_fork`
  (`link_origin=True`, `_play_world` only) sets `RunDir.origin_link = (step, source save)`. The first save of the
  planet (`save_checkpoint`, the same call as a plain start) then makes the state file a **link**: `os.link` to the
  source save under a temporary name and `os.replace` (`RunDir._link_state`), or a copy when the link fails (another
  volume); when the source save is gone (pruned while its world still plays), the origin is saved from the state in memory, as any save is (review F6). A compressed source stays compressed. Nothing is written into the source: every writer of a save goes
  through a temporary name and `os.replace`, so the source's later prune only removes its own name (the planet keeps
  the bytes). **Exactness is the condition:** the link is taken only when the fork's state is the source's byte for
  byte (`state_digest` before and after the fork's transformation), the fork has no weather spin-up
  (`--weather-spinup`), and the source's stored `config_hash` equals the fork's. The fork's transformation resets the
  diagnostics (`diag`), the ledger (`ledger_cum`) and `total0` and resets the environment levers to inert, so a
  planet made from a world that has run is **not** linked: its origin is written, compressed, as before (about
  230 MB, not 687 MB). A link would make the planet continue the source's ledger, a change of the planet's energy
  accounting that §33 does not make; this is an owner decision (see the handover of stage B2), not taken here.
  `tests/test_play_single.py` (the link: same inode and two links, the copy fallback, the source's prune, and a
  planet from step 0 linked and from step 5 not).
- **The save choice and the strip (stage B3, the Swift side).** The Storage strip's choice is one segmented control of
  three: `All` (`saves all`: the last saves and the origin), `Start` (`saves newest`: the newest save and the origin) and
  `Newest` (`saves single`: the newest save, the origin goes too). Choosing `Start` or `Newest` asks first (a confirmation dialog: "Keep newest + start?", the older saves named as deleted and not restorable); `All` is not asked. The full names ("All saves", "Newest + start", "Newest
  only") are in the details popover and the tooltip. The segments are short on purpose: the strip is one line of 26 points
  in the narrowest dock, 260 points beside the size (`theStripFitsTheNarrowestDock`), and the full names need 242 points at
  the mini control size before the size is printed (`Start` and `Newest` take 147). The room left is no longer printed beside
  the size (it does not fit with the choice): the number still turns orange or red, and the tooltip and the details give the
  room. The control sends `saves all|newest|single` only when the choice differs from the mode in force and the world offers
  it (`StorageStripView.command(choosing:current:header:)`); it shows the mode the world echoes (`SaveModeView.current`, bit 3
  for `single`); the whole control is disabled when the world does not take the line or is a research run played in place
  (only `All` is offered there, `SaveModeView.offers`). `StorageReadout.pruningPending` counts from two saves in `single`.
- **Counting (B3, review).** `StorageScan.measure` counts `step_<t>.safetensors.zst` as a save (a `*.tmp` is not one); `saveCount` is the number of steps with a save, so a step held in both forms for a moment during a compressed save is one save; the bytes of a `*.tmp` under `checkpoints/` are `savingBytes`, counted on the disk and shown in the details as "a save is being written". It stats each
  save once by its device and inode, so a file linked twice inside one world is counted once. A save linked from another
  file (a planet's origin linked to its source's save, the exact case of B2) is on disk once, but both worlds count it:
  `StorageSample.sharedSaveCount` (a link count above 1) gives the details one line: "1 save is linked from another world: on
  disk once, counted in both."
- **The launcher hint (B3).** With the Make planet form's source a played world (it has a `play.json`), the form shows
  "To continue this world, use Resume. Make planet starts a new branch from one of its saves." under the source picker, and
  Resume stays the first box. The hint does not say that the planet shares the save on disk: the planet's link is taken only
  when exact (B2), so a planet from a played world does not share its save (the owner's decision above).
- **Review fixes (the adversarial review of stage B4, saves/review.md; commit 'light saves: review fixes').** Held and fixed: the first save of a world had no loadable save while its origin compressed (now the plain save is named first); a SIGINT during the quit wait lost the quit save (the wait goes on); a compressed save that failed its check moved LATEST (now it never does); the compress did not reach the drive before the older saves went (_full_sync before LATEST); truncate_after deleted only one form of a later step (every file of a later step goes); a stale hard-linked .tmp was written through (unlinked first); a planet whose source save was pruned failed its first save (the origin is then saved from memory); a failed plain write left a partial file (unlinked); a save error skipped the checkpoint's storm and kin-thread files (they are written, then the play stops); the level (now 15, the 30 s budget above); the analysis scripts (evaluation, resim, houses) print an error and exit 2 instead of a traceback, and resim names saves single when no save is kept. Held and not fixed, an owner decision: the planet link is not taken for a planet made from a played world (the fork's transformation, above); the decision of 2026-10-24 (3) is met only for a planet from a world that has not run (the step-0 case). The planet's link is not claimed beyond that. Also held and documented: the resume's temporary space (above). The four claims the review found wrong are restated in the bullets above (the level, the 30 s budget, LATEST moves only over a complete save, a kill at any point leaves a resumable world).
- **Not in this change (B4 state).** (a) `compress` is a runtime setting: it is not in `play.json` and there is no `--no-compress` flag; a played world saves compressed wherever `serve_play` runs. (b) A planet made from a played world is not linked (the fork's transformation, above): its origin is written, compressed, about 250 MB. The owner accepted this on 2026-10-24 over the two ways to link it: the fork keeping the source's accounting (a change of the planet's energy accounting, DESIGN §33), or the transformation stored with the origin and applied on load (a larger file). (c) Nothing here is run in the app or on the GPU: the save, resume and mode paths are CPU tests and the measurements above; the quit path is measured for the save only (about 11 s), not for a quit of the window, and not on the external drive. (d) The launcher's Resume is hinted, not reworked: the hint is the B3 text.


## 36. The World viewer v2 (legibility; the globe overview is PRs A1 and B; B as built is 36.10)

The v2 of the World window changes what the owner sees at the planet, region and organism levels, in three PRs (A0 legibility, A1
orientation and input on the flat map, B the globe). **PR A0** is client only: no engine, stream or config change (no config key,
`POST_V01_KEYS` untouched, no golden). Sections 36.2 to 36.4 and 36.8 (the globe, the morph, the globe's flight, the whole test list) arrive with PR B; **36.5 (the pose, the one-world patch, the input, the flights, the minimap and the other orientation aids, and the height colour) is written by PR A1**; 36.1, 36.6 and 36.7 are as built in A0, and 36.9 holds what each PR's review found and left.

### 36.1 The diagnosis (measured) and the fixes F1 to F8

Method: a recorded play stream of the first planet (`g3a/macday/play20k/run1.json.mid.bin`: the 64k3d world forked at 450,000,
`L` = 320, height 80, 44,162 alive, 20,742 bonds, weather 160 x 160, territory 32 x 32) is fed through `PlayController`, the
production `Renderer` draws it offscreen at 2280 x 1800 px (a 1140 x 900 pt free rectangle at 2x) and the pixels are measured
(`DiagProbe`, skipped without `ALIFE_V2_STREAM`). Luminance is Y' = 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B of the 8-bit values; contrast is
WCAG on linearised values. The clear colour is (9, 10, 14), Y' 0.040.

What v1 got wrong: **R1** the cold sea (5, 17, 35) sat 1.05:1 from the clear colour and was 0 over half of the rows; **R2** the map
was mixed back to the clear colour at 0.6 (region) and 0.25 (organism); **R3** the territory film (0.25 of the owner's colour over 94%
of the cells) carried no weather and made the home pose brown; **R4** the vorticity tint was additive and tiny; **R5** no organism
had an edge, and at the region level they were drawn at their physical size and overlapped into a carpet (83.6% of the pixels belong to
an organism, 22.5% of the organisms keep half of their disc visible), while at the planet level none were drawn (a step to about 35,000
instances at the planet-to-region edge).

| fix | what A0 does |
|---|---|
| F1 | the map palette has its own luminance range (36.6): cold sea (20, 59, 107), Y' 0.212 |
| F2 | the map's opacity is a continuous function of the camera distance: 1.0 from 0.296 L, 0.9 at 0.15 L, 0.7 at and under 0.08 L (v1: 1.0 / 0.6 / 0.25 by level) |
| F3 | territory is borders (white at 0.55) and a 10% tint; the View menu's Territory has three states (off, borders, tint) and `3` cycles them |
| F4 | signed vorticity (30% amber / indigo) and a 3% hemisphere tint of the sea, fading out under 0.12 L |
| F5 | (the light) belongs to PR B: the flat map is unlit |
| F6 | the coverage-limited size and the outline chosen from the shaded colour (36.7) |
| F7 | View menu Brightness (0.8, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5; persisted as `world.exposure`) multiplies the map's colours (not organisms: there is no light in the flat view) |
| F8 | the depth cue is `0.85 + 0.15 z / height` (v1: 0.62 + 0.38 z / height, which dimmed 58% of the recorded population by over 25%) |

Measured on the recorded frame at 2280 x 1800 (before is the commit before A0, 2bea1a0; the same probe file ran on both):

| pose | frame Y' mean | under Y' 0.10 | map-only Y' mean | sea vs clear, WCAG p50 | organism pixels | organisms keeping half their disc |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| planet home | 0.191 -> 0.326 | 3.6% -> 12.7% (outlines) | 0.191 -> 0.298 | 1.05 -> 1.85 | none drawn -> 30.1% | n/a -> 81.1% (48.7% at physical size) |
| region at the storm (0.339 L) | 0.481 -> 0.356 | 3.4% -> 4.0% (outlines) | 0.155 -> 0.325 | 1.04 -> 1.95 | 83.6% -> 23.3% | 22.5% -> 89.7% |
| region, wider (0.35 L) | 0.472 -> 0.357 | 3.8% -> 4.2% | 0.154 -> 0.323 | 1.04 -> 1.95 | 83.1% -> 24.8% | 23.0% -> 88.8% |
| region at 0.15 L | 0.489 -> 0.452 | 0.2% -> 0.5% | 0.206 -> 0.431 | 1.22 -> 2.98 | 80.4% -> 16.7% | 44.0% -> 94.4% |
| organism fly-to (0.08 L) | 0.246 -> 0.375 | 41.9% -> 0.1% | 0.088 -> 0.314 | 1.05 -> 2.00 | 41.0% -> 33.2% | 77.5% -> 88.7% |
| organism close (0.04 L) | 0.233 -> 0.356 | 51.0% -> 0.0% | 0.085 -> 0.298 | 1.05 -> 2.02 | 36.6% -> 29.5% | 81.8% -> 86.4% |

The frame mean at the region poses falls because the bright carpet of balls is gone; the map under it more than doubles. The
share of organisms that keep half their disc is the acceptance metric (at least 80% at the region and organism poses, measured by
the occlusion raster `OcclusionRaster` with the drawn radii of the rule; the GPU's covered pixels agree with the raster within 4
points). The edge contrast of the kin colours with their outline (palette slots on the recorded rows, unoccluded and isolated discs,
the pixel on the ring against the one inside it): p1 3.6 to 3.9 at the region poses and 3.95 at the planet pose, 0.4% to 0.5% of the
discs under 3:1 (a neighbour's or the organism's own nose at the ring), none at the organism poses. The organism-against-map contrast
(the 1.3 table of the spec) is lower than v1's (mean 5.2 -> 3.2 at the region): the organisms are smaller and the map brighter; the
legibility guarantee is the outline, not the palette (36.7).

### 36.5 The view's pose, the one-world patch, the input and the flights (PR A1)

**The pose.** `WorldPose` (AlifeCore; the spec calls it `WorldView`, which is the SwiftUI view of the window) is the state of the view: the centre `(x, y)` in
`[0, L)` (the equator is `y = 0`, where the weather is; `ybar = wrapDelta(y)` is the signed readout; the wrap in `y` is at `L/2`), the height `z`, the `heading` (the map
turned about the view axis, 0 = north up), the `tilt` from straight down and the `distance`. `Camera` is derived from it (`camera(size:height:)`: yaw `pi/2 + heading`,
pitch `-pi/2 + tilt`; a 2D world is `faceDown`, seen from below with y down); the renderer, the projector, the picker and the size policy still take a `Camera`, and
`WorldModel.camera` is computed. `WorldModel.editPose` applies `WorldPose.clamp` after every edit; `edit(_:)` (a `Camera` closure) remains for the glide's callers and the tests.

**One world per view, whatever the heading.** The map is no longer a quad of 5 x 5 worlds: at most one world is ever drawn, so no storm is drawn twice. The picture may reach
`WorldPose.reach` = 0.49 L from its centre along x and along y (`footprint(aspect:size:height:)`: the floor points the four corners of the view see, which bound them because the
map from the view to the floor is projective; nil when a corner ray misses the floor, the horizon). The farthest distance is closed form: with half extents `(d + z) tan(fov/2)
(a |cos h| + |sin h|, a |sin h| + |cos h|)` for a window of aspect `a` and heading `h`, `maxDistance = 0.49 L / (tan(fov/2) max(...)) - z`, never under 4 (the Home view is at
this distance: the whole width of one world, 0.83 L at aspect 1.27, so in a wide window the height shows 0.77 of the world). A turn of the heading shrinks it. *(A1 as first built eased
the tilt back with `limitTilt` until the footprint fitted, 52 to 57 degrees at 0.12 L; the camera controls below replace that by the eye's limit and the haze: the tilt is the player's, to edge-on.)* v1's tiled-quad reach (`Camera.keepFloorInReach`, `tiledReach`, `farthestFloorDistance`,
`edgeDepression`) and `Camera.tiledScene` are gone; the clip planes hold `Camera.patchScene` (radius `(L sqrt 2 + 0.5 H) 1.05` about the target since the camera controls: the map is drawn until the haze has taken it). The planet level
begins at a visible half extent of 0.45 L (`WorldLevels.planetHalfExtent`; the Home view is 0.49 L): it stays the level of the zoomed-out map until PR B's globe replaces it by the morph.

**The patch and its copies across the wrap** (`SeamCopies`; `mapVertex`; `WorldU.patch`; `WorldU` is 160 bytes since the camera controls). The patch is `L` wide about the camera in x (3 `L` with the haze, below) (the texture repeats, so the wrap in x is seamless for any
centre) and `L` tall in y over the cell `y` in `[kL - L/2, kL + L/2]` the centre is in (`k = rint(y / L)`). Its two neighbours across the wrap, `k - 1` and `k + 1`, are copies drawn (three
instances; those not wanted collapse) only when the picture reaches within `0.1 L` of the edge (`SeamCopies.plan`; all three while the horizon is in view), with alpha
`1 - smoothstep(0.1, 0.3, s)` (`s` = 0 on the flat map, so 1; the morph is PR B's). **One seam rule for every layer**: a layer of a copy draws at that copy's image of the point (the minimum image about the
view's centre, which lies in the cell of exactly one planned copy, `SeamCopies.copy(containing:)`) and with that copy's alpha: the organisms, the bonds, the storm rings and tracks and the picker already
used the minimum image, so on the flat map they follow the rule unchanged. A renderer with no plan (`WorldDraw.copies` nil: the direct renderer tests) draws all three.

**Grab and zoom, exact on the plane.** The plane is the one through the centre (height `z`). `offset(at:aspect:)` is where the ray of a pointer meets it, relative to the centre, which does not depend on where the centre is: so
`grab(anchor:at:)` (the left drag; `WorldModel.beginGrab` at the press, `grab(to:)` at each move) puts the point under the pointer at the press back under it for any pointer, heading and tilt (tests: within 0.5 px over 400
random poses, across both seams), `pan(dx:dy:)` (the trackpad and the middle button) is a grab of the centre carried by the displacement, and `zoom(by:at:)` changes the distance (clamped) and grabs the point that was under
the pointer back (0.5 px). A pointer off the plane (the horizon) zooms about the centre. Option-drag and right drag turn the heading (0.008 rad a point) and the tilt (`turn`). A drag or a pan cancels a follow and a flight; a
zoom stops a flight and goes on with a follow, at the user's distance (v1 kept the flight's place).

**The scroll law** (`ScrollLaw`, decision D8). A trackpad's two-finger scroll (`hasPreciseScrollingDeltas`) **pans**, its momentum included (the system's own momentum events are the glide); View > "Scroll zooms"
(`WorldDisplay.scrollZooms`, default off, persisted) restores v1's scroll-is-zoom. The mouse wheel zooms about the pointer, 0.1 per line; with the switch on the trackpad zooms at 0.006 per point (v1: 0.01). **Momentum never zooms**
(an event with a momentum phase is ignored for zoom), an event zooms by at most `e^1.5` and **a gesture cannot cross the range**: the summed `|ln factor|` from `began` to `ended` (for an unphased wheel, the events with no pause of a quarter of a second between them: a wheel spun for three seconds is one gesture and a factor of 4 in all, not 4 a second)
is at most `ln 4` (below the per-event cap, so one absurd event is a factor of 4). v1 read the whole range, `ln(0.8 L / 4)`, as 420 points of summed delta at 0.01: one hard flick with its tail. **Unverified on hardware**: the owner's
trackpad is the test of the feel. A pinch zooms about the pointer as in v1 and is not capped (it is direct manipulation).

**Flights** (`FlightPath`; spec 3.6). Every fly-to that is not a follow (the Cast, the Chronicle, the alerts, a pool, a double click, Home) is the arc of van Wijk and Nuij: zoom out, pan, zoom in, at an even speed in the
metric of zooming and panning (`(d ln w/ds)^2 + rho^4 ((du/ds)/w)^2 = rho^2` with `rho = sqrt 2`, pinned by a test), the centre going the short way round the torus, the duration `clamp(S / 1.2, 0.45, 1.8)` s (a pure zoom is
exponential in time, `clamp(0.35 |ln(d1/d0)|, 0.2, 1)`), the end pose exact; reduce motion (`NSWorkspace`) is a straight 0.25 s ease. Only the flight to Home turns the view (north up, straight down). A followed target keeps the
critically damped glide (`CameraGlide`): a path that is planned again every frame is not a path. **A double click on an empty point or a territory cell dives** there, to the region distance unless the camera is closer.

**Home and the keys.** `h` and `r` (`WorldAction.home`), the View menu's "Home view (H)" and the toolbar's Home button fly to `WorldPose.home`: the flat overview, north up, straight down, at the equator, facing `populatedX`
(the circular mean of the alive rows' `x`; the first frame of a world nobody has touched turns the Home view that way once, `homeAwaitsFrame`); a resize of the window refits the distance while the camera is at Home. `n` eases the
heading to 0 in 0.3 s (`northUp`; a drag stops it). `i` toggles `WorldDisplay.minimap` (persisted; the minimap is the second stage's, below). `r` no longer snaps. The View menu's "Agent points" is always listed (it was a
function of the level, which is a function of the continuous distance: no camera-driven value is a field of `ViewMenuInputs`, §36.9; `MenuStabilityTests` zooms across the levels, grabs, scrolls, turns, flies Home and checks
that the menu is not evaluated again).

**Tests.** AlifeCoreTests: `WorldPoseTests` (the camera and its inverse, the readouts, the farthest view at every aspect and heading, the tilt limit, the clamps, grab, pan and zoom exact to 0.5 px at random poses, turning, Home, the
circular mean), `SeamCopiesTests` (the plan, the fade, the coverage of every pixel's floor point by the patch and the copies over 300 random views, the rule), `FlightPathTests`, `WorldScrollTests`, `WorldKeysTests`, `WorldLevelsTests`,
`PatchCameraTests`. AlifeControlTests: `WorldModelTests` and `WorldInteractionTests` re-based on the pose (the grab through the model, the scroll streams, the flights, the follow and the dive), `WorldInputTests` (hosted: the
routing, a left drag grabs, a trackpad scroll with phases and momentum pans, the wheel zooms about the pointer, `h n i r` with the focus elsewhere), `MenuStabilityTests`, `WorldRenderingTests` (`WorldU` 128 bytes, the `patch` field, the
vertex shader's patch), and **`GPUPatchTests` (opt-in, through the hosted `WorldView`: after I61 every draw test of A1 takes the renderer from the view that owns it)**: no pixel of the picture is the clear colour at the farthest
distance at eight poses across both seams and at every heading, nor tilted as far as allowed; each pixel is the map at the point the model says is under it (a checkerboard of rain, six poses, 600 pixels compared); a stripe of rain across the wrap in y and across `x = 0` is one unbroken band;
an organism past the wrap is where the projector puts it. A mutation of the copies (none drawn) fails three of them.

**Camera controls: the tilt to edge-on, the haze, the standard views (A1 camera follow-up; the owner's play of 2026-10-24).** The owner: spatial controls should be evident in the 3D view, with a tool for another angle and standard angles on a toggle; and "Option-drag is neat, but limited by the fact that the maximum angle is pretty limited" (the footprint's limit). Built, in this order of the coordinator's answer:

*Pitch convention.* `tilt` is measured from straight down: 0 is the Top view, 45 degrees the Oblique one, 70 the Low one, 90 (`WorldPose.maxTilt`, was 85) edge-on, the view axis along the floor (camera pitch `tilt - pi/2`; at 90 the eye is at the height of the point looked at). The heading is read as a compass bearing: `bearingDegrees` = `-heading` mod 360 (north up looks north, 0; turned a quarter towards the west it looks west, 270), shown as "Tilt 45 deg . heading 270 deg" (`WorldReadout.viewText`, with the degree sign and a middle dot).

*No clamp of the tilt; the eye is held over the clear box instead.* `WorldPose.clamp` no longer calls `limitTilt` (removed): the tilt is clamped to `[0, pi/2]` and the distance to `WorldPose.maxDistance(..., tilt:)`: the A1 straight-down limit (the height `z` of the point looked at counts by `cos tilt`, so edge-on it does not) and the eye's horizontal offset from the point looked at, `d sin(tilt)`, at most `WorldFog.eyeReach` = 0.45 L, so the eye is over the clear box (0.05 L inside its edge at the least favourable heading) and neither the near edge of the patch nor the floor under the eye is ever in the haze. The two limits meet without a step (the second is none at tilt 0; a test steps the tilt by degrees over three aspects and five headings). At 320: 144 units edge-on, 153 at 70 degrees, 203 at 45. Tilting does not forget the zoom: `WorldModel.distanceWish` is the distance the player had while the limit holds the view nearer, and any edit that leaves the distance alone (a pan, the tilt relaxing, a window refit excepted) gives it back as far as the new tilt allows; a zoom, a flight and Home clear it. So tilting to the horizon and back leaves the zoom where it was (test).

*The haze* (`WorldFog`; `mapFragment`, `skyFragment`; `WorldU.fog`, `WorldU.fogShape`). **It is a function of where the floor point is in the world, not of the eye**: its Chebyshev distance `C` from the point looked at (unwrapped; the fragment carries the floor point in world units). Nothing up to `0.5 L`, then `1 - exp(-((C - 0.5 L) / 0.2 L)^2)`: 22% at 0.6 L, 63% at 0.7 L, 98% at 0.9 L, 99.8% at L. Exponential in the square of the excess (`WorldFog.amount`), not in the distance from the eye: the Top view reaches 0.49 L from the point looked at at its farthest, so any fog that starts nearer shows in the Top view; and a fog tied to the eye is strongest where the eye is far from what it looks at, which is where the near edge of the patch would show. In the world's frame the clear box is the one world everything is drawn in (every organism, bond and storm is at its minimum image about the point looked at, none beyond `L/2` of it; beyond it the map is the same map again, which the haze hides). **The mesh is wider than the haze needs**: with the haze the map's quad is `1.5 L` either side of the point looked at in x (3 L wide; the texture repeats, so it is seamless; `WorldFog.meshHalfX`, `fogShape.z`) and, with the copies across the wrap, `1.5 L` in y at the farthest and `L` at the nearest (the centre is in its cell): the haze is 99.8% there, so **no edge of the mesh is visible at any tilt or heading**; the far plane is behind everything the haze has not taken (`patchScene`). Without a fog (a 2D world, a 3D one with no map and no territory, and the minimap, `fog.w = 0`) the mesh is `L` wide as in A1. **The colour**: `WorldFog.hazeColour` (0.071, 0.229, 0.332: between the sea and the clear colour, a dusk of the same water) scaled by the Brightness (clamped) and mixed to the clear colour by the map's opacity as the ground is (`WorldFog.colour`), so the Brightness setting moves the horizon with the sea. **The sky** is a full-screen pass drawn first (`skyPipeline`, at the far plane): the haze at and below the horizon, falling away above it as `exp(-elevation / 0.22)` towards the clear colour, so the fogged floor and the sky are one colour at the horizon. A world with a map and no tilt shows none of it (every ray hits the floor inside the clear box); a world with no map has the clear colour for its haze (`worldUniforms`). The measure: with a uniform map and the equator lines off (`WorldDraw.equatorLines`; a line is a step), the largest step between neighbouring rows of any column after a median of five is **6 of 255 over 216 views** (tilts 0, 15 ... 90, eight headings, three centres, one on the wrap in y, at the farthest distance each tilt allows); with the haze off (`WorldDraw.fog`) the same detector finds the edge of the world, a step over 20, at 60, 80 and 90 degrees (`GPUCameraTests`).

*Picking and reading at oblique and grazing angles.* Organisms are picked by their projection, which is right at any tilt (tests at Oblique and Low: every isolated organism in view is picked at its own place). **The floor is not read beyond `WorldFog.readReach` = 0.65 L of the point looked at** (the haze is 43% there): `WorldProjector.world(at:)`, `WorldPicker.floorPoint` (a territory cell), the pointer readout ("floor 270 E 28 N"), the place for a power, a double click's dive and `WorldPose.point(at:)` / `grab` return nothing for a pointer in the haze or above the horizon, as they did for the horizon in A1; a drag that took hold in the sky takes hold of nothing (and stops no follow), and one in the haze does not move the map (a point of the screen toward the horizon is a world away: an exact grab there would throw the map). The plane a grab takes hold of is the floor from `gripTilt` = 80 degrees (`WorldPose.gripZ`; below it the plane through the point looked at, as in A1: at edge-on that plane is the eye's own and no ray meets it); `pan` (a trackpad, the middle button) moves along the floor by the displacement at the distance of the point looked at from that tilt, sideways for `dx` and along the heading for `dy`. **The minimap's footprint is clipped to the clear box** (`WorldPose.clippedOffset(at:aspect:planeZ:limit:)`: a border ray that misses the floor or meets it beyond the box goes along its own horizontal line to where it leaves the box about the centre), so it is never more than one box across and `pieces(of:)` shows it whole (a trapezoid or a triangle at the Low and Side views); the readout line, the scale bar and the compass are as before (the scale bar is true at the point looked at only; its label says so from a tilt of 0.3 radians: "on the floor at the centre"); a storm's ring on the floor is an ellipse flattened by the view (`WorldProjector.flatten`, never under 0.12).

*The seam at grazing angles.* `SeamCopies.plan` is unchanged: all three copies while the horizon is in view (the footprint is nil), else those the footprint reaches within 0.1 L of the edge; the footprint's four corner rays still bound the picture. The test (`SeamCopiesTests`) now asserts that every floor point the haze has not taken (fog under 98%) is in a cell of the plan and within the mesh, over 300 random views to edge-on; and `GPUCameraTests` renders rain in bands of rows across the wrap in y at 45, 70 and 85 degrees facing both ways and compares the pixel classes (rain or sea) with the model's floor point, where a pixel covers a fraction of a cell.

*The controls.* A column down the right edge above the minimap (`WorldHUD`, built from the bottom up and keeping what fits, in this order: the zoom buttons, the compass, the 3D button, the strip of views, the readout over it, the tilt handle from 48 to 96 points (the strip, which is words, before the handle: a bottom dock leaves 430 points under a 120-point minimap, and the strip is there); below 150 points of height nothing; a 2D world only the zoom buttons). From the top: the **readout** "Tilt 45 deg . heading 270 deg" (a plate), the **strip** Top | Oblique | Low | Side (the view whose angle the tilt is at is lit), the **compass** (moved from the top right, where the clock badge of a collapsed dock is again at the corner), the **3D button** ("3D" while the view is straight down, "2D" while it is angled: from the Top view to the angle last used, Oblique at first and never steeper than Low, and back, keeping the heading, eased), the **tilt handle** (a vertical track, straight down at the top and edge-on at the bottom, ticks at the Oblique and Low angles, a thumb: a press goes to the pointer at once, holding the thumb where it was grabbed if the press was on it; a drag follows it) and **+ / -**. The compass is **a dial**: a drag turns the heading by the angle the pointer turns about its centre (`Compass.angle(of:around:)`; the needle follows the pointer exactly at the Top view), a click is north up, a double click Home (a drag is neither). The needle is north's projection on the screen (`atan2(sin h, cos h cos tilt)`) going over smoothly to the heading alone from 60 to 85 degrees (`Compass.needleAngle`): edge-on the exact projection swings sideways whatever the heading and is the noise of a zero over a zero at 90, while a view facing north must show north up. A pointer within 6 points of the dial's centre has no angle (`Compass.dialAngle`): a press there takes its reference from the first sample outside, and samples inside move nothing. The plate of the readout takes the press (`.readout`, no action): a click on it is not a click on the map. Press targets `.toggle3D`, `.tilt`, `.preset(_)` join the rest (`HUDTarget` is `Hashable`); no `NSView` lies over the map (the hosted routing test finds the Metal view at the centre of every control). `WorldModel.hudPress(_:at:)` takes the point (the dial and the handle need it).

*The standard views* (`ViewPreset`, `ViewEase`): **Top** (tilt 0, north up), **Oblique** (45), **Low** (70: the altitude layers stand out, the horizon is in the picture), **Side** (90, edge-on from the floor's mid-height `H/2`, at the distance at which the layer from 0 to `H` fills 0.8 of the picture's height at the point looked at, `H / (2 tan(fov/2)) / 0.8`, held to the eye's limit: 107 for `H` = 80 at 320, so the whole layer of life is in view at a glance). Keys **`t o l s`** (none clashes with the table: `WorldKeys` had `space . c 1 2 3 f [ ] r h n i esc g p a k return`; a capital is the same key; arrow keys are not used, they are the Cast list's), the strip, and View > View angle (the four, each with its key, and "Tilt on or off (3D button)": static items, disabled in a 2D world, and no camera value is an input of the menu: `MenuStabilityTests`). Each is an ease of the tilt, the heading (the short way round), the height of the point looked at and the distance (in its logarithm) over 0.5 s (0.25 under reduced motion), smooth; Top turns north up and the others keep the heading; the stored height `z` is 0 (the floor) for every view and unchanged while an organism is followed (the view then is of the organism at its height; a follow goes on); **the point looked at is lifted toward the middle of the height from 70 degrees to edge-on** (`WorldPose.lift`, a smoothstep of the tilt times `max(H/2 - z, 0)`, kept in step by `clamp`, none for a followed organism or lineage, a 2D world or a world with no height), so that the eye is at the middle of the height at edge-on however the tilt was reached (the handle, an Option drag, a flight from Side: with the eye on the floor the lower half was a flat slab and the life a line) and the floor is back when the tilt is relaxed; the scale bar reads at the lifted point; the distance is the wish held by the limit of the angle it ends at, and **the wish is given back at the end of the ease** (`ViewEase.endWish`: Top after Low, and the 3D button twice, go back out); the Side view has a distance of its own, so the one before it is kept (`WorldModel.sideReturn`) and is the wish of the next view or 3D press from Side, unless the player zoomed since. The 3D button goes back to the angle last used but never steeper than Low (edge-on is the Side button's and the handle's), and to the floor at Top unless an organism is followed. Any other input ends an ease where it is (`n` and a compass click too). A press that takes hold of nothing (the sky or the haze of a tilted view) moves nothing and stops no follow. **Height guides:** from 80 degrees in a world with a height, in the engine's colours, faint dashed rows mark the floor, the middle and the ceiling (0, H/2, H) at the depth of the point looked at (`WorldModel.heightGuides`; at least two in the picture; the height colour has its legend). The frame of the world (View > Frame) is faded by the haze like the floor (`worldBoxFragment`: the edge point's raw Chebyshev distance from the point looked at, as alpha), so its far edges are not a thin bright rectangle across the haze; the edges within the clear box remain, as the frame is a toggle. A storm's pick is the ellipse the ring is drawn as. 

*Tests.* AlifeCoreTests: `WorldCameraTests` (the presets and their rules, the ease: 30 frames, monotone, short way round, exact end, the fog's numbers at 0.6 ... 1.0 L, the haze colour and the sky, the projector's reading of the floor, the ring's flattening, the dial's angle), `WorldPoseTests` (the eye limit over aspects, headings and degrees: monotone and without a step; the camera well defined at every tilt including edge-on; the bearing), `WorldHUDTests` (the column, what fits in order of priority, the handle's mapping, the targets), `WorldInsetTests` (the clipped footprint), `SeamCopiesTests`, `WorldKeysTests`. AlifeControlTests, **through the hosted `WorldView`** (`WorldCameraControlsTests`; `HostedWorld`): each key reaches its pose in 30 frames from every other view; Side at the distance its layer needs; a followed organism keeps its height; any input ends an ease; the strip, the 3D button, the handle and the compass dial pressed with events sent through the window (the Metal view hears every control); the dial at three tilts; the tilt reaches edge-on and the zoom comes back; picking at Oblique and Low; the floor unread in the haze and the sky; a grab in the sky or the haze takes hold of nothing and stops no follow; a pan at edge-on; the review's cases (`WorldCameraReviewTests`, and in `WorldCameraControlsTests` the eye at the middle of the height at edge-on by the handle and an Option drag, a flight from Side, the zoom given back after Low, 3D and Side, `n` and a compass click during an ease, the dial's dead zone, the readout plate as a press target); the footprint clipped at every tilt; the copies at the wrap at grazing angles; `MenuStabilityTests` (no camera control rebuilds the View menu) and `WorldHUDModelTests` (a 2D world has none of it). GPU (`GPUCameraTests`, opt-in, hosted): no hard edge at any tilt and heading and no black pixel, the detector's control without the haze, the horizon is the haze and the sky above it falls to the clear colour, the Top view is as it was, the Brightness scales the haze, the seam, and (with `ALIFE_V2_STREAM`) the renders of the planet at the four views in both colours; `GPUPatchTests`' tilt test now asserts that the tilt stays and the horizon is the haze. A mutation, the haze off, fails the first and passes the control; the frame test (pixel differences, frame on against off, along the frame's own projected edges, no median) fails with the unfogged frame (115 to 133 levels) and passes with the fade; the edge-on test checks that the floor, not the clear colour, is below the horizon.

*Deviations and limits.* (1) The fog is a function of the floor point's Chebyshev distance from the point looked at, not "exponential with distance along the floor from the eye": the eye's distance cannot be clear at the Top view's corners and complete at the near edge (above). (2) The tilt is not clamped; the distance is (the eye over the clear box): a tilted view cannot be zoomed out to Home's distance (edge-on: 0.45 L). (3) Beyond 0.5 L from the point looked at the map is the world's map again, but organisms, bonds and storm marks are at their minimum image, so they stop at 0.5 L where the fog is still 0: the floor beyond that box is not in the haze only (at the farthest distance, 18% of a 1.6 aspect picture at 45 degrees, 25% at 60 and 19% at 70 is floor beyond the box, and 6%, 18% and 15% is more than half fogged); on an uneven planet a drawn edge of the populated box may show there. Not changed; a fog that starts nearer for tilted views, or organism copies across the wrap in the haze zone, would. (7) Pool rings are circles (not flattened) and so is their pick. (4) The globe of PR B is later: the same controls will tilt and turn around the planet, and `maxDistance`, `WorldFog` and the clip are the flat map's. (5) Keys: `t o l s`; no key for the 3D button. (6) **Unverified on hardware: the feel** of the handle's drag, the dial, the ease and the haze on the owner's display; the renders are of the hosted renderer on the recorded planet (`scratchpad/viewer2cam/render`).

**Where am I (A1, stage 2; the spec's 4 and 5.3).** All of it is drawn over the Metal view and takes no mouse: the minimap by the Metal pass, the rest by a `Canvas` (`WorldHUDView`, `allowsHitTesting(false)`), so no `NSView` and no hit-testing SwiftUI view lies over the map
(`everyPointOfTheMapFindsTheMetalView` and the overlay tests pass as they were). The rectangles are `WorldHUD` (pure); `WorldModel.pressTarget(at:)` says what a press lands on (`.map`, `.minimap`, `.home`, `.compass`, `.zoomIn`, `.zoomOut`),
`WorldMTKView.mouseDown` keeps it for the whole gesture: **a press that began on the map never becomes a control's gesture, and the reverse** (an Option press is always the map's). The minimap is the lesser of 220 pt and 0.28 of the shorter side of the free rectangle, at the bottom
right with a 12 pt margin; hidden when off (`i`, View > Minimap), when the world has no weather map, or when that side would be under 96 pt (`WorldHUD.minimapMinSide`). It is **north up, east to the right**: `u = x / L`, `v = 1/2 - ybar / L`, the equator through the middle, the wrap in y (`L/2`) along the top and bottom edges (magenta, dashed),
the equator gold (`WorldInset`). The renderer draws the map's fragment shader over a quad in a viewport and scissor of the drawable (`insetVertex`; full opacity and hemisphere tint, no equator lines), then the organisms as 1.5 pt points, pale and 16% opaque (`insetPointVertex`: a crowd is a brighter haze; the average of
40,000 colours is mud, so they are not coloured), last and over everything. The overlay adds the **footprint**: the border of the picture projected onto the floor (`footprint(of:aspect:)`, 16 samples a side through `WorldPose.offset(at:aspect:planeZ: 0)`), unwrapped about the centre and drawn as the pieces a torus needs (`pieces(of:)`: one, or two across a seam, or four at a corner), in yellow with the outside dimmed by 35%; a cross at the
centre of the picture; the storms as dots in the two hemispheres' colours (the selected one ringed), the selected organism; "Northern hemisphere", "Southern hemisphere", "W", "E" (shorter below 170 pt); the readout of the place under the pointer over the box, else the view's. **A click flies there keeping the distance and the heading, a drag moves the centre live** (the pointer held inside the box; it cancels a follow and a flight), **a double click dives to the region distance, the house glyph is Home,
the wheel and a pinch over it zoom the map about its centre** (the pointer is off the map's surface).
