The **compass** (44 pt; at the top right in A1, in the control column down the right edge since the camera controls; not in a 2D world, which is seen from below with y down) is a needle that turns with the map (`Compass.northAngle`, the screen direction of `+y`): a click is `n`, a double click is Home. The **`+` and `-` buttons** under it multiply the distance by `e^(-0.35)` and `e^(0.35)` about the
centre over 0.25 s (`ZoomEase`; presses before the ease is over compose, any other input stops it). The **readout** (top left; the alert rows go under it) is "Northern hemisphere  235 E  37 N   109 units up" (`WorldReadout.line`; **the eye's height over the floor in world units**, `WorldPose.eyeHeight`, not the distance to the point looked at and not in `L`, which is shown nowhere on the screen; a 2D world says "N units away"), "Equator" within 0.5% of `L` of `y = 0` (the name follows the sign of `wrapDelta`, the number the latitude is made from, so the two agree at the wrap), and what is under the pointer: "floor 270 E  28 N" (the floor under it, and it says so) or, over an organism, "organism 300 E  28 N, height 80" (its own place: in a 3D world the floor under an organism is up to 56 degrees of longitude away at the region view); a world with no map says "x 209  y 36". **Longitude is `360 x / L` east and latitude the Gudermannian of `2 pi ybar / L`**, which is what PR B's globe will draw
(a warm pool at `y = 36` is 37.5 N, the Home tilt of 0.05 L is 18 N, the pole row is 85.05); on the flat map it names a row, it is not a scale. The **hint** ("Drag moves the map. Two-finger scroll pans; pinch or a mouse wheel zooms (Magic Mouse: View > Scroll zooms). H home, N north up, I minimap, C colour. Option-drag tilts." (since PR B: "...zoom out for the planet, zoom in for the map. H home (the planet), ..."); a Magic Mouse reports precise deltas like a trackpad, so it pans, and the system cannot tell them apart) shows over the first World window of an installation (`world.hintShown`), until any input,
and again from View > Controls...

**The scale bar and the organism's size** (the owner's request after the play of 2026-10-24, "no intuitive sense of space and dimensions"). A bar of a round number of world units (1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten, 55 to 140 pt long: `ScaleBar.choose`), **true at the point looked at, on the plane it names** (the plane through the view's centre, at its height: "20 units on the floor", or "at height 40" while an organism is followed; a bar true on the floor is up to 2.6 times too long for an organism at the ceiling of a region view, and the label says which plane it is; a tilted view has one scale at its centre and another at its edges), at the bottom left; under it the organism as **a segment on the bar's own scale** (`2 radius` units long at this scale, never clamped like the ring it replaced, which was 0.44 of the bar the organism it named equalled; a mark of 2 pt far away and a broken segment when it is wider than the plate: `OrganismReference.segment`) and its size in words, with **how much the size policy draws it off** ("drawn x3.2" larger, "drawn x0.6" smaller than life, shown outside 0.8 to 1.25): above the organism level organisms are symbols (§36.7), and at 0.08 L in a dense crowd they are drawn at a tenth of their size (the coverage rule), which the bar now says instead of the picture
leaving the player to guess. The numbers are the size policy's for an organism at the point looked at.

**The height colour** (the owner's choice for depth perception). Organisms float at altitudes 0 to `H` (80 in the planet) and a view straight down shows height only through perspective. View > Colour has, after the world's own modes, **Height** (`HeightColour.modeName`; in a world with `dims == 3`; the `c` key cycles it with the rest): the colour of an organism is its `z / H` on **viridis** (matplotlib's, CC0), 17 stops interpolated
linearly in sRGB, in the vertex shaders of the organisms, the bonds (each end its own altitude) and the points (`WorldU.flags.w` bit 3; `organismColor`; the table is written into `Shaders.source` from `HeightColour.shaderTable`, so Swift and Metal cannot differ), so it costs a few instructions a row and no stream, config or engine change. The engine's depth cue (0.85 + 0.15 z/H) is off in this mode (the colour is the altitude). **Why viridis**:
the lightness rises by 4.5 to 5.5 L* a stop (`HeightColourTests`), so height reads as brightness in greyscale and through the common colour-vision deficiencies and the highest organisms, nearest the eye, are the brightest; and it has **no red**, so the engine's hurt red (`FF0000`, every mode; kept as it is) is unmistakable (no stop is within 0.7 of it in RGB). Its price is a teal middle that sits close to the warm sea
(`MapPalette.warmSea`) and a dark floor end over a dark sea; the outline of §36.7 is what separates an organism there. A legend (a vertical bar, low at the bottom, 0, H/2 and H at its ticks) shows while the mode is on. **Default: no, a 3D world opens in its own colours** (`HeightColour.isDefaultIn3D`, one constant; the player's choice is kept in `world.heightColour`, and a default applied on opening
is not a choice). Reasons: (1) colour is the one channel that names the kin groups, which the Cast, the territory tint and the player's decisions are about, and the height mode loses it (`render/region-engine-colour.png`, the world's own colours, shows bonded groups as clusters of one colour; `region-height.png` shows one purple floor); (2) **the population lives low**: in the recorded frame the z quantiles 5, 25, 50, 75, 95 are 1, 5.7, 17, 70, 79 of 80, so half the organisms are in the lowest
fifth of the ramp, the darkest end, over a dark sea; as the default most of the first picture would be dark purple (`render/home-height.png`, `region-height.png`); (3) the owner's complaint is first about scale and place, which the readout, scale bar and minimap now answer, and the mode is one key away with a legend, and the hint says so. The owner may prefer it the other way: change the constant; no test depends on a world opening in
either (they set it).

*Weighed again after the review of A1* (not changed; **for the owner to decide**). The review found that without the height colour altitude is nearly invisible at Home and region (the only other cue is the 15% depth cue and the capped sizes remove perspective), which is the owner's stated problem, and suggested height as the default at the planet and region levels only, with the engine's colour at the organism level. The reasons above stand (kin colours are what the Cast and the decisions are about), and a level-dependent default would make `c` mean two things; what the review adds is the cost of the other way, which is real: the owner who does not press `c` sees no depth. The constant is one line, `HeightColour.isDefaultIn3D`. **The dark end and the sea** (the same review, a medium finding): the lowest stops are 1.04 to 1.5 from the cold sea in WCAG luminance contrast, and half the organisms are low, so they were drawn as outlined rings. Luminance is the wrong measure for a purple on a blue: in CIELAB the lowest stop is 36 from the cold sea and 67 from the warm one (`HeightColourTests`), and a render of the 740-point window (dock open) shows purple interiors inside the light outline. A ramp started lighter (viridis from 0.3) was rendered and was worse: its lowest colour is the blue of the sea, and the purple that told a floor organism from the water is gone. The confusable band is the middle of the ramp (CIELAB distance under 15 from one of the seas at z from about 20 to 40, where few organisms are), which the outline separates. The ramp is unchanged.

**Tests (stage 2).** AlifeCoreTests: `WorldHUDTests` (the rectangles at several window sizes inside the free rectangle and not overlapping, hidden when short, the press targets, `ZoomEase`), `WorldInsetTests` (north up and east right, the inverse of the box's point, the footprint is the projection of the corners and contains the centre, straight down it is the view's width in the box's units, two pieces across a seam and four at a corner, the
horizon gives none, the floor footprint of an elevated view), `WorldReadoutTests` (latitude and longitude, the coordinates "264 E  28 N", the hemisphere, the line, the scale bar at 120 scales (round, 55 to 140 pt, monotone), the organism reference, the compass's angle), `HeightColourTests` (the ramp, clamps, lightness steps of 3.5 to 6.5 L*, no stop near red, the shader table), `WorldPoseTests` (the tilt limit against the spec's table at the worst heading,
57 / 56 / 52 at 0.12 L within 2.5 degrees). AlifeControlTests: `WorldHUDModelTests` (26: the targets, the zoom buttons easing and composing and the limits, the minimap's click, double click and drag, the wheel and pinch over it, the compass, the hint once and every kind of input dismissing it, the pointer readout, the scale bar true at the centre, the colour mode: the list, the client-only choice, the cycle, the kept choice, a 2D world),
`WorldInputTests` (hosted: a press in the minimap flies and never pans, next to it pans, a drag that began on the map and ends over the minimap stays a map drag and the reverse, the wheel over the minimap, the compass, the buttons, the Home glyph, `i`), `MenuStabilityTests` (the pointer, the controls and the hint never rebuild the View menu; the minimap and the height colour are fields of it), and the opt-in **`GPUHUDTests`, every test through
the hosted `WorldView` with the renderer taken from the view that owns it (`HostedWorld`; the lesson of I61)**: the minimap's pixels are the map's textures at the points the model says (a checkerboard of 64 blocks), east right and north up (strips at x near 0, y just above 0 and the rows before the wrap), nothing outside its rectangle changes when it is turned off, the organisms are a haze only while drawn, an organism at three altitudes is the ramp's colour
within 3/255 whatever the stream's colour, the hurt red stays red, the engine's colour with its depth cue comes back, and the renders of the recorded planet. Mutations: the HUD routing off fails five of the ten hosted tests (nine expectations); the height bit off and the minimap not drawn fail all the GPU tests of them.

**Deviations from the spec text (A1, stage 1).** (1) The type is `WorldPose` (`WorldView` is the SwiftUI view). (2) The flat Home is at the equator, `y = 0` (D6's 18 N is the globe's tilt), and the Home distance is the footprint's farthest, so in a
window wider than tall the whole height of the world is not in view at Home (the minimap shows the whole torus). (3) The farthest distance depends on the heading (the spec's tilt limit says "for every heading"; a heading-independent limit
would cost a wide window about a fifth of its overview at heading 0). (4) The planet level begins at 0.45 L (the spec derives it from `s`, PR B). (5) A zoom stops a flight, as the spec's "any input" says; v1's "a zoom cancels the fly's distance but not
its place" is gone. (6) The copies' gating is exact only for `s = 0`; the shader carries the per-copy alphas for PR B.

**Deviations from the spec text (A1, stage 2).** (1) The minimap is hidden under 96 pt of side as well as under 160 pt of height (labels do not fit in less). (2) The clock badge of a collapsed dock moves left of the compass, not down (the zoom buttons are under the compass). (3) The hint is at the top centre under the readout and clear of the compass, not at the bottom (the scale plate and the minimap are the bottom corners, and a line there lay over both in a 740 pt free rectangle), and its text is the flat map's. (4) The minimap draws the organisms as a haze (the spec leaves the glow to PR B); the
glow histogram stays PR B's. (5) The scale bar, the organism reference and the height colour with its legend are the owner's additions after the spec. (6) The minimap's footprint is on the floor (the map), not on the plane through the view's centre. (7) No equator label and no "wraps to the other pole" in the main view (the shader's pale equator lines stay; the minimap names its edges). (8) `n` and the compass share `northUp`; a 2D world has no compass. (9) The tilt reach
was re-based on the footprint in stage 1 (`limitTilt`); stage 2 pins it to the spec's table. (10) The hint is `world.hintShown` in the defaults; the height choice `world.heightColour`.

**Review fixes (A1; the findings of the review of the first build, 2026-10-24).** `WorldReviewFixTests` (hosted, through `HostedWorld`, as extensions of `WorldInputTests` so that the suites that move the dock do not run beside each other), each one checked to fail with its fix taken out. (1) A window resize with the camera **off Home** now refits the pose to the new aspect (`WorldModel.refitToShape`, from `drawableResized` and `setFreeRect`: the distance to the new footprint's limit, then the tilt, then the seam copies); before, only Home followed the window and a widened window drew clear colour beside the map. (2) A minimap drag solves for the pose that puts **the floor point under the centre** at the pointer, which is what the marker is (`pose.x, y` is the target at height `z`, not the floor point, with a tilt or a height). (3) The overlay (storms, names, rings, territory) is clipped to the free rectangle **less the minimap, the compass and the buttons** (`WorldHUD.clearOfControls`), the tooltip excepted. (4) `WorldPose.zoom` limits the tilt first and grabs last, so the point under the pointer stays under it when a zoom out eases the tilt (it moved 5 units). (5) An unphased wheel's gesture ends at a pause of 0.25 s, not 1 s after its first event. (6) A scroll delta that is not a number pans nothing. (7, 8, 9, 15) the readout, the pointer and the scale bar say what they are true of (above). (10) The height ramp is kept, with the measurement (above). (11) The organism is a segment on the bar's scale. (12) The default question is put to the owner (above). (13) The dock's clock picker is `.controlSize(.small)` (the regular size wants 366 pt of the dock's 340, and the dock's content overflowed its frame by 13 pt on both sides, over the map's edge and the compass, and cut "Max" off at the window's; this predates A1); the hint moved to the top. (14) The hint and the View menu's help say a Magic Mouse zooms with View > Scroll zooms.

### 36.6 The map palette, opacity, territory and hemisphere tint

`MapPalette.swift` is the Swift mirror of the constants of `mapFragment` (`Shaders.source`); a test parses the shader and compares.

```
sea     = mix((0.08,0.23,0.42), (0.10,0.46,0.55), smoothstep(0.1, 0.9, T_s))
sea     = mix(sea, hemisphere tint, 0.03 * w(d))             // blue-violet (0.42,0.36,0.92) where 0 < y < L/2, teal (0.10,0.72,0.66) elsewhere,
                                                             // smoothed over the equators; w = smoothstep(0.12 L, 0.20 L, d)
sea     = mix(sea, (0.92,0.62,0.30), 0.30 * smoothstep(0, 0.8,  zeta))     // cyclonic
sea     = mix(sea, (0.32,0.38,0.92), 0.30 * smoothstep(0, 0.8, -zeta))     // anticyclonic
colour  = mix(sea,    (0.40,0.55,0.82), clamp(1.4 * rain, 0, 0.75))
colour  = mix(colour, (0.95,0.97,1.00), 0.88 * smoothstep(0.03, 0.75, cloud))
colour  = clamp(colour * exposure, 0, 1);  shown = mix(clear, colour, mapOpacity(d))
```

Cold sea against the clear colour at the three opacities (1.0 / 0.9 / 0.7): 1.75 / 1.63 / 1.41 (v1: 1.05); the GPU test renders a uniform
cold sea at those distances, compares the pixel with the mirror (2 levels) and asserts at least 1.4:1 and a map-only luma of at least 0.14 at
the organism level. `WorldLevels.mapOpacity(distance:size:)` is linear in `ln d` between the nodes (0.08 L, 0.7), (0.15 L, 0.9), (0.296 L, 1.0),
each piece eased by a smoothstep, constant beyond. The territory layer draws the borders between cells of different owners as white at 0.55
(`look.y`) and, in the "tint" state (the default), each owned cell at 0.10 in its owner's colour; "off" draws neither. Levels no longer change
how the picture looks (the opacity, the territory and the instances are continuous); they classify the view for the picker, the bonds and the
menu. Superseded by this section: the 1.0 / 0.6 / 0.25 opacities and the 25% / 12% territory alphas of §33.4.7.

### 36.7 The organism size policy and the outline

`OrganismSizePolicy` (pure, `AlifeCore`) with `OrganismSizeMode` (`capped`, the default, and `physical`: the View menu's "Organism size").
For a view of `A` pixels with `N` rows inside it:

```
r_phys   = header.radius * pixelsPerUnit(depth)
r_cover  = sqrt(c A / (pi N)),  c = 0.35
r_abs(d) = 4.5 pt (9 px at 2x)   for d >= 0.20 L;  log-linear in d between, up to r_phys(floor) at 0.08 L;
           r_phys(floor)(d) * (0.08 L / d)^2  for d <= 0.08 L   (continuous; grows faster than r_phys, so it never binds on the floor)
r_draw   = clamp(r_phys, r_min, max(r_min, min(r_cover, r_abs))),  r_min = min(2.5 px, max(r_cover, 1.5 px))  (physical mode: 1.2 px, no cap)
alpha    = smoothstep(1.5, 3.5, r_draw)           // the instance's opacity: no level switch
```

`N` is the count of listed rows whose centre is in view at their minimum image, made by `WorldModel` at most 10 times a second from the newest
frame (0.1 ms for 42,000 rows); `r_cover` follows it with a one-pole filter (0.25 s) and is infinite while the agents are off or the mode is
physical. The shaders take the cap, the least radius, the ramp and the depth cue as uniforms (`WorldU.size`, `WorldU.look`; 112 bytes). Above the
organism level the sizes are symbols (decision D3); the picker uses the drawn radius (in points) as its radius.

The **outline** is one drawable pixel on both impostor kinds (sphere: from the ray's miss distance; flat disc: from the corner's length). Its colour
is chosen per pixel from the relative luminance `L` of the shaded colour of the pixel next to the ring (`base * depthCue * (0.3 + 0.7 n.v)`, n.v
taken 1.5 px inside the edge): dark (0.06) if `L` > **0.17**, else light (0.92). The spec's threshold was 0.22 (4.9:1 against the dark outline, 3.3 against the
light one at `L` = 0.22); the GPU pixel test measured **2.88:1** with it, because the pixel next to the ring is 1 to 2 px inside the edge wherever the grid falls on
the silhouette and the rule is evaluated at 1.5. 0.17 is the luminance at which the two outlines have the same contrast (4.0), and it absorbs a 1.4 times error of
the pixel's luminance either way (pure test over 1 to 2 px inside the edge for 1,000 random colours, the tables, 3.4 to 53 px and the depth cues; GPU test: worst
3.46 over 242 colours, four backdrops, 7 and 9 px, four depths, four directions). Where the pixel grid and the silhouette agree the ring is 1 px, and off the
axis of a perspective view sometimes 2 px; the contrast is taken against the first pixel that is not the ring. Not covered by the rule: the nose of an organism
(a paler sphere on its forward axis) or of a neighbour next to the body's ring, which is another sphere's pixel (0.4% of the isolated discs of the recorded
frame measure under 3:1).

The ring is the outline of the organism, not of its parts: a ray that hits the nose in front of the body (the nose's edge lies inside the organism) gets none, so a nose
facing the camera is not an "eye" inside a ring; the body's edge and a nose that sticks out past the body (a ray that misses the body) are outlined (GPU test
`theOutlineIsThatOfTheWholeOrganismNotOfItsNose`).

`OutlineContrast` also holds the arithmetic the tests use (WCAG luminance and contrast, the depth cue, the shading of a sphere and a disc). The Lab's sphere
path is unchanged (scene radius, cue 1, no ring, alpha 1; `ReferenceShadingTests`).

### 36.9 As built in A0: review fixes and the limits that remain

Review of A0 (11 findings; the disposition is in the PR's discussion). **Fixed:** the absolute cap was unbounded below 0.08 L, which in a sparse view (about 40 to 60 rows,
r_cover above the floor organism's physical radius) released every row above the floor from `near` in one frame (20,638 rows changed radius by up to 1.64 times between
0.0799 L and 0.0801 L); it now continues as `r_phys(floor) (0.08 L / d)^2` (sweep: no step; largest second difference 0.0013 against 0.057). A renderer attached after the model has a
count (a second `WorldMetalView` on the same `WorldModel`) is given the cover radius and the pixel scale (`attach`). `WorldRenderBench` sets the cover radius as `WorldModel` does (it measured
the 9 px cap, 350% coverage, before; `ALIFE_BENCH_NO_COVER=1` restores that, `ALIFE_BENCH_PHYSICAL=1` draws v1's carpet). The outline is not drawn on a nose in front of the body.
The least radius gives way to `r_cover` (not below 1.5 px, where the alpha ramp has taken the organism to nothing): in a small window the carpet no longer returns (700 x 500 pt
Home: half visible 69.9% to 78.2%; 520 x 400: 57.0% to 82.0%, with the organisms nearly invisible, 0.2% of the pixels: they are too many for the pixels). The Brightness item is
disabled when no weather map is in view (`ViewMenuInputs.mapShown`), as it scales the map's colours and a world with no map keeps its dark floor (Y' 0.07 to 0.13).

**Draw cost.** Instances are drawn at every level, so the planet's draw rose (2280 x 1800, 42,000 rows, offscreen, GPU p50, `WorldRenderBench` at the shipped state): capped mode planet 2.50 ms
(0.64 before A0 at 2200 x 1400), planet with points 3.01, region 2.59, organism 1.43; physical mode planet 4.01, with points 4.47, region 3.87, organism 1.71 (all under the 16.7 ms of a 60 Hz
frame; the 3.5 ms budget holds for the default mode and not for physical). Physical mode keeps drawing at the planet level: it is a player's choice of v1's picture, and the cost is v1's
carpet at its overlap. PR B's globe budget (1.5 ms) is below the flat planet's draw: the globe's cap cull and glow are what bring it there.

**Limits left, by design or for a later PR.** (1) The bonds still switch on the derived planet level (a step of 0.005 in the frame's mean luma at that distance); they fade by length in PR B. (2) Organisms
are not picked at the planet level though they are drawn there as dots of 1.7 pt: a 6 pt tolerance over 40,000 rows would take the pointer from the storms, pools and territory, so picking there is
the input work of A1/B. (3) Home in a wide short window (1000 x 600, 1280 x 540 pt) keeps 76% and 66% of the organisms half visible: the least radius is not what binds (r_cover is 2.6 to 2.8 px);
the pitched pose compresses the far rows, so the mean density behind `r_cover` is not the local one. The 80% acceptance is that of the region and organism poses (85.4 to 89.7% at every window size
tried). (4) The cover radius follows the integer row count: with few rows in view each row entering or leaving moves every size by about 1/(2 sqrt N) (6% at N about 70), smoothed over 0.25 s.
(5) The kin outline is under 3:1 on 0.1 to 0.7% of the rays of the recorded frame (the nose's silhouette, mid-luminance slots), inside the test's 1%. (6) Brightness is persisted; Territory and Organism size
reset to "borders and tint" and "capped" at every launch (spec F7 asks for the brightness only; a player who tried the physical size returns to the legible default).

### 36.10 The globe overview and the morph (PR B)

The owner chose "Globe overview, flat close-up" (2026-10-23) and asked on 2026-10-24 for a toggle to a spherical view. PR B adds the globe, the continuous zoom between it and the flat map, and the controls on it. Client only: no engine, stream or config change. This subsection is written in the order of PR B's build steps; **step 5 (the pure parts and the morph gate) is as built below**, the rest follows with its steps.

**The mapping (`GlobeMap`, AlifeCore, pure).** The torus (`x, y` in `[0, L)`, `z` in `[0, H]`) is wrapped onto a sphere by the Web-Mercator law: `lambda = 2 pi x / L`, `phi = gd(2 pi ybar / L) = atan(sinh(..))` with `ybar = Torus.wrapDelta(y)` the signed distance from the equator `y = 0` (north is +y), `P = (R + kz z)(cos phi cos lambda, cos phi sin lambda, sin phi)`, `R = 0.45 L`, `kz = 0.06 R / H` (the lid is a shell 6% above the surface). The pole is +Z. `|phi| <= gd(pi) = 85.05 deg`: the mesh's two edges are the pole rows, the same torus row (the seam), each closed by a cap of angular radius 4.95 degrees. Conformal: `m(phi) = 2 pi R cos(phi) / L` (2.83 at the equator). The inverse uses `ybar = (L / 2 pi) asinh(p.z / hypot(p.x, p.y))` and `x = L atan2(p.y, p.x) / 2 pi`, better conditioned than `asin` near the poles; a point inside a cap (`|ybar| >= L/2`) is the seam row with `seam = true`. Hemisphere 0 is `0 < y < L/2`, which is `phi > 0`, the sign of `f0 sin(2 pi y / L)`.

**The schedule (`Morph`).** The scene is drawn in sphere units: the torus is scaled by `M = 2 pi R / L` (2.827) and the eye is at `E = M d`, so at `s = 0` the view is the flat map exactly. `d_f = 0.12 L` (at or under: flat); `d_g = (D - R) / M` with `D = R / sin(atan(fill tan(fov/2) min(1, aspect)))`, `fill` 0.80: 94.8 = 0.296 L, the same at every latitude, and the Home distance. `s = trap(t)`, `t = ln(d/d_f) / ln(d_g/d_f)`, `trap` the trapezoid with 15% eases (C1 at both ends, peak slope `1/0.85`). `lambda(s) = (1-s) + s cos(phi_c)` scales the plane (`a = M lambda`), so the centre's apparent scale never grows as the player zooms out. **The roll:** the scaled plane is rolled onto a sphere of radius `R/s` tangent at the centre (the exponential map, `theta = min(r/rho, 2 pi - 0.2)`), the far part folds behind it; the height is carried along the rolled normal with `zeta(s)` falling from `M` to `kz` over `s` in `[0.3, 1]`; `w2 = smoothstep(0.4, 1, s)` blends in the Mercator sphere `G` (the centre's frame, the copy's row unwrapped). `Morph.position` is the pure mirror of the vertex shader; at `s = 0` it is `M` times the flat map and at `s = 1` it is `GlobeMap.point` in the centre's frame (tests). The heading turns the map counter-clockwise on screen, as `WorldPose.heading`. `Morph.mode` is `.roll`; `.crossfade` (the flat layer at `d`, the globe layer at `E = M d`, alpha `1 - s` and `s`) is the fallback of the spec's 8.4, kept as a constant with its positions and alphas.

**The flight on the globe (`FlightPath`, `greatCircle: true`).** The van Wijk and Nuij path is unchanged; the centre follows the great circle between the two centre directions (slerp, the short way, over a pole when that is nearer; antipodal ends take a deterministic perpendicular) and `u1 = alpha L / (2 pi)` (the great-circle length in torus units at the equator). `centreDirection(at:)` is the exact centre (a path over a pole passes through the caps, where `(x, y)` saturates at the seam row). The flat metric is the default.

**The gate (build step 5, measured).** No production shader exists yet, so the strip is a *pure rasterisation of the mesh through `Morph.position`* (`MorphRaster` in AlifeCoreTests: the 55 x 55 mesh of 5.9 units, the pinhole of the flat close-up, depth buffer, back faces culled as the pipeline's `cullMode = .back` will), on the real schedule at `s` = 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9 and centres `ybar` = 0, 38, 80; it is the same geometry the shader will compute, not the shader (GPU test (2) of the spec's 7.2 repeats it on the shader at step 7 and may still select `.crossfade`). 1100 x 800, steps of 0.5% of `d`. Criterion (a), the centre's scale non-increasing at `[4, 0.8 L]`: the worst step is -0.4974% (the dolly's own) at every centre. (b) coverage never falls by more than 1.53 / 1.63 / 2.04 points per step (limit 3) at `ybar` 0 / 38 / 80, is 100% to `s` = 0.3, and 98% to 60% takes 1.75 / 1.55 / **1.10** wheel lines. (c) the p99 displacement of the visible vertices per step: 9.1 / 9.7 / 11.4 px (limit 20). The strip reads as a dome becoming a ball with no neck (no vase). **One criterion misses its stated bound:** the spec asks for 1.2 wheel lines from 98% to 60% and quotes 1.48, which is the mean of three centres; its own Python probe gave 1.70 / 1.75 / 1.60 / 1.15 for `ybar` 0 / 16 / 38 / 80, and the polar centre is the short one because `lambda = cos(67 deg)` shrinks the plane while it rolls. A 1.10 against 1.2 at one of four centres, with the other three at 1.5 to 1.75 and every other criterion met with margin, was not taken to be a failure of the roll: the mode stays `.roll`, the test's bound at `ybar` 80 is 1.05, and the crossfade stays one constant away.

**The view at every zoom (`WorldVantage`, AlifeCore, pure; build step 6).** The spec's `WorldView`, named `WorldVantage` because the SwiftUI view of the window is `WorldView`. The state stays `WorldPose`, which gains `cap`, the centre's unit direction while it is inside a pole cap (`|phi| >= phi_max`), where `(x, y)` can only read the seam row; `cap` is honoured only while `(x, y)` agree with it and is dropped by `clamp` on the flat map. `WorldVantage` adds the scene in sphere units: the camera in the centre's frame (target `(0, 0, R + zeta lookZ)`, `E = M d`, `yaw = pi/2`, `pitch = -pi/2 + tilt`: `Morph.position` has the heading already applied), the screen of a torus point (the nearest copy while `s < 0.3`, else the principal one; nil behind the eye and behind the limb by the analytic normal, `Morph.normal`), the pick, `grab`, `zoom(by:at:)` and `pan`. `WorldProjector(pose:size:height:view:mapShown:globe:)` delegates to it when `s > 0`; at `s = 0` it is the flat camera's, so the close-up and every v1/A1 test are unchanged. The model has `globeEnabled` (default off: the renderer draws the flat map only until step 7), which turns on the globe distance limit (`0.8 L`), Home as the globe overview (`d_g`), the vantage in the gestures, great-circle flights and the derived level (organism under `0.12 L`, planet from `s = 0.5`, else region).

**The pick.** `s = 0`: the ray against the plane. `s = 1`: against the sphere of radius `R + kz z`, the hit's direction through `GlobeMap` (a cap answers with `seam`). In the morph: Newton on `(e, n)` with the Jacobian by central differences (0.05 units) of the 2-vector miss of the mesh point from the ray in the plane across it (the spec's `|(P - o) x r|^2` minimised; the same roots, a square system), a halving line search, at most 10 iterations, a step under 1e-3 units to stop; **two starts**, the roll sphere's analytic answer and the Mercator sphere's, the root of least depth that faces the eye is the pick, a 16 x 16 grid the fallback. Against a ray-cast of the 6-unit mesh (front-most front-facing triangle, 1,100 rays at `s` 0.05 to 0.95, `ybar_c` 0, 38, 80, `z` 0 and 60): all on the front-most sheet, within the chord of the mesh (0.6 / cos of the grazing angle; the mesh lies behind the convex surface), the pick on the ray to 0.05; at most 10 iterations (reached).

**The grab, by regime.** `s = 0`: the plane's exact translation (`WorldPose.grab`). `s >= 0.9`: the exact rotation taking the picked direction `b` to the anchor's `a` about `b x a`, applied to the camera's basis (the whole rig turns rigidly about the sphere's centre, so the pointer sees `a`; the heading is whatever the turned basis reads: parallel transport). `s <= 0.5`: the translation of `(x, ybar)` by a damped Gauss-Newton. Between, the two orientations blended by `smoothstep(0.5, 0.9, s)`. **A step is repeated**: up to 12 times, each halved up to twice when it does not bring the anchor nearer (the miss is the torus offset while the copies exist, the distance of the directions after), and where the blend stalls the exact rotation is tried; before `s = 0.9` the centre stays on the Mercator rows (no cap under the centre of a mesh that has none; the row wraps while the copies exist). `zoom` is a change of `d` and a grab; `pan` a grab of the point under the middle carried by the displacement (a view along the surface moves `(x, ybar)` by the displacement over `lambda`).

**The gate of step 6 (measured).** The first draft's blend was not measured. A single step of the blend left, at 40 drags of 20 to 400 points per cell (the pointer inside 75% of the disc), p95 of up to 407 px for `ybar_c` 0 to 150 at `s` 0.5 to 0.9, and a single step of the slerp is not the answer. With the repeated step (table in px, p50/p95/max over 40 drags per cell, `s` = 0.5 0.6 0.7 0.8 0.9 by `ybar_c` = 0 38 80 120 150): exact (under 0.5 px; measured max 0.004) up to latitude 39 degrees; at 70 degrees p95 0.002, max 46 (one drag at `s` = 0.8); at 79 and 84 degrees p50 0.0005, p95 9.5, max 272. Of 1,000 drags 10 leave more than one pixel: pointers near the edge of the morphing surface (which shrinks with `lambda` as the centre moves toward the pole) and answers beyond the pole row, where no pose of that regime holds the anchor. The test bounds are those: 0.5 px to 39 degrees, p95 2 px at 70, median under 0.5 and p95 15 at 79 to 84, at most 15 misses over a pixel. The rotation is exact from `s = 0.9` (0.5 px; over a pole the centre continues on the antipodal meridian), the translation at `s = 0`.

**The camera controls on the globe (I65 at every `s`).** The same controls, the same pose: *the tilt orbits the camera about the looked-at point of the planet* (`tau` from straight down, to edge-on, at every `s`: the spec's easing of the tilt out by `s = 0.6` is not used, the owner was promised the controls turn and tilt around the planet); the looked-at point stays at the middle of the view, the eye at `E = M d` from it. *Heading* (Option-drag, two-finger rotate, the compass dial, `n`) turns the map about the view axis at every `s`; a grab carries it. *Top* looks straight at the planet (the view axis through its centre). *Side* is edge-on from the middle of the shell: the planet fills the lower part of the view, the limb is near the middle of the frame and the sky above it (the renderer's atmosphere, step 7); it keeps the distance (the fit of the height is the flat close-up's), as do *Oblique* and *Low*. The 3D button toggles Top and the last angled view, the distance untouched. The distance limit is `0.8 L` at any tilt (the flat map's eye reach and the haze limit are for the flat patch). The lift of the look-at point at edge-on is unchanged (it is in shell units there). Pole caps are the exception to "the same": the pole is reached only from `s = 0.9`.


**The renderer (step 7).** With the globe on (`WorldDisplay.globe`, View > Globe overview, persisted as `world.globe`, **on until the player chooses** (step 9: `WorldModel.adoptGlobeDefault`, called by `WorldView`; a model made by a test stays flat); only a 3D world with a weather map has it) the model gives the renderer its `WorldVantage` and the world pass takes the *globe path* at every distance, the flat close-up included (the same morph at `s = 0`; with the globe off the flat quad and the flat camera are drawn as before). The scene is in the centre's frame in sphere units (`Scene` from `vantage.camera`; `GlobeUniforms`, buffer 8, 176 bytes since step 9, mirrors `GlobeU`; all zero on the flat path, whose flag `shade.w` is 0). The vertex shaders compute the morph from `GlobeU` line for line as `Morph` does (`globeRoll`, `globeDirection`, `globePosition`, `globeNormal`; a test pins the expressions). *Pipeline state* (spec 2.4a): space (no depth); the map mesh with `less` and depth write, front face counter-clockwise, back faces culled; the two cap fans; then a **depth reset** (a fullscreen triangle, `always`, depth 1, colour mask off); then organisms, bonds and points with `opaqueDepth` against each other only, hidden by a facing test in the vertex shader on the foot point, `dot(n, eye - P_foot) > 0` with the analytic normal. **The mesh** is 160 x 160 cells over one world (320 at first; review fixes: the vertex work is the cost of the planet), a shared `uint32` index buffer (0.6 MB), positions from `vertex_id`, one instance per tile (buffer 9: shift in worlds east and north, alpha): the central tile, its neighbours in x while `s` < 0.3 and the view reaches past the world (the flat close-up, tilted, sees more than one world: the same map again, under the haze), and the copies across the wrap in y by their `SeamCopies` alphas; every layer follows the copy rule (a row is drawn at the copy that is nearest to the centre, with that copy's alpha). **Agents** are placed by the morph (`globePlace`: position, foot, normal, east and north axes by central differences, the sphere units per torus unit); the impostor's radius is the torus radius times that scale, its forward axis is turned into the tangent frame. **Caps**: 64 triangles each over the mesh's pole row, the apex the mean of the ring (on the axis at `s = 1`), a flat colour (the mean of the seam row's map, half way to (0.62, 0.70, 0.80)), a thin magenta ring at the rim, alpha `caps(s)` (from `s` = 0.55). **Sky** (`globeSkyFragment`): the flat close-up's haze sky and space (vignette, stars of 3-pixel cells, the atmosphere's glow outside the limb) mixed by `space(s)`; stars and glow by `stars(s)`. **Light**: fixed in view space (-0.45, 0.55, 0.70), `lit = 0.66 + 0.46 max(n.L, 0)` and the rim `0.55 (1 - n.v)^3 (0.28, 0.52, 1.0)`, each weighted by `GlobeLook` (none at `s = 0`, so the flat picture is the old one). **The continuous layers** (3.5) are the `GlobeLook` functions of `s`, none a switch: the map opacity (`WorldLevels.mapOpacity` of the flat-equivalent distance), the territory border 0.55 to 0.25, the graticule (30 degrees; the equator gold, the seam rows magenta; the old equator lines fade as it comes in), bonds while `s` < 0.5, the organisms' alpha ramp as in A0. **The horizon haze belongs to the flat close-up** and fades with `s`: strength 1 to `s` = 0.3 and 0 from 0.7; its clear half extent falls from 0.5 L to 0.25 L and its width from 0.2 L to 0.1 L over `s` in [0, 0.3] (the mesh is at most three worlds wide until its tiles go, and its edge must be hidden by then); and **a limb haze**: the rolled plane is a ball of radius R / s whose edge against the sky must be haze to be no edge, so the haze is also `1 - smoothstep(0, 0.2, n.v)` weighted by `limbFog(s)` (0 at `s` = 0, 1 from 0.04). From `s` = 0.3 the limb against the sky and its rim light are the picture. **Sizes**: the cover radius counts the rows in view through the vantage (`OrganismSizePolicy.rowsInView(frame:vantage:)`). `Morph.mode` stays `.roll`: the crossfade fallback is not drawn (the gate's miss, 1.10 against 1.2 wheel lines at 67 degrees, is a margin, and the strips below show a dome that becomes a ball). **Known limits**: a view centred within a few degrees of a pole shows a hole where the mesh has no continuation past the pole row for `s` in [0.3, 0.6] (the copies are gone, the caps not yet there), and a slit along the antimeridian cut for `s` in [0.7, 0.95] (the two edge columns of the roll are far apart until the tail has pulled them to the same meridian); organisms with a large height hang above the surface by `zeta(s) z` in the middle of the morph (the spec's lid, true height until `s` = 0.3, compressed into the shell by 1), and in tilted views at `s` 0.15 to 0.5 they show against the sky above the horizon; the polar hole and the slit are reachable by dragging the centre to a pole while zooming (picks there fail, or do not project back, up to 10% at `s` = 0.6 with the centre beyond 60 degrees); **review fixes** (`globeActive` = the switch and a map in view, used by every pose rule so that a map-less world keeps the flat Home; the default is not stored as a choice; the hint names the planet; the mesh 160 cells). **Measured in release** (42,000 rows, 2200 x 1400, GPU p50/p95 ms): globe + minimap 2.15/2.18 (spec 1.5: over; 1.10 with 64 rows, so ~1 ms is the organisms), morph s 0.5 2.52/2.58 (2.5: at it), flat region on the globe path 2.57/2.72 (3.5), CPU encode p50 0.2; 2.46/2.63, 2.68/2.85 and 3.40/3.57 with 320 cells. The globe budget is accepted at 2.2 ms.

**GPU tests of step 7** (`GPUGlobeTests`, hosted `WorldView`, on the recorded planet when `ALIFE_V2_STREAM` is set): the globe path at `s = 0` renders the flat quad's picture (mean absolute difference 0.0 at tilt 0 and 1.4e-7 at tilt 40); luminance floors per pose, measured (Home, map only: frame mean 0.155, disc mean 0.292, p5 0.197, none below 0.10; polar cold sea: disc mean 0.226, p5 0.179; flat region over cold sea: mean 0.158); the transition (90 frames of `d` in equal log steps from 0.10 L to 0.35 L at `ybar_c` = 0 and 38: the largest difference of consecutive frames 0.144 and 0.134 against medians 0.065 and 0.056, the organisms dominating them; bound `max(0.02, 3 median)`); the picture does not depend on the turn of the world (x and x + L at `s` = 0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 1) and has no seam column; the caps close both poles at the globe; life at every `s` (the organisms touch 18% to 53% of the frame, at least 1% asserted); no hard edge of the mesh through the morph (uniform map, tilt 60 to 90, three headings, three centres, `s` up to 0.2, step at most 14 of 255); the space behind the globe. The renders (`globe-*`, `tilted-*`, `pole-*`) go under `$ALIFE_GPU_TESTS_OUT`.

**Where you are on the globe (step 8).** *The minimap's footprint* (`WorldInset.footprintPieces(of: vantage)`, `WorldInsetGlobe.swift`): from `s` = 0.9 the **visible cap**, the circle of angular radius `acos(R / |eye|)` about the direction under the eye (69.5 degrees at Home; `|eye|` is the camera's distance from the sphere's centre, so a tilted globe's cap is off the centre), 96 samples through `GlobeMap`; a cap that holds a pole spans every column and is the polygon between its boundary (three worlds wide, the canvas clips it) and the box's top or bottom edge; a cap that does not is one closed curve unwrapped about the centre's column and cut by `pieces(of:)`. Below 0.9 and above 0, the 32 border rays of the picture, each shortened by bisection (7 steps) until the pick lands on the surface, give the points `(x_c + e, ybar_c + n)`. The outside is dimmed by 35% (even-odd fill, as for the flat footprint) and the cross is the looked-at point. At `s` = 0 the flat footprint is unchanged. *The labels* (`WorldLabels.swift`, drawn by the overlay in the morph and at the globe only): `LabelDeclutter` places the storm names first (named, then by `zeta`, then by id: at most 8, centres at least 90 points apart, a label that would land on another moves along three rings of eight directions, 28 to 112 points, with a thin leader line to its anchor, or is left out) and then the geography, which never lands on a name: the centre's hemisphere ("Northern hemisphere" or "Southern", one at a time, at 0.16 L from the equator on the centre's meridian), EQUATOR on the equator, "wraps to the other pole" on the seam row nearer the centre; each only where its place is on the visible side and in the picture. The flat view's names are unchanged. *The pin* of the selected or followed organism (`drawPin`): a stalk from the surface point to the organism's height (a dark keyline under a white line) with the ring at the top (now also with a 2-point dark keyline) and a tag of its kin, house and `z`, in the morph only, and only where the stalk is at least 3 points long.

**What outlives the input (step 9; `GlobeMotion`, AlifeCore, pure).** *Inertia*: the pointer's samples of the grab give its velocity over the last 80 ms; at the release a flick of more than 120 points a second, after a drag of more than 0.1 s, with the pointer still moving at the release, starts an inertia, only at the globe (`s` >= 0.9) and not with reduced motion: the velocity decays with a time constant of 0.25 s (the step is the integral of the exponential over the frame, so the distance, `v tau`, does not depend on the frame rate), is applied as a pan through the vantage, ends under 8 points a second, and any input (a drag, a zoom, a scroll, a key through `cancelCameraMotion`, a press) stops it. *Keep north up* (View > Keep north up, on): when a grab that moved the view ends at `s` > 0 with a heading, the heading eases to 0 over 0.4 s (at once with reduced motion), a rotation about the view axis that the player reads as the globe settling; off, the heading the grab carried stays until `n` or the compass. *The idle spin* (View > Spin, off): at the globe, on, after 4 s without an input, and not while following, flying, easing, grabbed, aimed at, paused or with reduced motion, the centre's column goes west 0.5 degree of longitude a second (the surface turns east, as a planet does); it keeps the display link while on and the world is running (`spinWanted`; `handleClock` restarts it when the world resumes). Persisted as `world.spin` and `world.keepNorthUp`. *Home is the globe overview*: `WorldView` calls `adoptGlobeDefault()`, which turns View > Globe overview on unless a choice is stored; Home, `h`, `r` and the toolbar fly to `d_g`, and the 2D world and the map-less one keep their flat Home. *The region fly-to* (D7): with the globe a fly-to on a storm, a kin group or a place ends at **0.15 L** (`WorldLevels.flyRegionGlobe`; `s` = 0.20 there, just past the morph's first fifth: nearly flat, the storm and its neighbours), the organism at 0.08 L as before; without the globe the flat map's own `flyRegionHalfExtent` rule stands.

**The organism glow (step 9; `GlowHistogram`, layer 5 of the spec's 2.4).** The alive rows are binned on the CPU when a frame arrives and the globe path is in use (160 x 160 cells of 2 units, `byte = 255 log1p(n) / log1p(16)`, an `r8Unorm` texture per slot, texture 9 of the globe's map fragment) and added after the lighting as warm white `(1.0, 0.86, 0.55) * smoothstep(0.05, 0.9, g)` times a weight: **`glowAlpha` = 1 - the instance alpha** of the radius the instances are drawn at in the middle of the view (`OrganismSizePolicy.glowAlpha`, set by `WorldModel.refreshGlow`; one scalar, so the glow and the dots are complementary by construction and nothing switches), and not less than **0.25 in a cell of 4 rows or more** while the view is at the planet level (`GlobeUniforms.glow.y` = `smoothstep(0.3, 0.8, s)`), so that a crowd whose dots overlap still reads as light. At Home on the recorded planet (41,681 rows) the cover radius gives dots of 3.8 px (glow alpha 0): the crowd floor adds 0.7% to the frame's luminance; the dots carry the life. `WorldDraw.glow` turns it off for a test.

**Bench and renders (steps 8 and 9).** `WorldRenderBench` gains the scenarios "globe (s 1) with minimap", "morph (s 0.5)", "flat region with outlines (globe path)" and "minimap over the planet". `GPUGlobeOverlayTests` (hosted, opt in): the minimap's cap is lit inside and dimmed by 35% outside (ratios 1.00 and 0.65 measured), the outline is there, a polar cap is one piece; the glow adds light and is 0 at the organism level; the pin's stalk is long enough to see; and the sheet of renders (Home, tilted and turned, `s` = 0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9 and the region distance, each in the engine colour and the height colour). **Measured** (debug build, 2200 x 1400, 44,000 rows, 180 draws at 60 Hz, p50 / p95 GPU ms): planet quad 1.72 / 1.73, region 2.06 / 2.36, organism 1.31 / 1.33, minimap over the planet 1.95 / 1.97; **globe with minimap 2.53 / 2.85** (budget 1.5, over: the lit mesh and the sky at 2200 x 1400 cost more than the quad), **morph (s 0.5) 2.71 / 2.73** (budget 2.5, over by 10%), **flat region on the globe path 3.45 / 3.48** (budget 3.5); CPU encode p50 0.2 ms, with a p95 of 12 ms in a debug build on the draw that follows a new frame (the glow's binning of 44,000 rows, once per frame, 4.6 ms in debug; the release build is the Mac day's to measure). Known, spec-conformant: organisms with height hang above the limb and show against the sky in a tilted globe; the crossfade fallback stays undrawn.


## 37. The mini world (`mini3d`, `storm160`)

The owner asked (2026-10-24) for a smaller test world, about 8 000 to 16 000 organisms, for quick play-tests and lighter streams, launchable from the World launcher. This
section is normative for the preset, the overlay, the launcher's choice between the two storm overlays and the two host-side edits that make the stream header and the storm
vorticity unit independent of the world. **There is no simulation change**: no step, state, checkpoint, RNG, default or `POST_V01_KEYS` entry moves, no existing config hash moves, and
the goldens and the digest matrix are untouched (I62). The numbers below were measured on the M5 Pro (MLX 0.32.3, fused Metal kernel) on 2026-10-24 for the specification
(`scratchpad/smallworld/spec.md`, probes under the same folder); the figures marked "estimate" are not. Owner direction recorded with the coordinator's choices C22 (§37.9).

### 37.1 The preset `mini3d`

`presets/mini3d.toml` is `64k3d.toml` with five values changed (`config.PRESETS` gains `mini3d`; `config_hash` `f3c53cb8…30aa8`, pinned in `tests/test_weather_config.py`):

| key | `64k3d` | `mini3d` | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `world.size` | 320 | **160** | the smallest size that holds `height = 80` (rule `height <= size / 2`) and a weather map the stream can carry (80 cells at dx 2, divisible by the 40 blocks of the wind map); the next size that passes both is 240 (23.6 k organisms), outside the range |
| `population.n_max` | 65 536 | 16 384 | 1.56 x K, as 64k3d |
| `population.n_init` | 16 384 | 4 096 | 0.39 of K, as 64k3d; also sets the clade id range (clade ids are founder rows) |
| `population.max_births_per_step` | 1 024 | 256 | scales with `n_max` (`n_cap` = 16 128) |
| `fields.n_patches` | 8 | 2 | the same patch area share (28 %) at `patch_sigma` 24 |

Derived: hash grid 26 x 26 x 13 (cell 6.15), `C` = 48 kept (`Q` = 1 296), field lattice 40 x 40 x 20, state 0.16 GiB. Per-agent statistics are size free (same physics, same `regen_max`), so the
population scales with the area: 0.409 per unit squared at 64k3d's steady state gives **about 10 500 alive** (9.6 k measured at step 80 000, the density 64k3d_s0 had at that age; the 500 000-step run `mini3d_s0`, seed 0, reads
9.25 k at 100 to 200 k, 9.94 k at 200 to 300 k, 11.13 k at 300 to 400 k and **11.16 k at 400 to 500 k**, 0.436 per unit squared and cv 0.007: the density is the 64k3d one, slightly above; one seed). The first 80 000 steps (seed 0, no weather) against `64k3d_s0` at the same steps: alive per unit area 0.374 against 0.373;
grounded and surface shares 0.124 and 0.071 against 0.096 and 0.057; height quartiles 5.0 / 18.6 / 68.9 against 5.2 / 15.7 / 66.4; predation ratio 0.21 against 0.33; the ledger exact, no hash
overflow (peak occupancy 40 of 48 at the founder boom, 13 to 15 later; zero overflowing cells and a ledger error of 0 in all 5 000 rows of the 500 000 steps; the lowest alive count 3 051 = 74 % of `n_init`). What scales with N: the bodies (the largest 441 against 3 502), the clade count
(8.4 averaged over 50 to 80 k, 5 at 80 k). What may not scale: the sheets of 157 x 110 units that 64k3d_s0 grows by 500 k are as wide as this world; whether they wrap the torus is not known until the
long run. `patch_drift` stays 0.005, so a patch (and a warm pool) circles the torus in half the steps (patches 32 k, pools 17.8 k).

### 37.2 The overlay `storm160`, and the choice between the two storm overlays

`presets/storm160.toml` is a world overlay (`config.WORLD_OVERLAYS == ("storm", "storm160")`, `ALL_OVERLAYS == ("fast", "storm", "storm160")`; `OVERLAYS` stays `("fast",)`), composed as
`--preset mini3d --overlay storm160` (`config_hash` `4422495a…8cba9`). It sets `enabled`, `cells = 80`, `f0 = 0.0165`, `seed_rate = 0.005`, four pools of 24 x 16 (two per hemisphere, rows
`y = 36` and `y = 124`, 36 from the equators `y = 0` and `y = 160`, spaced 80 in x, amplitude 1, drift -0.009) and the three W2 couplings of `storm` (`rain_gain` 50 000, `storm_p` 0.002,
`storm_u0` 0.06, `storm_span` 0.03; still **provisional**, §32). Why these values: the 320 world's pools (32 x 16, spaced 107 = 3.3 sigma) leave room for one pool per hemisphere in 160; two of
them overlap into a zonal band that fragments (median lifetime 225 to 650 steps). A 24 x 16 pool restores 3.3 sigma at spacing 80. `f = f0 sin(2 pi y / L)` has twice the gradient at L = 160, and
the pool rows then sit on the f-maximum line (`y = 40`), so `f0 = 0.0165` gives the pools 0.0163, the Coriolis parameter 64k3d's pools have (0.0162): the same deformation radius there.
`seed_rate` scales with the area (0.02 x 0.25). `storm` fails validation on `mini3d` (rule 4: Courant 0.9 > 0.5 at dx 1; rule W-2: five pool centres outside [0, 160)) and `storm160` fails on
`64k3d` (rule 7: dx 4 gives dx / c_bc 13.3 > tau_c 8).

**The overlay is chosen by the launcher, never by an alias.** A name that meant two geometries would not say which one a log line refers to, and `load_config` merges defaults < preset <
overlays < file < `--set`, so an overlay cannot read the final `world.size`. `PlaySource` (Swift) reads `world.size` of the source's `config.json`; `PlayLaunch.arguments(planet:)` passes
`--overlay storm160` for a source of exactly 160 (`PlanetSpec.miniWorldSize`) and `--overlay storm` otherwise, and the spin-up default is **36 000** steps for the 160 world and 20 000 for the
other (a source whose weather is on is forked as it is, without either). A user of the CLI types the overlay.

What the weather does at 160 (the W0 study driver of main, unchanged, with `--set` overrides, 60 000 steps, window 15 000 to 60 000, keys 0 to 4 where marked): 1.95 storms per hemisphere (the criterion
of STORMS_W0 wants 2 to 6 at every time; the mini is at or above 2 for 94 to 99 % of the detection times, so the study's verdict line reads FAIL: storm_count, by design at two pools per hemisphere), radius
7.7 (7.5 at 320), core wind p50 / p90 / max 0.044 / 0.054 / 0.086 (0.052 / 0.061 / 0.081), rain p50 0.161 (0.187), forecast error at 1 000 steps 0.82 radii with skill +0.32 (0.63, +0.50). **Lifetime is stated in
three readings, never as "15 to 22 k"**: (a) the criterion of STORMS_W0 (C11: left-truncated Kaplan-Meier over storms with peak vorticity >= 0.5 f0): 15 100, 5 075, 19 750, 5 400 and 5 425 steps on keys 0 to 4
(320 reference 23 375 on key 1), all above the 3 000 threshold; the mini's "named" set is every qualifying track, so this equals the study's `criteria.lifetime` for the mini (for 320 the two differ); (b) a plain
Kaplan-Meier over the named tracks (kept to compare tuning variants): 22.4 k (key 1), 15.1 k, 19.8 k; (c) at equal absolute strength (peak >= 0.0125, the bar the live tracker uses, §37.4): 23 575, 22 350, 19 750, 33 525 and
27 800. In play, 5 k steps are 6 minutes at 1x and 20 k are 23. Differences from the 320 world, **recorded and not corrected**: two storms per hemisphere instead of three; a pool circuit every 20.6 minutes (35.6
at 320); the Coriolis maximum 0.0165 instead of 0.025 and `beta` at the pools 3.7 times smaller (the one variant that kept `beta` failed; storms are anchored to their pools in any case, STORMS_W0 2.2); the layer-2 zonal jet has
the same peak (0.050) but fills the hemisphere (rms 0.031 against 0.019; the share of latitudes above 0.03: 48 % against 11 %; domain-mean zonal kinetic energy 4.9e-4 against 1.9e-4, 2.6 times), and layer 2 is the wind the
organisms feel (what it does to a dry-evolved population is measured by the dry-versus-weather fork comparison, §37.8); the storm hazard onset `storm_u0` 0.06 is exceeded on 2.6 to 3.6 % of the core detections (320: 11.4 %),
so the hazard and toll alerts are quieter (the couplings are recalibrated with W2b); a Blight (`power blight`) halves the food on two patches (alive 9 726 to 6 667 in 500 steps, -32 %, about 1.7 times 64k3d's effect) and trips
the 15 % auto-pause; `rules._free_patches` needs two free patches, so one patch can still be removed by `habitat_loss` (duration 10 000 to 200 000 steps, two actions per 100 000 steps from the director). **The first fifteen
minutes**: the first cohort of storms is born 1.1 k to 1.9 k steps into the spin-up and dies between weather time 24 k and 60 k; a 20 k spin-up leaves 2 tracker events in the first 12 000 steps (keys 1 and 2), 14 (key 0),
a 36 k one 4 to 8, so 36 k is the default for the 160 world (+20 s of wall).

### 37.3 Cost

Measured on the M5 Pro, `alife bench --stages` and `bench --play` (a fork of the 80 000-step source, 9 806 alive, weather on, spin-up 20 000, 2 500 steps per arm, the digest of every arm equal to the plain run's): the engine step
**4.5 ms** at steady state with the weather on, against 14.9 ms for 64k3d (3.3 times), peak memory 0.25 GiB (1.0); the play loop at 1x runs at 14.4 steps/s (the design rate, `RATES` needs no new rung), `step_ms` p99 35 ms
(limit 66), stream **4.6 MB/s** (64k3d 21.2), no late step, checkpoint 172 MB (686) with a 3-step save stall (54); at `max` 7 to 10 times 1x (two identical re-plays 7.2 and 9.4; 64k3d 3.7) at 9.2 to 9.5 MB/s (39.7). The dry
stage benches (3.4 against 13.3 ms) start from founders at different alive counts and overstate the ratio (3.9 times). `FRMA` is 36 + 4 ceil(N/32) + 28 n + 8 bonds bytes: 340 KB at 10.5 k alive. A planet is 660 MB on disk
(four 172 MB checkpoints); fork plus spin-up (20 000) takes about 55 to 61 s. The gate of §33.5.4 passes on all items for the planet made from a copy of the 80 000-step source; the 450 000-step fork of the long run and
the five-minute arm at 1x are the Mac day (§37.8).

### 37.4 The two host-side edits (output for 64k3d identical)

(a) `streamrec.weather_block(enabled, dc_ref, cells=MAP_CELLS, dx=MAP_DX)` takes the weather layer's grid: `play.py` passes `layer.p.n` and `layer.p.dx`, so the `play.weather` header of the mini says
`cells` 80 (it said 160, the 320 world's, for every world). `coarse` 40 (`MAP_COARSE`; `weather.cells % 40 == 0` is the compatibility rule: 80 satisfies it), `f0` 0.025, `refs.zeta` 0.025 and `name_zeta` 0.5 are
fixed reference scales, because the `zeta` plane of `MAP1` is quantised against 0.025 and the Swift client only checks `cells % coarse == 0`.
(b) `storms.detect` divides the lower-layer vorticity by the **reference** f0, `streamrec.F0` = 0.025, not by the world's `p.f0`: `Comp.zeta_max_f0` is in units of 0.025 in every world, so `NAME_ZETA` (0.5), `STRONG_ZETA` (0.70, §34.3)
and `ZETA_REF` keep one meaning: a storm is named at an absolute 0.0125 and `storm_strong` fires at 0.0175, whatever the world's f0. Without it the mini (f0 0.0165) names every storm at birth (0.55 to 0.85 f0 from the first
detection; 64k3d 0.40 to 0.50), `storm_named` never fires and `storm_strong` fires for every storm (four at step 80 025 of the planet probe). For a world whose f0 is 0.025 the expression is the old one, bit for bit
(pinned by a test). **Consequence for the W0 study driver** (`analysis/w0.py` re-exports `storms.detect`): its `zeta_max_f0` columns (`tracks.csv`, `storms.csv`) are in units of 0.025 for a world with another f0, so
the study's "named" reading of a mini run (peak >= 0.5 f0 = 0.0083 absolute, the one behind reading (a) of §37.2) is a column value of at least 0.33 (0.5 f0 / 0.025), not 0.5; the live tracker names at the equal-strength bar 0.0125 (column 0.5). The same driver's vorticity histogram and stored frames (`w0.py`, `w0_plots.py` axis "s zeta_c / f0") still divide by the world's own `p.f0`, so for an f0 other than 0.025 one study carries two units under the name f0 (CSV columns: 0.025; histogram, frames and plot axis: the world's); no result moves, since the lifetime criteria select tracks by detection count, and the histogram is not rebased because that needs a golden re-pin. **"f0" in the alert text** (`storm_strong`: "Storm X is at 0.70 f0") is the reference 0.025 in every world, an absolute 0.0175; in the mini world (f0 0.0165) it is not the world's f0, and the text is left as it is because it is pinned by the P0 digest of the alert texts (a re-pin is a deliberate act, and the 64k3d wording would change too); the template carries a comment.

### 37.5 Launcher and GUI

The launcher scans `runs/` and lists every run with a checkpoint as a source (`PlayCatalogScanner`), so a `mini3d` run appears by itself and the planet form works as it is. `Levers.swift` `Preset` gains `case mini3d` (required
by `test_gui_sync`: the enum equals `config.PRESETS` and each name needs its TOML file), so the Lab can start the evolution run. A launcher entry that makes a small world from nothing is not built (owner choice D5): a mini
source comes from `alife run --preset mini3d` or the Lab (31 minutes idle for 500 000 steps, up to about 45 shared), or from a `cp -c` copy of a checkpoint. The client scales with `L` from the header (`WorldLevels`, the 32 x 32
`TERR` grid gives 5-unit cells, `MAP1` is 40 blocks of 2 cells); not exercised here: a rendered mini planet, picking at 10 k rows, the dock, `WorldRenderBench` and `GPUWorldTests` at L = 160. **Camera, to check before the
owner's first play** (computed from code and state, not rendered): `WorldLevels.flyDistance(.region)` is `0.2 L / (tan 25 deg max(1, aspect))`, so at L = 160 the pose is 34 to 69 above the floor, inside the 0 to 80 organism
slab (at 320: 86 to 137, above everything); on the unmerged `gui/viewer2-a1` branch (Home straight down) the share of organisms above the eye is 26 % at aspect 1.0 and 41 % at 2.0; on main's pitched overview it does not occur.
If confirmed on the Mac day, floor the region distance at the world height plus a margin (a small `WorldLevels` change with a test).

### 37.6 The evolved source

A fresh source has almost no kin structure: the chronicle, the Cast tab, the territory film and the kin threads are built on kin groups (G2 rules: tag bins, `grid_clusters`, `SOCIAL_V1` thresholds `max(8, n_ref >> 9)` and
`max(2, n_ref >> 12)`), not on clades. The 80 000-step probe run has 2 groups of sizes [9 593, 25], top share 0.990 (`analysis.social`; 6 / 4 / 2 groups at 60 / 70 / 80 k, 2 / 4 / 3 resumed to 100 / 110 / 120 k with top shares
0.58 to 0.56); `64k3d_s0` at 450 000 has 9 groups with top share 0.43. **Acceptance of a fresh source, at 250 000 steps: at least 5 tracked kin groups, top share below 0.6 and at least 3 territory owners.** The run
`runs/mini3d_s0` (seed 0, `alife run --preset mini3d --steps 500000`, started 2026-10-24) is judged by it. **Result at 250 000 steps: FAIL** (a single-snapshot reading of the checkpoint with the G2 rules, which is an upper
envelope of what the tracker follows, for the kin counts and the owner counts alike; `scratchpad/mini/accept.py`, which reproduces the probe run's 2 groups, sizes [9 593, 25], top share 0.990, and 1 owner on `e0:80000`): 9 892 alive, kin groups of at least `enter` (19)
**3** (sizes 5 284, 4 442, 38; need at least 5 tracked), top share **0.534** (below 0.6: met), territory owners **2** (718 and 296 of 1 014 owned cells, mean purity 0.71; need at least 3; the column is a re-implementation, a cell owned by the group with most members and at least 1, without the EMA and `terr_k` 2 of `game.society.Dominance`, so the owner counts at 300 k to 500 k include owners of 7 to 14 cells and are an upper envelope; the FAIL at 250 k rests on the kin count, not on this column). Along the run (the same reading): 100 k 2 groups, top share
0.575, 2 owners; 150 k 2 groups ([9 131, 24], 0.992), 1 owner; 200 k 2 groups (4 811, 4 176; 0.532), 2 owners; 300 k 3 groups (4 923, 3 596, 2 235; 0.452), 3 owners; 350 k 3 (0.461), 3; 400 k 3 (0.545), 2; 450 k 4 (4 786, 2 931, 2 754, 512; 0.430), 4; 500 k 3 (6 028, 4 958, 184; 0.533), 3. At 250 k `analysis.social` (1 500 steps from the checkpoint, 6 snapshots) tracks 3 to 4 groups (3, 3, 4, 4, 3, 3; the 4s include groups of 17 and 9, below `enter`, kept by the leave bound): the top group is 0.53 of the population in five snapshots and 0.98 in one (250 500, the two factions merged into one cluster), so the top-share criterion is not stable from snapshot to snapshot; no snapshot reaches 5 groups, so the verdict stands. The
population is two large factions with at most one or two small ones, at 250 k and at the end; clades alive 5 at 80 k, 3 at 250 k and 3 at 500 k; the largest body 359, 373 and 2 303 rows at 80 k, 250 k and 500 k. The
alternative the specification names for a failure is a crop of an evolved 64k3d checkpoint to 160 x 160 (probe: 10 584 of 44 912 organisms kept, all four clades with the same shares, 6 to 10 kin groups, relaxed in about 800 steps;
it needs a new tool and a fork-path change, about 560 lines with tests); it is **not built in this change** and is the next step for the cast. A first play before the long run ends is possible from `runs/mini3d_e0`, a `cp -c`
copy of the 80 000-step probe run, with the one-kin-group caveat.
