## 38. Built structures (PR S1: the engine)

Normative text for the built-structures layer of the five-feature series (spec `structures/spec.md`, owner decision "B" of
2026-10-28, all nine decisions O1 to O9 accepted, the first effects the coordinator's choice C23 (revisitable), protection
from predators a third first-class effect by the owner's scope change of the same day). **S1 is the engine**: the grid, the
build action and the material sensor, decay, the three effects, the anti-trapping geometry R1 to R3, the counters, the
invariants, the tests and the bench. Absent from S1 and arriving in their own PRs: the observer and stream half (the `STRC`
record, `play.structures`, the `mat` dump, the observers' drift, `Acts.ext.structures`, the `BUILDING` flag: S2), the GUI
(map overlay, 3D cubes, levers: S3), the first world, the runs and the fork tool (S4; the fork is PR 0b's `alife migrate`).
Off by default and bit-identical when off (`tests/identity_matrix.py`, 43.9). Not enabled by any shipped preset; the overlay
`build` (`presets/build.toml`) switches it on.

### 38.1 The grid

`State.mat` / `State3.mat`: int32, shape `dims.field_shape` (`(FG, FG)` in 2D, `(FZ, FG, FG)` in 3D, z-major, the flat index
of `fields.cell_index`), a conditional extension field (43.2) that exists only with `structures.enabled`. 64k3d: 20 x 80 x 80 =
128 000 cells; mini3d 20 x 40 x 40. A cell is `world.field_cell` = 4 units (an agent has radius 1 and crosses a cell in at
least 8 steps): structures are coarse walls and clouds. The unit is the material unit, an integer in `[0, cap]` (default
4096). There is no float state, so decay is exact and bit-reproducible on any backend. Material does not move, diffuse,
settle or sink (v1); in 3D a builder deposits in its own layer, so structures can float (O3). A pre-structures checkpoint
loads with `mat` zeros when the feature is on (fill-on-load, 43.2) but cannot resume with it on (the weights differ): `alife migrate --enable structures` (PR 0b, 43.8) moves an evolved world onto the layout with zero new rows and columns, `mat` starting empty.

### 38.2 Deposit, cost, cap

Brain input `material` (`m/cap` at the agent's start-of-step cell, in [0, 1]) and output `build`; the blocks come from the
registry row (38.5). `actions.decode_build`: `b = max(tanh(y[OUT_BUILD]), 0)` (an exact zero is reachable, as `emit` and
`share`), `units = floor_i32(b·build_max)` in `[0, build_max]` (default 16 per step), 0 on a dead row. The cost is
`units·build_cost` quanta (default 2 q per unit), an int32 product (exact, no float floor), returned by the registry row's
`due` hook and added to the action due by `energy.pay_costs(3)` through `extra_due` (43.4): it counts in the solvency test and
is booked in `HEAT_ACTION` (`paid_action`). At full output an agent pays 32 q per step against a basal and brain cost of
about 137. An insolvent row (`structures.mask`) deposits nothing; its cost was due and is paid as far as it holds, as
`emit`'s. The deposit is `dep = ops.scatter_add_i32(n_cells, fcell, units)` at the START-of-step cell (order independent;
the one scatter of the feature, in `ops`), then `m1 = min(m + dep, cap)`; the excess is wasted (`MAT_WASTED`), the cost was
paid on the requested units: overbuilding a full cell wastes energy, a deliberate pressure not to stack builders. A row that
dies at S14 of the same step still deposits what it paid for at S8. A dead builder's structure persists and decays by itself.
Validation: `build_max <= 1024` and `cap <= 32767` keep `dep < 2^25` and `m1·decay_q12 < 2^27`.

### 38.3 Decay and the material identity

`loss = (m1·decay_q12 + 4095) >> 12` and `m' = m1 - loss`, applied after the deposit, the cap and the aperture gate in
`fields.update_mat` (S17): `ceil(m1·decay_q12/4096)`, an exponential decay of `decay_q12/4096` per step (default 16: 0.39 %)
with a floor of one unit per step on every non-empty cell, so material always disappears in finite time (`decay_q12 >= 1`,
O8). A full cell with no builder lasts exactly 864 steps and halves in 170; one builder at full output (16 units per step)
holds a cell at 3825 of 4096, 8 hold 1785, 4 hold 765, 2 hold 255 and 1 holds nothing (all pinned by `test_structures_effects`).
A structure needs sustained building of at least about 2 units per step per cell to exist and more than 4 to be effective.
**The second conserved quantity** (the material holds no energy, 38.7): per step, exactly,
`Σmat' = Σmat + BUILD_UNITS - MAT_WASTED - MAT_DECAYED`, with `BUILD_UNITS = Σ units` of the solvent builders, `MAT_WASTED =
Σ(pre - m1)` (the cap and the refused closings of 38.4b; per cell at most the cell's deposit) and `MAT_DECAYED = Σ loss`.
`MAT_TOTAL` is the end-of-step `Σmat`; `validate` bounds `cap·n_cells < 2^31` so the int32 counter cannot wrap. Checked every
step by the tests and by the smoke, not by a device bit (the range reuses `Diag.FIELD_RANGE`).

### 38.4 The effects

Per step, once, from the START-of-step `s.mat` at the start-of-step cell `fcell` (the field the organism senses is the field
that acts on it; `fcell`, a pure function of `s.pos`, is computed above S3w, which moves no trajectory): `structures.sense`
builds the per-cell table `fields.mat_table` (`here = m/cap`; `cover = max(m, reach·max over the face neighbours)/cap`; the
central-difference gradient of `m/cap`, divisor 2 as `sample_fields`, z mirrored) as lattice operations and gathers it ONCE,
`(n_cells, C)[fcell]`. A column exists only when used (static): `cover` needs `reach > 0` and a positive `shield_gain` or a
positive `shelter_gain` with the weather on (with `reach = 0` it is `here`), `grad` needs `barrier_gain > 0` and `exit_ease >
0`. "Around an organism" is the four (3D: six) face neighbours at weight `reach` (default 0.5): a wall protects what stands
beside it at half strength. No directional lee in v1 (O4).

1. **Shelter** (S3w). `weather.shelter_wind(wind, k, cfg)` with `k = 1 - shelter_gain·cover` multiplies `wind.force` and
   `wind.speed`, recomputes `breaks = speed·k > storm_break_u` (None stays None) and leaves `clip_bad`. It feeds, with no further
   edit, the bond break (`wind.breaks`), the storm hazard (`lifecycle.storm_mask(wind.speed)`: `p_i = storm_p·clip((speed -
   u0)/span, 0, 1)`, so a sheltered row dies less with no change in the number of draws) and the wind force of `physics.forces`.
   The weather itself is untouched: organisms do not change the storm, only what they feel. In a dry world shelter is inert
   (the branch needs the weather); barrier and shield still work. `weather.agent_drift(..., shelter=)` takes the factor for the
   observers; S1 does not yet pass it from the labels, the tracers or `game.observe` (S2), so the "velocity minus drift" labels
   are biased inside structures until then.
2. **Barrier** (S15). `physics.integrate(3)(..., drag_mult=)` divides by `gamma·drag_mult`; in 3D the z divisor gets the same
   factor (a dense medium also slows sinking; grip stays floor-only). `v = F/gamma` is overdamped, so thrust, wind drift and
   gravity are slowed alike; the clip to `v_max` follows. `drag_mult = physics.barrier_drag(F, here, grad, cfg)` is computed
   from the same total push `F` the integrator divides (38.4b R3). The slow-down uses the start cell (an agent entering a
   wall is slowed from its next step; a step moves at most 0.5 of a 4-unit cell, so the lag is at most one step).
3. **Shield** (S11). `energy.combat(..., shelter=shield_gain·cover)`: the victim's protection fraction enters the protection
   product of 43.6 (armour, then shelter, then guard, under `combat.protect_floor`), before the behavioural `defend`. The
   reduction acts on the integer demand before `proportional_take`; every later line (grant, gain, spill, residue, the drain
   rule) is unchanged and integer-exact, so `FLOW_STOLEN = FLOW_ATTACK_GAIN + FLOW_SPILL` closes with no new ledger term. It
   is a damage reduction, not a chance (O9): no RNG, deterministic, multiplicative with `defend`. The attacker's `attack_cost`
   is still paid, so shielded attacks are less profitable: predators keep the decision, prey gain from standing next to
   material. `SHIELDED_ATTACKS` counts the attacks on a victim with a positive fraction (`Combat.shielded`).
   `shield_gain = 1` (a full cell would make the victim immune, demand 0) is refused unless `combat.protect_floor > 0`,
   as `arms.key_floor = 0` is (cf289b4).

### 38.4b Anti-trapping geometry (R1 to R3; no R4)

Goal: builders can never trap themselves or others. All rules are fixed-shape lattice operations with no Python branching on
array values. A cell is OPEN when `m < thr`, `thr = ceil(open_frac·cap)` (default 2048), else CLOSED. `nopen[c]` is the number of
OPEN cells among the full neighbourhood of `c` (centre excluded): 8 in 2D, 26 in 3D, **17 on a floor or surface cell** (x and y
wrap, z does not; a missing cell counts as not open). `k = ceil(aperture·n_nbr)` (a 1e-9 guard keeps 0.25·8 at 2); default
`aperture` 0.25 gives k = 2 in 2D and 7 in 3D; `aperture = 0` switches R2 off statically.

* **R1 porosity.** The barrier is a drag, never a block: `here` is in [0, 1] and `validate` requires `0 <= barrier_gain <= 3`, so
  `drag_mult <= 1 + barrier_gain <= 4`. At `thrust_max` 0.1 a full cell (4 units) is crossed in about 160 steps, about the
  material's half-life (170), so an organism never needs a decay event to get out (`test_structures_trapping`: any single closed
  cell is crossed in at most 200 steps).
* **R2 aperture.** In `fields.update_mat`, from the start-of-step `m`: a deposit may not CLOSE a cell (`m < thr <= min(m + dep,
  cap)`) unless the cell is active in this step's colour phase and `box_min(nopen) >= k + 1` over its 3x3(x3) box; a refused
  closing leaves the cell at `thr - 1` (still open; the cost was paid and the clamped excess is `MAT_WASTED`). The colouring
  `cx mod px + px·(cy mod px) + px²·(cz mod 3)` with `px` the smallest divisor of `FG` that is at least 3, active when equal to
  `step mod n_phase` (`n_phase = px²`, 3D `3px²`: 16 / 48 on mini3d), keeps closing cells at least 3 apart, so the boxes are
  disjoint and each loses at most one open cell: **if every cell has `nopen >= k` at the start of a step it has at least `k` at
  the end** (decay only opens cells), and the all-open start has 8, 26 or 17. Hence `k >= 1` implies no cell is ever without a
  passable neighbour. Closing latency: one chance per `n_phase` steps. The invariant is a state property: the counter
  `APERTURE_VIOLATIONS` (cells with `nopen < k` in the start-of-step material), the device error `Diag.FIELD_RANGE` and the host
  `check` of `invariants.full_check`. Probe: the closed share stayed at most 0.59 to 0.67 under adversarial loads; the rule
  restricts shape, not quantity. **E8**: `validate` refuses `aperture > 0` on a lattice side `FG` below 4 or prime (no colouring
  with a short cycle), a sweep test checks every side from 1 to 130 and that cells of one colour are at least 3 apart.
  **E9**: `k <= 8` (2D) or `<= 17` (3D), the true count of boundary rows is used, and at k = 17 no boundary-layer cell can ever
  close (tested at both boundaries).
* **R3 easy exit** (variant A1, owner-approved, default). `drag_mult = 1 + barrier_gain·here·(1 - exit_ease·out)` with `out =
  max(0, -c·g)·s` in [0, 1], `c = F/|F|` the direction of the ACTUAL push (thrust, wind, repulsion, gravity: the `F` the
  integrator divides, so displacement counts, not intended motion: edge case **E6**), `g` the unit gradient of `m/cap`, `s =
  |grad|/(|grad| + 0.05)` the confidence that a surface is there. Moving down the gradient (out of dense material) is eased to
  `1 + 0.25·barrier_gain·here` at the default `exit_ease` 0.75; entering pays the full price; a plateau (zero gradient) pays the
  plain drag; a one-cell membrane has no central-difference gradient at its own cell, so R3 needs walls at least two cells thick
  to act. This deviates from the literal "drag only for motion up the gradient", which would make the interior of a plateau free of
  drag. `exit_ease = 0` is the plain barrier. No `where`, only `maximum`.
* **R4 accretionary growth** is not built (named in the spec; revisit if scattered single-cell piles never combine into shelter).

### 38.5 The sensor and the brain layout

The registry row (`ext/structures.py`, `alife.structures`) declares the blocks input `material` (1) and output `build` (1),
appended after the base and 3D tails and before any later feature's: 2D `IN_MATERIAL` 69, `D_IN` 70, `OUT_BUILD` 35, `D_OUT` 36;
3D 84, 85, 39, 40 (with structures alone; consumers read `lay.IN_MATERIAL` and `lay.OUT_BUILD`, None when off). `W1` has one
more row and `W2` one more column; the brain cost grows by about 1.3 % automatically. `layout_features` is `structures@1`, the
mask bit is 1 (extension index), so `genome_layout_version` is `base + 8` (2D 9, 3D 10; the spec's 5 and 6 predate the arms row
at index 0). Founders and immigrants have random weights (O6: about half build a little from step 0); `structures.silent_build`
zeroes the `build` column of founders (the control run: nobody builds until mutation finds it; the `material` row stays random).
Reproduction copies and mutates the parent's weights; material is environment, not genome.

### 38.6 Birth, death, bonds

Birth and death paths are untouched (a dead builder deposits nothing; its structure persists). A director catastrophe kills
agents only. Shelter lowers `breaks`, so a sheltered colony keeps its bonds; there is no other bond interaction (the guard
shield of the bonds series joins the same protection product).

### 38.7 Energy ledger, counters, crowding

* **Ledger.** Material holds no energy (O1): the build cost leaves the agent through `paid_action` into `HEAT_ACTION`, decay
  moves no energy, `total_energy` does not include `mat`. `N_LEDGER = 16`, `LedgerIdx`, `ledger_cum` and every consumer are
  unchanged; no new term. The rejected alternative (material as an energy bank with `FLOW_BUILD` and `FLOW_DECAY` terms) needs a 17th
  slot, makes a structure a recyclable energy store and has a large blast radius.
* **Counters** (block `structures`, 11 int32, after `DEATHS_STORM` and the `protect` block; `state.counter_index(cfg, name)`):
  `BUILD_UNITS`, `MAT_WASTED`, `MAT_DECAYED`, `MAT_TOTAL`, `MAT_CELLS` (cells with material), `SHIELDED_ATTACKS`, `TRAPPED` (alive
  rows in a cell with `nopen < 1`; 0 by construction with R2 on, the experiment metric with it off), `APERTURE_VIOLATIONS`,
  `SLOWED` (alive rows with `drag_mult > 2`), `MAT_CLOSED` (cells at or above `thr`), `HASH_HIDDEN` (agents beyond the hash
  capacity `C` in their cell, `Σ max(count - C, 0)`: the neighbours the search cannot see). The metrics row gains `build_units`,
  `build_wasted`, `build_decayed`, `build_mat_total` and `build_mat_cells` and `build_mat_closed` (interval means),
  `build_shielded`, `build_trapped`, `build_aperture_violations`, `build_slowed_frac` (over agent-steps) and `build_hash_hidden`
  (interval sum, int64), only with the feature on.
  **E10**: a per-step counter is int32 (bounded: `BUILD_UNITS <= N·build_max`), the interval sums are int64 on the host
  (`interval_row`), a long-count test sums 5.2e9 units in one row.
* **E7, crowding (advisory).** The barrier slows agents inside walls, so they can crowd into one hash cell, and the
  neighbour search then hides the agents beyond its capacity `C`. This is reported, never fatal (the coordinator's decision):
  `Diag.CELL_OVERFLOW_WARN` as in every world, the per-step counter `CELL_OVERFLOW` (cells over capacity, in every world) and the
  structures counter `HASH_HIDDEN` (agents hidden), summed per interval in int64 in the metrics row (`cell_overflow`,
  `build_hash_hidden`), and an `alert:` line on stderr from the runner at each interval that hid anyone. Structures-off runs
  behave as before. **Runs with persistent overflow are excluded from experiments** (the measurement suite gates on
  `build_hash_hidden`); evolved structures-off worlds peak at a hash occupancy of 31 to 40 against `C` = 48 (`fast`: 12), and
  the barrier adds clumping, so a long build run should be watched for the alert (raise `sensing.cell_capacity` if it fires).
* **Hash salts / RNG.** No stream, no draw, no hash: everything is integer or elementwise float32.

### 38.8 State, checkpoint, digests, config

`mat` is the last field of the generated state class (after `arms` when both are on, 43.2). `legacy_state_digest(_3d)` hash
frozen name lists, so the goldens and the legacy digests do not see it; the full `state_digest` of a structures-on state includes
it. `state_from_arrays` fills a file lacking `mat` with zeros when the feature is on and refuses a file that has `mat` when it
is off (43.2). All 13 keys are in `POST_V01_KEYS` and `SERIAL_OMIT_KEYS` through the registry row, so every existing hash is
unchanged, the section is absent from `config.json` while default, and each key is inert at its default while `enabled` is
false (`validate`). The Director never reaches the structures keys (E24: no menu parameter, env field or policy key carries one,
no director module names the section; `tests/test_structures_step.py`).

### 38.9 What S1 leaves to S2 and S3

Stream record `STRC`, `play.structures`, the `mat` dump kind and its cadence key, `Acts.ext.structures` and the `BUILDING` flag,
the observers' drift (`labels`, `tracers`, `game.observe`), the inspector, the GUI (map layer, instanced cubes, levers,
`GUI_LANDED`) and the world `mini3d + build` runs. The registry row declares `metric_prefix = build_`, `act_flag = BUILDING` and
the overlay `build` but no dump kind, colour mode or stream tag yet (the registry test checks those against `streamrec`).

### 38.10 Config

`[structures]` (`StructuresConfig`): `enabled` false; `cap` 4096; `build_max` 16; `build_cost` 2; `decay_q12` 16; `shelter_gain`
0.8; `barrier_gain` 3.0; `shield_gain` 0.5; `reach` 0.5; `open_frac` 0.5; `aperture` 0.25; `exit_ease` 0.75; `silent_build` false.
All values are provisional until the first runs; the sweep axes are `build_cost` (1, 2, 4) and `decay_q12`. Reasons: `cap` 4096
(12-bit headroom, levels fit a byte on the wire); `build_max` 16 and `decay_q12` 16 (one builder at full output holds a cell at
93 %); `build_cost` 2 (32 q per step at full output, about 23 % of the basal and brain cost; a full cell from empty costs 8 192
q, 16 % of `e_init`); `shelter_gain` 0.8 (a full cell cuts the felt air speed to 20 %, peak core wind 0.054 to 0.086 against
`storm_u0` 0.06, never total); `barrier_gain` 3 (the R1 maximum); `shield_gain` 0.5 (halves theft damage); `open_frac` 0.5 and
`aperture` 0.25 (the probe holds the invariant with the closed share up to about 0.65). Validation (with `enabled`): `cap` in
[256, 32767] and `cap·n_cells < 2^31`; `build_max` in [1, 1024]; `build_cost` in [0, 2^15] with `build_cost·build_max < 2^20`;
`decay_q12` in [1, 4096]; `shelter_gain`, `shield_gain`, `reach`, `exit_ease` in [0, 1]; `barrier_gain` in [0, 3]; `open_frac` in
(0, 1]; `aperture` in [0, 1] with `k <= 8` (2D) or `17` (3D) and, when positive, a colourable `FG` (38.4b); `shield_gain = 1` needs
`combat.protect_floor > 0`. `aperture = 0` with `barrier_gain > 0` validates but logs a warning: R2 is off, walls can enclose
organisms (`TRAPPED` can be above 0; R1 still bounds the drag at 4x), so it is a control only. `alife bench
--structures` times the step with the feature on against the same config with it off (blocks off, on, on, off).

### 38.11 Tests

`test_structures_ledger` (the ledger and the material identity every step for 1 500 steps in 2D and 3D, the cost in
`HEAT_ACTION`, an insolvent builder), `test_structures_effects` (decay in 864 steps, steady-state levels, `decode_build`, the
sensor, a deposit, shelter in the step in 2D and 3D, the barrier, the shield with `defend`), `test_structures_trapping` (the
spec's six tests: by construction in 2D, 3D and in a storm, the adversarial property test over lattice sizes, `k`, `open_frac`
and four deposit patterns, the numpy reference equal to the engine bit for bit, escape time from a sealed pocket within 10 % of
the analytic bound and shortened by decay, the R1 bound, the R3 direction; E6, E8, E9), `test_structures_config` (ranges,
hashes, layout 70/36 and 85/40, schema, fill and refusal, `silent_build`, the overlay), `test_structures_determinism` (twice,
resume from a checkpoint, row-order independence, the functions compiled equal eager, the device range check),
`test_structures_off`, `test_structures_crowding` (E7), `test_structures_compile` (E4: every constant, pairs that print alike),
`test_structures_step` (the bench mirror in 2D, 3D and a storm, observer purity, the pair with arms, E24, the metrics row and
E10, a CLI run). The whole step is not bit-equal compiled and eager from step 0 (the brain's reductions, 42.7), so compiled equals
eager is asserted for the structures functions only. MLX 0.32 cannot compile a graph that builds one roll of one array twice, so
`update_mat` and `sense` are each called once per step.

### 38.12 Departures from the spec, and non-goals

Counter and block placement, the `mask` and layout version (9 / 10), the `silent_build` key and the registry hooks follow the
integration plan and 43; the lattice gather is one table instead of 4 to 6 gathers of N (cheaper); the cover and gradient are
lattice operations, not per-agent gathers; crowding is an advisory counter and alert, not an error (E7, 38.7); the identity matrix
takes the overlay list from the base tree (a feature overlay switches its feature on, so it has no counterpart in the base);
`shield_gain = 1` needs `protect_floor > 0` (cf289b4); the registry row carries `enable=` (`alife migrate --enable structures`) and
declares `mat` with `conserved=False` (the material holds no energy, so a forced removal cannot leak `TOTAL`); the observers'
drift (`agent_drift(shelter=)`) is not wired from the labels, tracers and `game.observe` (38.9, S2: it must land before any
labelled run with weather and structures both on). Non-goals: the Director does not act on structures; material
does not move or hold energy; no directional lee; no gradient or lee sensor (one `material` input in v1, O5).

Identity matrix against a fresh `git archive` of e64be03, structures off, after merging the current `engine/arms` (PR 0a, 0b, the A1
review fixes, cf289b4): "OK: bit-identical, 0 DIFF, 0 INFO" (the matrix takes the overlay list from the base tree). Fast suite
(`-n 4 --dist loadfile`, `-p cpu_device`): 4,857 passed, 91 skipped, 1 xfailed, 3 failed: the baseline
`test_lifecycle_compiles_and_matches_eager` (HANDOVER B1) and two stub-counter tests that this change's eleventh counter broke and the
same change fixed (they pass: `test_ext_counters`, `test_ext_ledger`, `test_ext_registry`, 25 passed). Metal (one job): `test_game_purity`, the
structures files, `test_ext_migrate` (with the structures case), `test_ext_counters`, `test_bench`: 286 passed and the known timing test
`test_the_device_part_of_a_snapshot_is_evaluated_when_timed` once over its bound (passes on rerun, as in 43.10). Smoke on the GPU, `mini3d`,
random founders, per-step identity and `full_check`: with `storm160 + build` 6,000 steps, population 4,096 to a minimum near 2,900 and back
to 5,164, material total up to 1.20e6 units on 3,800 cells with up to 89 closed, 7.9 % of agent-steps slowed, 94,110 shielded attacks,
`TRAPPED` and `APERTURE_VIOLATIONS` 0 at every step, `diag` 0; dry `mini3d + build` 5,000 steps alike (peak 1.14e6 units, 81 closed cells).
The independent review's 4,000-step storm run had `cell_overflow` 0. `bench --structures` on 64k3d (GPU, another session's CPU job running
in the first run): steady **+0.24 to +0.31 ms** on about 15.4 ms (1.6 to 2.3 %); the first block pair can be an outlier up to 1.0 ms. The
spec's estimate was 0.15 to 0.4 ms (under 3 %).

## 39. Communication: the voice channel (PR C1: the engine)

Normative text of the voice channel (Review-log I68; the specification is the owner-accepted `comm/spec.md`, all
recommendations D1 to D15 accepted). This section follows §43 for its registry row (`ext/comm.py`), counter block,
`ActFlag` bit and layout version. **No new energy source and no 17th ledger term**: the cost of speaking is an
addend of the action due and is booked in `HEAT_ACTION`. C1 is the engine; the observer channel for the analysis
(`Acts.ext.comm`), the stream record, the GUI and `analysis/comm.py` are C2 and C3 (39.8, 39.9).

### 39.1 Scope and principles

An optional, evolvable **voice channel** beside the legacy 2-number `msg`: W call channels per organism (default 4),
each an intensity in `[0, 1)`, zero exactly reachable. Listeners hear the K sensed neighbours they already have (no
new search). Speaking costs energy, so honest signalling is a consequence of the ledger, not an assumption. Two
engine controls make the receivers' side measurable. With `comm.enabled = false` (the default) nothing is allocated,
hashed or serialised and the engine is bit-identical to the one without the feature (the identity matrix gates it).
The other channels are left alone: the legacy `msg` (2 numbers, `IN_MSG_MEAN`, `NBR_MSG0`, `BOND_MSG0`, cost
`energy.msg_cost`) and the three chemical `emit` channels.

### 39.2 The legacy channel (for the record)

`msg = tanh(y[OUT_MSG:+2])`, bipolar, masked by alive and solvency, stored for one step in `State.msg (N, MSG)`,
cleared at birth (`lifecycle.clear`), read as the unweighted mean over the K neighbours (2 inputs), as channel 0 of
each of the NS nearest (`NBR_MSG0`) and of each bond partner (`BOND_MSG0`); cost `floor(msg_cost · Σ|msg|)` inside
`action_due`. Receivers cannot tell one loud neighbour from eight faint ones, cannot locate the sound, and there was
no control that removes the receivers' side (`docs/SIGNALS.md` §5, §6). The voice channel adds those, as a parallel
type; the legacy channel is untouched.

### 39.3 State

No new `State` field. `State.msg` widens to `(N, MSG + W)`: columns `0..1` are the legacy channels, columns `MSG:` the
voice (f32 in `[0, 1)`, dead rows 0, a newborn row 0 by the existing `clear`). `Dims.voice_w = W` (0 off),
`Dims.msg_w = MSG + voice_w` (`state.expected_layout` and `init_state` use it), `d.ext("comm").hear_range`. The one
legacy reader that mixed columns, `sensing.build_inputs`' `msg_mean`, slices `s.msg[:, :MSG]` (static: no slice while
off, so the off graph is unchanged). `invariants` checks the legacy range on the first two columns and
`msg: voice outside [0, 1)` on the rest; the dead-row rule already covers the whole array. The offline readers
(`analysis/signals.py`) use `act.msg`, which stays `(N, MSG)`.

### 39.4 Speaking (S7, S8, S15)

`comm.decode` (the registry `decode` hook) returns `Voice(sig, due)`: `sig = clip(tanh(y[OUT_VOICE:+W]), 0, 1 - 2⁻²⁴)`
(non-negative on purpose: silence is exactly reachable and free, a channel is a call type and not a sign, and
superposition at the receiver cannot cancel; the clip keeps `sig < 1` where f32 `tanh` saturates), masked by alive.
`comm.mask` (after S8) zeroes `sig` and `due` of an insolvent row: it pays everything it holds and does not speak.
S15 stores `concatenate([act.msg, sig])` in `msg` (`step._msg_columns`, mirrored in `bench._StagedStep`). One step of
latency: the voice heard at step t was spoken at t-1.

### 39.5 Hearing and the controls (S5)

`comm.hear(voice, nbr, desc, cfg) -> (N, W + nd)` is a pure function of the stored voice (so offline counterfactuals
call it with a modified array). Neighbour `j` of `i` weighs `a = clip(1 - dist/range, 0, 1) ** atten_pow`, 0 where
`desc[..., NBR_PRESENT]` is 0 (invalid or dead), times `desc[..., NBR_KIN] ** kin_exp` when `kin_exp > 0`. The first
`W` outputs are `min(Σ_j a_j · voice_j, 1)` (saturating superposition); the last `nd` are the bearing, the
loudness-weighted mean of the body-frame offsets `desc[..., NBR_DX/DY(/DZ)]` (`/R`): `Σ w_j rel_j / max(Σ w_j, 1e-3)`
with `w_j = a_j Σ_c voice_jc`, so `|bearing| <= 1` and it is exactly 0 with no sound. A neighbour at `dist >= range` or
invalid contributes exactly 0; the result is equivariant under row relabelling; the K = 8 sum is a fixed-order
reduction (no matmul, so DESIGN F20 does not apply). `comm.range = 0` means the sensing radius (`hear_range`); a larger
range would need a larger `sensing.radius` (the hash cell is at least R), so the cap is deliberate (D7): relaying gives a
wave at one body range per step. `kin_exp = 0` (default) hears everyone (eavesdropping and deception possible); `kin_exp
= 1` weights by the kin similarity of §5 (Mitri et al.'s relatedness lever, an experiment arm). Bonded partners are
ordinary neighbours.

`comm.control` selects what the listeners receive; costs and the speaking path are identical in every arm:

* `none`: the stored voice.
* `deaf`: both input blocks are exactly 0.
* `decoy`: each alive row's voice is taken from another alive row, a cyclic shift in alive-rank space
  (`comm.decoy_index`): the alive rows in row order are ranked and rank `r` is heard as rank `(r + shift) % n_alive`,
  `shift = 1 + hash32(step, 0, SALT) % (n_alive - 1)`. Integer arithmetic and the comm hash salt only, no RNG stream, no
  layout bump, traced only for `control = decoy`. A bijection on the alive rows, never the identity, so the marginal
  statistics of what is heard are the population's while the sender-receiver coupling is cut (E19; the spec's `step · 40503`
  stride overflows int32 after 53 k steps, a hash of the step does not). A shift over all N rows would deliver mostly
  silence when alive << N (a partial deaf: mean heard 0.015 against 0.09 under `none`, found by the C1 review), hence the
  ranks; a test with alive << N pins the decoy's mean heard to `none`'s.

A listener hears its K nearest neighbours inside the range (the list of §4). Under hash-cell overflow (`HASH_HIDDEN`, advisory)
which neighbours are visible depends on row order; this is the pre-existing behaviour of the neighbour search, not of comm.

### 39.6 Layout, version, checkpoints and the migration

Registry row `comm` (index 3, `ext/comm.py`): inputs `voice` (W) then `voice_bearing` (nd), output `voice` (W), appended
in `TAIL_ORDER` after the bonds tail (alone: 2D `D_IN/D_OUT` 75/39, 3D 91/43 at W = 4), token `comm{W}@1`, mask bit 3.
`Layout.IN_VOICE`, `IN_VOICE_BEARING`, `OUT_VOICE` are None when off. The `layout_features` meta (§43) carries the width,
so there is no separate `voice_w` key (the spec's, superseded by §43.2). Founders and immigrants get random weights
(D13). Existing checkpoints load into an off config unchanged; they do not auto-load into a comm-on config. The migration
is `alife migrate --enable comm` (`ExtSpec.enable` sets `comm.enabled`): W + nd zero rows in `W1`/`pend_W1` between the
old inputs and the recurrent rows, W zero columns in `W2`/`pend_W2`, W zero columns in `msg`, so the migrated brain
computes the same hidden state and legacy outputs and its voice is `max(tanh(0), 0) = 0`: a silent start from an evolved
population (the "language from nothing" experiment). Mutation noise is drawn with the new shape, so the trajectories part
at the first mutated child; the equivalence test compares one step with reproduction unrequested.

### 39.7 Cost and ledger (E17)

`due_of(uid, step, sig) = floor(cost · Σ_c sig_c + u)`, `u = dither(uid, step)` the top 24 bits of `hash32(uid, step,
SALT)` over 2²⁴: an integer per row and step, exactly 0 for silence (`u < 1`) and exact on average for a call below one
quantum (E17: without the dither `floor` makes every whisper under 1/cost free, and a population could signal for
nothing). It joins the action due through the registry `due` hook (`extra_due`), so it is booked in `HEAT_ACTION`, solvency
and payment order are the existing ones and the 16-term ledger closes. `cost = 0` has no hook (None, nothing traced).
Counters `COMM_SPEAKERS` (rows with some call quantum `floor(256 · sig) > 0` after the solvency mask, the `ActFlag.SPOKE` form)
and `COMM_DUE` (the dues of the solvent rows; `COMM_DUE <= HEAT_ACTION` every step, equal when voice is the only action term;
`COMM_DUE` is the masked due, so an insolvent row's partial payment is in `HEAT_ACTION` but not in `COMM_DUE`: `comm_due_share`
undercounts under starvation).
The per-step counters are int32; the interval sums in `metrics.interval_row` are int64 on the host (E10), and `validate`
bounds `cost · width < 2¹⁵` and `cost · width · n_max < 2³¹` so neither the row due nor the counter can overflow.
Founder arithmetic (64k3d, basal 100 + brain 37.6 q): a full chorus at `cost` 4 is 16 q (11.6 % of upkeep); the cost is
provisional and the first parameter the experiments sweep ({0, 4, 16, 64}); the sweep decides it (90 to 94 % of founders speak at
`cost` 4, which is no pressure). The brain's listening cost is already in the L1
upkeep of the wider weights.

### 39.8 Observers, stream, GUI (C2, not in C1)

C1 sets only `ActFlag.SPOKE` (1024 = 128 << 3) in `Acts.flags` (the per-row form of `COMM_SPEAKERS`) and publishes the
metrics `comm_speaker_frac`, `comm_due`, `comm_due_share`. `Acts.ext.comm` (voice, heard, audible), the `FSIG` stream
record, the `voice` colour mode, the organism-panel bars and the GUI levers (`GUI_LANDED`) are C2/C3. The Director gets no
comm lever (E24: `comm.*` are config keys outside the Director's env levers; a test pins it).

### 39.9 What the analysis needs (for C3 and the measurement suite, §44)

The language-score adapter of the measurement suite (E6) and `analysis/comm.py` need, per sampled pair of consecutive
observed steps: the voice spoken (`msg[:, MSG:]`, quantised), the voice heard (the `hear` result of the start-of-step state,
which `comm.hear` reproduces from `(voice, nbr, desc)` for `control = none` only: the adapter must call
`comm.ext_inputs(s, cfg, ctx)` for `deaf` and `decoy`), the neighbour list, the sender context (hurt, food, crowd, energy,
bonds, height) and the receiver's next-step behaviour. Everything but the heard vector is already in `State`/`Acts`; the
heard vector is the C2 observer field, or an offline `hear` call on `resim.cached_states`. The causal controls are runs from
one checkpoint with `--set comm.control=deaf|decoy` (a start-of-run key: `comm.control` is not layout-affecting, so a fork
may change it). The operational definition of a language in the spec (transfer information above its shuffle null, absent in
`deaf`, at the `decoy` level or below, and `none` beating both on fitness at the same cost) is C3's verdict, not C1's.

comm`. Constants in code, not keys: the saturating min at 1, the bearing floor 1e-3, the `1 - 2⁻²⁴` clip. 2D and 3D both.

### 39.12 Evidence (PR C1, 2026-10-29)

* **Layout**: alone, 2D `D_IN/D_OUT` 75/39 and 3D 91/43 at W = 4 (the spec's numbers); the brain grows by 7 inputs and 4 outputs in
  3D (about 7 % of the parameters). Off: the identity matrix against `e64be03` is bit-identical (0 DIFF, 0 INFO).
* **Smoke** (mini3d, N = 16 384 slots, Metal, founders with random brains, one seed, 6 000 steps each; not a result): for
  `control` none, deaf and decoy the ledger closes at every step (0 bad steps), `COMM_DUE <= HEAT_ACTION` every step, `diag` 0,
  the host `full_check` is clean every 1 000 steps, the population goes from about 2 900 to 4 700 to 4 900. The calls are neither
  dead nor saturated by the counter (`COMM_SPEAKERS`), but **nearly everyone speaks**: 93.8 to 93.9 % of the alive rows say
  something each step, which is the founders' arithmetic (a random output is positive in half the draws, so 1 - 2⁻⁴ = 93.75 % have
  some channel up) and not selection; the mean call is 0.14 per channel and the voice costs 2.1 to 2.2 q per agent-step, 4.3 to

  16, 64}) is where honest signalling or silence has to appear.
* **Cost** (`alife bench --preset 64k3d --overlay comm --comm --stages`, M5 Pro, Metal, interleaved off/on blocks): the step is
  13.83 ms off and 14.56 ms with the voice channel (**+0.735 ms, +5.3 %**, the two block pairs +0.69 and +0.71 ms; the spec's gate
  is +8 %, its estimate under 0.5 ms for `hear` plus 3 to 4 % for the wider GEMVs). Fused step 14.45 ms, peak memory 1.07 GB.

* **Tests**: ruff check and format clean on the whole repo; fast suite (CPU plugin, `-n 4 --dist loadfile`) 5 018 passed, 91 skipped,

  `test_invariants`, `test_bench`, `test_game_acts` (the known timing test `test_the_device_part_of_a_snapshot_is_evaluated_when_timed`
  once over its bound, passes on rerun, as in 43.10). On the GPU the migrated brain differs from the source in the last float bits (the
  GEMV order changes with the inserted zero rows), so the one-step equivalence is exact on integers and the ledger and 1e-5 on floats.

## 40. Bonds that pay (PR B1: conductive sharing and the bond block; PR B2: the roles)

Normative text of the bonds feature (Review-log I69; the specification is the owner-accepted `bonds/spec.md`,
recommendations O1 to O11, germ role deferred, R4 movement not built). This section follows §43 for its
registry row (`ext/bonds.py`), conditional state fields, counter block, `ActFlag` bit, `Acts.ext` and layout
version. **No new energy source and no 17th ledger term**: every flow here is `FLOW_SHARED`/`HEAT_SHARE` (B1) or
a multiplier on a flow the ledger already books (B2).

### 40.1 Switch, state, config

`bonds_ext(cfg) = roles.enabled or bonds.share_mode != 0` is the one static switch (`ext.bonds.bonds_ext`,
`bonds.bonds_ext`). When true the feature has a brain footprint (40.4), three conditional per-agent state fields
and a counter block; when false nothing of it exists and the engine is bit-identical to the one without it.

| field | dtype / shape | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | int8 `(N,)` | 0 generalist, 1 forager, 2 guard (3 reserved for the deferred germ); changes only with `roles.enabled` (B2) |
| `role_dwell` | int16 `(N,)` | steps since the last switch, saturating at `ramp_steps`; 0 unless `roles.enabled` |
| `bond_flow` | int16 `(N, B)` | net received minus sent at the slot at the last S12, clipped to ±32767; 0 on an empty slot and on a dead row |

All three are `conserved=False` (labels and a flow memory, no energy quanta), `on_birth = "rest"` (a newborn or
immigrant starts with role 0, dwell 0 and no flow memory). Config: `[bonds] share_mode` (0 the legacy gift, 1
conductive with mutual consent, 2 conductive and obligate), `share_kappa` (0.125), `share_kin_floor` (1.0);
`[roles] enabled`. All four are in `POST_V01_KEYS`/`SERIAL_OMIT_KEYS` and so leave the hash and `config.json` of
every existing run unchanged (frozen defaults pinned in `tests/test_ext_guards.py`). Validation: `share_mode in
{0, 1, 2}`; with `share_mode == 0` the other two keys must keep their default; with a conductive mode
`share_kappa in (0, 1/(2B)] = (0, 0.125]`, `share_kin_floor in [0, 1]`, `share_rate in [1, 2^22)`. `alife migrate
--enable bonds` sets `roles.enabled` (allocates the block and the state; `--set bonds.share_mode=2` moves the
sharing). The world overlay `bonds` (`presets/bonds.toml`) sets `share_mode = 2`, `share_kin_floor = 0.5`,
`roles.enabled`; the brain-cost compensation of spec O11 is NOT applied (scale `energy.brain_cost_per_l1` by
`params_off/params_on` with `--set` for a clean A/B). The **inert twin** of the measures (O3) is
`roles.enabled = false` with `share_mode != 0`: the layout, state and cost of the full configuration with the
role effects cut.

### 40.2 The conductive share (S12)

`energy.share_slots(..., kin=None)` replaces only the `amount` line and the gate; `share_mode == 0` is the legacy
expression, bit for bit (static branch; test S-4 against a copy of the old function). Modes 1 and 2, on the
energies at the start of S12 (both ends of a bond read the same two values):

```text
gap      = E_i - E_j                                      (N, B), E = cb.energy
amt      = min((gap * q8(share_kappa)) >> 8, E_i // B)
mode 1:  s = clip(floor(256 * act.share), 0, 255);  s_j gathered through rev;  amt = min(amt, (min(s_i, s_j) * share_rate) >> 8)
         gate: s_i > 0 and s_j > 0
mode 2:  amt = min(amt, share_rate)                       (the share outputs are ignored)
out      = amt  where valid and partner == partner0 and solvent_i and gap > 0, else 0
inc      = the partner's out gathered through rev;  got = (inc * eff) >> 8
eff      = q8(share_efficiency)                           when share_kin_floor == 1 or mode 0
         = floor(256 * share_efficiency * (f + (1 - f) * kin_ij))   kin_ij = exp(-|tag_i - tag_j|^2 / tag_scale^2), f = share_kin_floor
```

Properties (tests `test_bonds_share.py`): only the richer end sends, so each quantum is received exactly once
(`Σ out == Σ inc`, `Σ E_before - Σ E_after == Σ (inc - got)` = `HEAT_SHARE`); the receiving end needs no solvency
(an insolvent poor partner is rescued, as in §10.7); nothing is sent over a slot whose partner changed at S9;
`share_kappa <= 1/(2B)` bounds the receipts so that no row ends above its richest neighbour (the maximum never
rises, the minimum never falls). **E14 (ring overdraw):** the per-slot cap `E // B` bounds a row's total send by
its energy on any bond graph (full-degree rows in a ring, a star hub, K5), so no row goes below zero; the
adversarial ring/star/K5 tests with ties, all-rich, all-poor, alternating and one-in-a-sea energies pass, and
the test fails when the cap is removed (with a kappa beyond the validated range, since the validated kappa makes
the cap redundant by a factor of two: `Σ_b amt <= E/2`). The kin-scaled efficiency changes only the heat; the
send is kin-blind. `kin` is computed from the post-S9 partner by `bonds.slot_kin` (None unless
`share_kin_floor < 1`).

### 40.3 State update, E15

At S14, after `drop_dead`, `bonds.state_after(s, sv, dt.partner, sl)` returns the new fields of the survivors:
`role`, `role_dwell` of dead rows are cleared to 0, and `bond_flow = clip(got - out)` where the slot is still
occupied after S14 and the row survived, else 0. **E15 (a partner dies and its row is reused in the same
step):** `drop_dead` clears every bond with a dead end before S16 allocates the free rows, `state_after` zeroes
the flow memory of the gone slot, and `FieldSpec.on_birth = "rest"` resets the newborn's role, dwell and flow;
the test runs 700 steps of a tiny world (mode 2, kin floor 0.5), asserts at every step that a row reused in
the step has no partner but its parent, fresh fields, and that no survivor points at a reused row but its
parent, and requires at least one reused row that had bonds. `tests/test_bonds_step.py::test_state_after_*`
is the unit form.

### 40.4 Brain layout

Thirteen inputs after the structures tail (`TAIL_ORDER`): `IN_ROLE` 1 (own role code: forager +1, guard -1,
generalist 0), `IN_BOND_ROLE` B (the partner's code per slot), `IN_BOND_KIN` B (`kin_ij`), `IN_BOND_FLOW` B
(`clip(bond_flow / share_rate, -1, 1)`), 0 on empty slots; two outputs `OUT_ROLE_A`, `OUT_ROLE_B` (read in B2).
2D `D_IN` 69 to 82, `D_OUT` 35 to 37; 3D 84 to 97, 39 to 41; `genome_layout_version = base + 4*mask` with bonds
mask bit 2; `layout_features` token `bonds@1`. The whole block is allocated in B1, so the layout changes once;
the role inputs read 0 and the outputs do nothing until B2. Founder weights are random (not silent).

### 40.5 Counters, observer channel, metrics

Counter block `bonds` (five int32 per-step counters, summed in int64 on the host, E10): `ROLE_SWITCHES`,
`N_FORAGERS`, `N_GUARDS`, `SHIELDED_BY_GUARD` (the role counters read 0 until B2), `SHARE_SLOTS_ACTIVE` (slots with
`out > 0`). Interval-row keys (prefix `bond_`): `bond_flux` (interval sum of `FLOW_SHARED`), `bond_share_slots`
(mean per step), `bond_role_switches`, `bond_forager_frac`, `bond_guard_frac`. Observer channel:
`Acts.ext.bonds = BondActs(role (N,) int8 start-of-step, bond_flow (N, B) int16)`; the per-slot flows are
already in `Acts.share_out/share_got`; the `ActFlag.ROLE_SWITCHED` bit (512) is reserved by §43.5 and set in B2.
With the feature on, the step computes the S12 slots in both the observed and the plain graph
(`share_from_slots(share_slots(...))` is `en.share`); `bench.py`'s staged mirror does the same.

### 40.6 What is left

B3: observers and scorecard (`body_role_entropy`, `role_diff_z`, assortativity, `analysis/bonds.py`), the bond-flow
overlay, the role colour mode, GUI levers (`roles.*` and the `bonds.*` keys into `AlifeCore/Levers.swift`). R4 (movement
couplings) and R5 (germ) are not scheduled; the runs (spec section 14) wait for B3.

### 40.7 Tests (B1)

`test_bonds_share.py` (S-1 conservation on random graphs in both modes with and without the kin floor, S-2
antisymmetry and no overshoot on star/chain/ring/K5, S-3 consent, solvency and `partner0`, the kin heat, S-4
mode 0 bit-identical, E14), `test_bonds_step.py` (footprint and layout, validation, the overlay and the inert
twin, ledger closure and sharing active in 2D and 3D, `bond_flow` as the net slot transfer, determinism and
resume, observer purity and `Acts.ext.bonds`, E15, E10), `test_bonds_compile.py` (E4: kappa, kin floor, rate,
efficiency and mode compiled in one process equal their eager results and differ from each other),
`tests/test_ext_migrate.py::test_migrating_an_evolved_world_onto_bonds` (the migration case).

### 40.8 The role machine (PR B2)

`roles.enabled` switches the machine on (static); without it `roles.decode`/`mask`/`due` are the identity and the
roles never change (sharing only, or the inert twin of the measures). Two brain outputs `OUT_ROLE_A`, `OUT_ROLE_B`
(the block allocated in B1) give `a = tanh(y_a)`, `b = tanh(y_b)` and, with the dead zone `τ = roles.threshold`
(0.5, in `(0, 1)`):

```text
a > τ, b < -τ  -> forager (1)       a < -τ, b > τ  -> guard (2)       a < -τ, b < -τ -> generalist (0)
anything else (the dead zone; the a > τ, b > τ corner is reserved for the deferred germ) -> keep the role
```

Keep-by-default is the hysteresis: a role persists without a sustained output. `roles.decode_role(y, role, cfg)`
is a function parallel to `actions.decode_motion3` (`Actions` keeps its fields); the registry hooks are
`roles.decode` (S7, a `RoleDec(req, role0)`), `roles.mask` (after S8: an insolvent row keeps its role, its
switch cost was due and is paid as far as it holds) and `roles.due` (`switch_cost·(req != role)` quanta in the
`extra_due` of `pay_costs`, so booked in `HEAT_ACTION`, and counted in the solvency total). At S14
`bonds.state_after` commits: `role' = req` for a survivor, `role_dwell' = 0` on a switch else
`min(dwell + 1, ramp_steps)`, dead rows cleared. A newborn or immigrant starts with role 0 and dwell 0
(`on_birth = "rest"`); with `roles.inherit_role` a bud takes its parent's committed role (the value in the
step's survivors, i.e. including a switch made in the very step it is born), dwell still 0.
`ramp_q8 = min(256, dwell·256 // ramp_steps)` (integer): the ramp is the cost of specialising, a switching row is
useless as a specialist for `ramp_steps` steps (default 64), which also makes the benefit convex in time. The
effects read the START-of-step `role` and `role_dwell` (a step input: no ordering hazard); a switch shows from
the next step. `ActFlag.ROLE_SWITCHED` (512) marks the rows that switched; `ROLE_SWITCHES`, `N_FORAGERS`,
`N_GUARDS` are live counters; `Acts.ext.bonds` gains `shield` (`round(256·guard)`, int16).

### 40.9 The effects (all multipliers on flows the ledger books)

`roles.effects(s, act, partner, cfg)` returns the three per-row quantities; each is a static branch on its key,
so an effect key at 0 traces nothing. `partner` is the post-S9 partner.

1. **Harvest cap** (S10). `hm = H + (H·q8(forage_gain)·ramp·F >> 16) + (H·q8(synergy)·ramp·F·has_guard >> 16) -
   (H·q8(guard_harvest_pen)·ramp·G >> 16)` with `H = energy.harvest_max`, `F`/`G` the role indicators and
   `has_guard` = some valid partner is a guard with ramp at least 128: a forager harvests more, more again
   beside a guard (`synergy`), a guard less. `en.harvest(..., harvest_cap=hm)` uses `hm` in `want` and the
   final clip (None traces today's graph). `energy.harvest_max·(1 + forage_gain + synergy) < 65 536` is
   validated (`proportional_take` needs a demand below 2^16). Field removal is still booked by `taken`:
   `FLOW_HARVEST`; a larger cap wins a larger share of a contested cell, which pays only where food is contested.
2. **Own defence** (S11). `defend_mult = 1 - forage_defend_pen·ramp/256` for a forager, 1 otherwise;
   `roles.combat_act` passes `act._replace(defend=act.defend·defend_mult)` to `combat` only (the cost paid and
   the observer channel keep the raw output).
3. **Guard shield** (S11). A guard's potential is `gp_i = ramp_i/256 · act.defend_i` (it pays `defend_cost` for it)
   and 0 while the row attacks this step; the victim's protection fraction is `guard_shield · max(gp_t, max over
   its valid partners of gp)`, so a guard shields itself and each bonded partner, never a third party. It is
   passed as `combat(guard=)`: the second environmental factor of the §43.6 protection product (with the arms
   factor and structures' `shelter`, floored by `combat.protect_floor`, liftable by `pierce`), acting on the
   integer demand BEFORE `proportional_take`, so grant, gain, spill, residue and the drain rule are untouched
   and `FLOW_STOLEN = FLOW_ATTACK_GAIN + FLOW_SPILL` closes. `guard_shield <= 0.9` keeps the demand positive.
   `SHIELDED_BY_GUARD` counts the attacks whose victim has a guard fraction above 0.
4. Sharing feeds the specialist: with mode 1 or 2 the richer end pays the poorer across the bond (40.2).

**E16 (guarding one's own attacker; a bonded predator).** Combat is simultaneous and the guard fractions are
computed from the START-of-S11 actions, so the order is defined: a row that attacks this step (`attack` and a
target) contributes no guard potential. With `combat.attack_bonded` a guard that steals from its bonded partner
therefore gets the full demand (its own shield never covers its target); a third guard bonded to the victim does
reduce it (`test_e16_*`: demand `attack_max` without the third guard, `floor(attack_max·(1 - guard_shield))`
with it). Attacking and guarding are thus exclusive within a step, which costs an attacking guard its own cover.

**Calibration (R-2).** The payoff matrix, measured on the engine's own flows (`test_r2_*`: a cell of supply `S`
shared with `outsiders` generalist rivals through `en.harvest(harvest_cap=)`, one attack per member through
`en.combat(guard=)` scaled by the attack rate, `defend_cost` per member), at `forage_gain 0.75`,
`forage_defend_pen 0.5`, `guard_harvest_pen 0.5`, `guard_shield 0.5`, `synergy 0.25`, `ramp_steps 64` (q per step
per group):

| case | GG | FF | DD | FD | FG | GD | lone G / F / D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S 1500, 2 rivals, attack 0.25 | 208 | -336 | 110 | **354** | -48 | 310 | 130 / 55 / 55 |
| S 900, 4 rivals, attack 0.10 | 58 | -122 | 38 | **130** | -24 | 104 | 59 / 3 / 29 |
| S 900, 4 rivals, no predation | 258 | **378** | 138 | 305 | 326 | 204 | 159 / 253 / 79 |

Under moderate predation the forager+guard pair beats two generalists (by 70 % and 124 %) and a generalist beside
a guard, and no lone specialist beats a lone generalist; with no predation foragers win and the guard is a waste
(the negative control of owner decision O4). The margin over GD is thin (14 % and 25 %); `synergy` widens it
(tested). All values are starting values; none ships on in any base preset (the overlay `bonds` leaves the
effect keys at 0 in this PR; the calibrated set is for the runs). The upkeep per specialised member of the
spec's probe (`UP`) is not built: no new energy path.

### 40.10 Config, layout, compile cache

`[roles]` adds `forage_gain`, `forage_defend_pen`, `guard_harvest_pen`, `guard_shield`, `synergy` (0.0),
`ramp_steps` (64), `threshold` (0.5), `switch_cost` (0), `inherit_role` (false); all inert while
`roles.enabled` is false and in `POST_V01_KEYS` (frozen defaults pinned in `tests/test_ext_guards.py`).
Validation: gains and `synergy >= 0`, `forage_defend_pen`, `guard_harvest_pen` in `[0, 1)`, `guard_shield` in
`[0, 0.9]`, `ramp_steps` in `[1, 32767]`, `threshold` in `(0, 1)`, `switch_cost` in `[0, 2^15)`. The layout is
B1's (the whole block was allocated there). E4: `test_bonds_compile.py` compiles `roles.effects`, `decode_role`,
the switch due and `ramp_q8` for configurations differing only in one key, in one process, and each equals its
eager result and differs from the others. The bench mirror (`bench._StagedStep`) takes the same helpers and
equals `step()` (`test_staged_pipeline_*`, roles on).

### 40.11 Tests (B2)

`test_roles.py`: R-1 (the corners and the dead zone, a switch commits, resets the dwell and costs, the dwell
saturates, the dead zone keeps a role, an insolvent row cannot switch, the newborn role and `inherit_role`),
R-3 (the ramp and the integer harvest cap including synergy, effects absent at default, the capped harvest and
its ledger, a guard shields itself and its partner and not a third party, the `FLOW_STOLEN` identity with guard

* **Gates.** `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean; the fast suite on the CPU plugin passes but for
  `test_lifecycle_compiles_and_matches_eager`, which also fails on the base in that environment (it passes on
